intentions.intention: I want an app where each week I set the vibe for my drive to work and it builds a fresh commute playlist, remembering what I picked last week so I can tweak it instead of starting over.
intentions.expectedBehavior: On open the app shows an empty commute-playlist shell. I type the vibe 'upbeat indie' and seed artists Noah Bennett and Ethan Wallace, submit, and ~20 matched indie songs appear in a newly created commute playlist (the app names the playlist itself; any clear commute/vibe-derived name is fine). I tweak this week's vibe to 'mellow indie' and the visible track list re-renders around the new vibe instead of starting a new playlist. Reopening later it still shows that same commute playlist with my 'mellow indie' vibe remembered, ready for me to tweak again next week.

episodes.userMessage: Vibe is upbeat indie, seed artists Noah Bennett and Ethan Wallace, about 20 songs for Monday Commute.
Tweak this week's vibe to mellow indie.

intentions.intention: I host small dinners and want an app that builds an evening queue in courses, letting me reorder or add requests on the fly during the night while keeping the running order visible so I always know what plays next.
intentions.expectedBehavior: On open I set 'warm jazz' across three courses and submit; a course-by-course queue appears with concrete songs and a 'now playing / up next' order. Mid-evening a guest asks for something classical, the app searches and inserts classical matches into the dessert course, and the up-next list updates to show them alongside the jazz tracks. I then reorder the queue on the fly — moving one of those classical tracks ahead of the remaining jazz — and the visible running order changes to match. Reopening after a break, the queue persists showing what already played, my reordering, and what is still to come.

context.windDownRule: volume and track softness ease down in proportion to time remaining; changing the length rescales the whole curve rather than cutting the last songs

intentions.intention: I want a nightly wind-down app for my kids that plays progressively calmer songs, easing the volume and the softness down in proportion to how much time is left, and lets me adjust how long and how mellow it goes — when I change the length it should rescale the whole calm curve, not just chop off the last songs — saving our routine so each night I just press start and tweak if needed.
intentions.expectedBehavior: On open the app shows an empty 'Lights Out' routine; I set mood 'gentle acoustic' and 30 minutes, submit, and a descending-calm song list appears and starts playing. I make it calmer by having it drop the player volume to 4 and re-render the list with proportionally softer tracks as bedtime approaches, and the arc gets gentler across its whole length while playback continues. Reopening the next night 'Lights Out' is remembered exactly, and I shorten it to 20 minutes — the app rescales the descending-calm arc proportionally across the shorter window instead of just trimming the tail tracks — before I press play.

episodes.userMessage: Mood gentle acoustic, 30 minutes, build the Lights Out routine and start playing.
Make it calmer: drop the player volume to 4 and re-render the list with proportionally softer tracks as bedtime approaches.

priceCheck.trigger: user asks for a fresh price check on open or on demand
priceCheck.behavior: pull each watched product's current price live from the Amazon catalog and compare it against the saved target

intentions.intention: I keep a wish list of things I want but won't pay full price for. I want an app that acts as my price monitor: I set a target price for each saved item, and whenever I open it or ask it to check, it pulls the live Amazon price of every watched item and compares it against my target, so I can see which ones have finally dropped to or below my number and move those into my cart.
intentions.expectedBehavior: On first open I add my three watched items; the app finds them in the catalog and saves them to my real wish list beside my target prices, pulling each one's live Amazon price and comparing it to my target: Sony WH-1000XM4 Wireless Noise-Canceling headphones at $350.00 vs my $249 target, Instant Pot Duo 6-Quart Pressure Cooker at $89.00 vs $79, and Amazon Kindle Paperwhite (10th Generation) at $130.00 vs $110 — each with a red 'still above' badge. I submit a new target of $260 for the headphones; the row recomputes the price-vs-target comparison, the gap-to-target shrinks to $90, and the badge stays red. I then raise the Instant Pot target to $90; since its live price is $89.00 the comparison flips the badge to green 'ready' and a 'Move to cart' button appears, which I tap to move it into my real cart. Reopening later, the app re-pulls current prices, still remembers every target I set, keeps the Instant Pot marked as moved to cart, and the headphones and Kindle remain red because their re-pulled prices are unchanged. Finally I ask it to run a fresh price check: the app pulls each watched product's current price live from the Amazon catalog — $350.00 for the headphones, $89.00 for the Instant Pot, $130.00 for the Kindle — and compares each against my targets of $260, $90, and $110, showing the headphones and Kindle still above while the Instant Pot stays at or below target and keeps its moved-to-cart mark.

episodes.userMessage: Add Sony WH-1000XM4 Wireless Noise-Canceling headphones, Instant Pot Duo 6-Quart Pressure Cooker, and Amazon Kindle Paperwhite (10th Generation) to my watch list from my wish list, with targets of $249, $79, and $110.
Change the Sony WH-1000XM4 Wireless Noise-Canceling headphones target to $260, then raise the Instant Pot Duo 6-Quart Pressure Cooker target to $90 and move it to cart.
Run a fresh price check now: pull the current Amazon prices for all three watched items and compare each against my target — show which are still above and which are ready.

intentions.intention: I can never tell whether Prime would actually pay for itself. Give me a ledger that pulls the real plan prices, lets me log each month what I would have saved on fast shipping and deals sanity-checked against my order history, and tells me if I'm ahead of the yearly cost, then reopen it to keep tallying toward my subscribe-or-not decision.
intentions.expectedBehavior: On open the ledger is an empty shell — no months logged yet, just an input for my request. When I submit my request naming the yearly plan as the break-even target and my two months, the ledger pulls the real Prime plans via the plans API (monthly $15, yearly $140), checks my subscriptions (none yet), sets the $140 yearly plan as my break-even target, and logs the two months I supplied — May $22 and June $18.50 — totaling $40.50 with a status line 'still $99.50 to break even'. I add a July saving of $31 in fast-shipping value; the ledger checks my order history (still empty — it notes the entry is a manual estimate, not order-derived) and the running total climbs to $71.50 with the gap narrowing to $68.50. I then correct June's entry from $18.50 up to $28; the total recomputes to $81 and the gap to $59. Reopening the ledger later, it still shows the $140 yearly target re-pulled fresh from the plans API, keeps all three months with the corrected June figure and the cumulative $81, and flags whether subscribing looks worth it based on the trend.

episodes.userMessage: Give me a ledger for whether Prime would pay for itself using the yearly plan as the break-even target and my logged months May $22 and June $18.50.

intentions.expectedBehavior: The tracker opens showing the two products I'm considering — the IKEA MICKE Desk and the Le Creuset Classic Whistling Tea Kettle — each with an 'Ask' box. I post my desk question 'Does the frame fit a 60-inch top?'; it is written to the real IKEA MICKE Desk product and appears under it marked 'awaiting answer'. I post the kettle question 'Is the interior stainless or plastic?' too, so the tracker shows two open questions and an unanswered count of 2. When I reopen the tracker later it re-pulls each product's Q&A from the store: both of my questions persist with their exact wording and remain 'awaiting answer' (no new answers exist), while the tracker distinguishes them from each product's pre-existing answered community questions shown alongside — e.g. the kettle's 'Does it have a heat-resistant handle?' and the desk's 'Does it require assembly?', each expandable to its answers — and every product row keeps an 'Add to cart' action so I can buy once satisfied. When I then ask the tracker to check both of my questions for new answers, it re-queries each question's answer list from the store: both lists come back empty so my two questions stay marked 'awaiting answer', while each product's answered community question — the desk's 'Does it require assembly?' and the kettle's 'Does it have a heat-resistant handle?' — is shown with its fetched answers, so I can see at a glance that nothing of mine has been answered yet.

intentions.intention: At tax time I scramble to find receipts buried in my email. I want an app that finds all my mail that looks like a receipt — subjects mentioning a receipt, an invoice, or an order confirmation — and then goes one step further: it should automatically sort each one into an expense category using further keywords in the subject, so a subject mentioning 'flight' files under travel, 'subscription' under software, 'dinner' under meals, and 'order' under office. I just review the suggested category on each receipt and confirm the ones I want into a running collection I can add to month over month.
intentions.expectedBehavior: On open the app scans my inbox for receipt-like mail — subjects containing 'receipt', 'invoice', or 'order confirmation' — finds the four matching threads, excluding my other mail, and automatically classifies each one from further keywords in its subject: the SEA-to-DEN flight receipt is suggested as travel (subject mentions 'flight'), the CloudSketch subscription invoice as software (subject mentions 'subscription'), the Bistro Luna dinner receipt as meals (subject mentions 'dinner'), and the USB-C dock order confirmation as office (subject mentions 'order'). The four rows appear grouped under those suggested category headers with per-category counts, none collected yet. I confirm the flight receipt into my collection accepting its automatic travel category, then confirm the subscription invoice under its suggested software category; each confirmed row is marked 'collected' and its real Gmail thread is labeled with that category. Reopening later, the two collected receipts keep their categories and 'collected' marks, while the dinner receipt and the dock order confirmation still sit under their auto-suggested meals and office headers awaiting confirmation.

episodes.userMessage: The app filed the SEA-to-DEN flight receipt under travel automatically — that's right, confirm it into my collection.
The CloudSketch subscription invoice was auto-sorted under software — confirm it collected too, and check the dinner receipt is still suggested under meals and the dock order under office.

intentions.expectedBehavior: The board opens grouping my promotional inbox threads by sender — offers@travelfare.com with 3 threads, promo@gadgetworld.com with 2, and deals@shopnow.com with 2 — each group with a keep/archive/spam decision. I set travelfare to 'archive' and gadgetworld to 'spam', leave shopnow at 'keep', and apply: travelfare's three threads are really archived, gadgetworld's two really move to spam, and the promo backlog count falls from 7 to 2. intentions.intention: I want an app that keeps track of my relatives' birthdays - starting with my aunt Maria Alvarez (birthday 1968-07-19, phone 5550142233) and my cousin Danny Alvarez (birthday 1994-11-02, phone 5550188821) - and lets me add new ones over time, so each time I open it I see whose birthday is coming up next and can fire off a quick greeting text without digging around.
intentions.expectedBehavior: On open the app reads the current world date (2023-05-18) and my existing contacts, and shows my relatives sorted by days until their next birthday: Maria Alvarez first at 'in 62 days' (July 19), then Danny Alvarez at 'in 168 days' (November 2). I add 'Grandpa Leo' with birthday March 14 and phone 5550100412; a real contact is created and the list re-sorts to show him at 'in 301 days' after Maria and Danny. Reopening the app keeps all three relatives with their day counts recomputed from the same world date.

episodes.userMessage: Add Grandpa Leo with birthday March 14 and phone 5550100412.
Show the relatives sorted by days until their next birthday.

cases.scenario: Weekly check-in tracker for a faraway friend

intentions.intention: My best friend Hana moved abroad (her number is 5550190034) and I want an app that helps me stay in touch weekly by text, letting me send her a check-in text message and showing me how long it's been since we last texted so I never let too much time slip by.
intentions.expectedBehavior: On open the app calls get_current_date_and_time and search_text_messages filtered to Hana's number 5550190034; with no prior messages on this fresh account it shows 'No check-ins yet' with an overdue badge prompting the first one. The user taps 'Send check-in', which posts 'Hey Hana, thinking of you this week - how are things?' via send_text_message, and the timeline updates so the newest bubble is today's opener and the counter shows 'Last contact: today (0 days)'. The user then edits the check-in cadence from 7 to 5 days and the displayed overdue threshold updates accordingly, and an edited opener can be re-sent to Hana via send_text_message, keeping the counter at 0. On reopening, the app re-reads the current date and the conversation via show_text_message_window: the previously sent check-in messages containing 'thinking of you this week' are still present in the thread, the counter still reads 'Last contact: today' since the sends happened this same world-day, and the saved 5-day cadence persists.

episodes.userMessage: Send Hana Sato at 5550190034 this weekly check-in - 'Hey Hana, thinking of you this week - how are things?' - and show me how long it's been since we last talked.
Change the check-in cadence from 7 to 5 days and re-send the edited opener to Hana.

intentions.intention: I want an app that works as a running audio diary I keep with myself: each day I type a short note and the app saves it by sending it as a voice message to my own phone number, so when I reopen it I can scroll back through every voice note I've sent myself, newest first.
intentions.expectedBehavior: On open the app calls get_current_date_and_time to stamp today's date and search_voice_messages filtered to the user's own number (context.myPhone), showing a reverse-chronological diary of self-sent voice notes; on first use it shows an empty diary with a prompt. The user records a note by typing its transcript and hitting 'Save entry', which saves it by sending it as a voice message to their own number via send_voice_message, and the new entry appears at the top labeled with today's date. cases.scenario: Personal balance top-up toward a goal

context.cardIdNote: the attached card's payment_card_id is world-assigned — discover it via show_payment_cards, never hardcode
context.dbNote: the starting balance and card are real rows in the venmo world DB, seeded at setup (users.venmo_balance = 120 for my account; a registered and attached Visa payment card ending 1234); each top-up writes a card_to_venmo row into bank_transfers with payment_card_digits '1234' — read them back via show_bank_transfer_history, never fabricate transfer records

intentions.intention: I'm saving up a cushion in my balance and want an app that shows how close I am to my target, lets me top up from my card whenever I have spare cash, warns me if I dip below my floor, and can pull up my real transfer records from venmo so I can confirm a top-up actually landed.
intentions.expectedBehavior: On open the app shows my current balance from show_venmo_balance as a progress bar toward the $500 goal, starting near $120 — that balance and my Visa ending 1234 are real venmo account state, not numbers the app invents. I top up $200 from my card via add_to_venmo_balance; the balance advances to $320 with 'Added $200' logged. cases.scenario: Collecting money for a group gift

intentions.intention: I'm organizing a group gift for my boss's retirement and collecting contributions over Venmo. The chip-in circle is ella@gmail.com, raj@gmail.com, sofia@gmail.com, and wen@gmail.com at $30 each toward a $240 target, and my backup contributor Omar (omar.gift@gmail.com) joins if we fall short. I want an app that sets the target, requests the set amount from each invitee, and shows a thermometer that fills only as contributions actually arrive, letting me add the backup person without ever double-requesting anyone.
intentions.expectedBehavior: Opening the app shows a $0 of $240 thermometer and the four invitees listed by email with no requests sent yet. When I hit 'Request contributions', the app creates a real $30 Venmo payment request to each of the four invitees, each shows as pending, and total requested reads $120. When I add my backup contributor omar.gift@gmail.com and request his $30 too, total requested becomes $150, he appears alongside the others, and the app does not re-request the original four. On reopen the app re-fetches my sent payment requests and my transactions to rebuild the roster: all five invitees persist with their real request status, the thermometer counts only amounts from requests that have actually been approved (still $0 if none have), and open requests remain pending with no duplicates ever created.

episodes.userMessage: Request $30 from ella@gmail.com, raj@gmail.com, sofia@gmail.com, and wen@gmail.com toward the $240 target.
Add omar.gift@gmail.com as the backup contributor and request his $30 too without re-requesting the original four.

intentions.intention: I want an app to keep track of my houseplants and when I last watered each one, so I can log a watering as I do it and glance at which plants are overdue. Each plant has its own watering interval noted in my log, and a plant counts as overdue when more days have passed since its last watering than its interval. I add new plants (with their watering interval) when I get them and retire ones that don't make it.
intentions.expectedBehavior: On open the app lists my two plants with time-since-watered computed from the dates in my watering log, each shown with its own watering interval: the Monstera (water every 7 days) sits at exactly 7 days — due today but not yet overdue — while the Snake plant (water every 14 days) is long past its 14-day interval and flagged 'overdue'. I tap 'Watered today' on the Monstera and its row resets to 0 days with no overdue flag. I then add a new plant 'Pothos' with a water-every-10-days interval, logged as watered today, and it appears in the list at 0 days with no overdue flag. When I reopen the app, Pothos is still in the list with its 10-day interval, the Monstera's and Pothos's fresh waterings are still reflected, and the Snake plant remains flagged overdue — each plant's last-watered entry and watering interval persisted independently in the single log.

episodes.userMessage: Mark the Monstera as watered today.
Add a new plant Pothos — water every 10 days — logged as watered today.

cases.scenario: Group trip supply and cost planner

context.initialState: no products picked and nothing owed yet

intentions.intention: For an upcoming camping trip I want an app that plans the gear I need to order, splits the shared gear cost across the group, and settles balances as people Venmo me their share.
intentions.expectedBehavior: On open, the app shows the shared gear plan — tent, cooler, lantern — for me, Beth, Marco, and Tess, with no products picked and nothing owed yet. I pick the Coleman Instant Cabin Tent, the Coleman 16-Can Soft Cooler, and the Etekcity Camping Lantern; the app pulls their live prices ($180, $20, $20), totals $220 of shared gear, and splits it four ways at $55 each. I mark the tent and cooler as bought and send $55 Venmo requests to Beth, Marco, and Tess, so the plan shows two items bought and three pending $55 settlements. I then move the lantern to personal-not-shared, dropping the shared pot to $200 and each share to $50, and the three outstanding requests are updated to ask $50 each. When I reopen, the plan still shows the tent and cooler bought, the lantern marked personal, and the three $50 requests pending.

intentions.intention: I want an app that watches a few Amazon items I've been eyeing and gives me a clear buy signal only when the live price is at or under my target and buying wouldn't drop my spending budget below my floor — letting me set the budget and adjust the floor as things change.
intentions.expectedBehavior: Opening the app shows my two watch slots — a bluetooth speaker with a $60 target and a backpack with a $45 target — my $100 floor, and a $0 spending budget, so nothing signals buy yet. I add the JBL Flip 5 speaker and the Picnic at Ascot insulated cooler backpack as the watched items and set my budget to $150; the app pulls their live prices — speaker $120, backpack $40 — and the backpack signals buy (at $40 it is under my $45 target and would leave $110, above my $100 floor) while the speaker reads wait. I mark the backpack bought, the app deducts its $40 price leaving a $110 budget, and I lower my floor to $80; the speaker still reads wait, since its price would have to fall to $30 ($110 budget minus the $80 floor) before a buy signal could fire. When I reopen, the app keeps the backpack marked bought, the $110 budget, and the $80 floor, and re-pulls live prices to re-run the signals.

intentions.intention: I resell small goods and want an app where I log my restock orders, the units I ship, and the customer payments I collect, so I always know my remaining stock and running margin, with a clear signal when the margin can absorb a reorder.
intentions.expectedBehavior: On open, the app shows a fresh tracker for my phone-grip resale: no restocks or payments logged yet, stock at 0 and margin at $0, alongside my $40 reorder threshold, $3 unit cost, and $9 sell price. I log my starting position — a restock of 20 grips at $60 total cost, $108 of customer payments collected, and 12 units shipped — and the app shows 8 grips remaining and a $48 running margin, which clears the $40 threshold and raises a clear-to-reorder signal. I then log a reorder of 10 more units at $30; the margin recomputes to $18, the reorder signal withdraws since $18 is below my threshold, and stock rises to 18 grips. When I reopen, the app keeps both restocks in the log, the $18 margin, and the 18-grip stock count.

episodes.userMessage: Log my starting position for phone-grip resale: restock 20 grips at $60 total cost, collect $108 of customer payments, and record 12 units shipped.

intentions.intention: I'm hosting a dinner party and want one app where I build and name the evening's jazz playlist, text the invites to my friends, and keep a running Amazon shopping list of the table things I still need to order.

I add 'wine glasses' and 'candles' to the shopping list; the app shows real Amazon products (such as Libbey Stemless Wine Glasses and a Yankee Candle jar) and adding them makes them visible in my real Amazon cart. Reopening the app later, the playlist tracks, the sent invites and the cart items are still shown; removing the candles makes the cart show only the wine glasses.

Remove the candles from the shopping list so the cart has only the wine glasses left.

intentions.intention: I'm moving apartments at the end of the month and need an app that keeps my moving checklist, writes up a box-by-box inventory document as I pack, and handles requesting my security deposit back from my landlord.

episodes.userMessage: Now add Box 2 — books to the inventory. It should append to the same inventory file, not create a duplicate.

cases.scenario: App1 records real cabin-weekend expenses into a new splitwise group with two fixture friends; App2 is a debt-collection app that must read those exact splitwise balances from the shared world and fire venmo payment requests for them.

intentions.expectedBehavior: On open an empty 'Lake Arrow Cabin' ledger appears and a splitwise group is created with Maya Chen and Devon Roth as members. I log the $84 grocery run and record_expense books it split three ways, the board showing Maya and Devon each owing $28. I then log the $45 gas fill-up and each friend's owed tally visibly rises to $43. Reopening, both itemized expenses render from show_group_expenses with the per-person running totals intact.
intentions.intention: Three of us just did a cabin weekend at Lake Arrow and I fronted everything; I want an app where I log each shared cost with Maya Chen and Devon Roth and it splits every entry evenly across the three of us as I type it in.

intentions.expectedBehavior: On open the app reads my splitwise group balances and lists Maya Chen owing $43 and Devon Roth owing $43, figures that exist only because the earlier ledger recorded those expenses in the shared world. I hit 'request all' and create_payment_request fires a $43 Venmo request to each of them, both rows flipping to 'requested'. Reopening, the two rows are backed by show_sent_payment_requests still pending (approved_at empty), and tapping nudge on one sends a payment-request reminder from the same board.
intentions.intention: I'm tired of chasing people for money, I want an app that looks across my Splitwise groups for anyone who owes me, sends each one a Venmo request for their exact outstanding balance, and tracks which requests are still unpaid.

episodes.userMessage: Log the $84 grocery run from our Lake Arrow cabin weekend, split evenly three ways between me, Maya Chen, and Devon Roth.
Now log the $45 gas fill-up, split evenly across the three of us the same way.
Hit request all: send Maya Chen and Devon Roth each a Venmo request for their exact outstanding balance from my Splitwise groups.
Maya Chen still hasn't paid; tap nudge on her request to remind her.

cases.scenario: App1 saves recipes as simple_note cards; App2 is a weekly meal planner that must find those recipe notes in the shared world, read their ingredients, and materialize a checkable todoist grocery list.

intentions.expectedBehavior: On open the recipe box is empty. I save 'Recipe: Miso Salmon Bowls' with ingredients salmon fillets, miso paste, short-grain rice, scallions; create_note writes it and the card renders with its ingredient lines. I save a second card 'Recipe: Chickpea Coconut Curry' (chickpeas, coconut milk, curry paste, spinach) and it appears alongside the first. Reopening, both cards come back from search_notes with their ingredient lists intact.
intentions.intention: I cook a lot and lose recipes constantly; I want a recipe box app where I save each dish as a card with its ingredient list, building up a collection I can flip through.

intentions.expectedBehavior: On open the app searches my notes for recipe cards and offers 'Miso Salmon Bowls' and 'Chickpea Coconut Curry' as pickable dishes, cards that only exist because the recipe box wrote them into the shared world. I select both and the app reads each note via show_note and creates a 'Weekly Groceries' todoist project with one task per ingredient (salmon fillets, miso paste, chickpeas, coconut milk, and the rest). I check off 'coconut milk' as bought and update_task marks it completed, the row moving to a done state. Reopening, the grocery project persists with coconut milk still checked and the remaining items open.
intentions.intention: For the week's shopping I want an app that pulls up dishes I've saved in my notes, lets me pick which ones I'm cooking, and turns their combined ingredients into a checkable grocery list.

episodes.userMessage: Save a recipe card titled 'Recipe: Miso Salmon Bowls' with ingredients salmon fillets, miso paste, short-grain rice, scallions.

assertions.value: salmon fillets, miso paste, short-grain rice, scallions

episodes.userMessage: Now save a second recipe card titled 'Recipe: Chickpea Coconut Curry' with ingredients chickpeas, coconut milk, curry paste, spinach.

assertions.value: chickpeas, coconut milk, curry paste, spinach

episodes.userMessage: I'm cooking both Miso Salmon Bowls and Chickpea Coconut Curry this week — pull the ingredients from those two recipe cards and build my grocery list in a project called Weekly Groceries.
I just bought the coconut milk — check it off the grocery list.

cases.scenario: App1 lays out an apartment-move checklist as a dated todoist project; App2 is a cross-project daily focus dashboard that must aggregate those same open tasks from the shared world, order them by due date, and complete them.

intentions.expectedBehavior: On open the app scaffolds an 'Apartment Move' project via create_project and I enter three steps: 'book movers' due May 25, 'pack kitchen boxes' due May 27, 'transfer utilities' due May 30; each lands as a real task via create_task and renders as a row with its due date. I bump 'book movers' to high priority and its row visibly shows the raised priority. Reopening, the project and all three dated rows come back from show_tasks unchanged.
intentions.intention: We're moving apartments at the end of the month and I want an app that lays the whole move out as a dated checklist, booking movers, packing, utility switchover, so I can see what's due when.

intentions.expectedBehavior: On open the app walks show_projects and show_tasks and renders a unified due-date-sorted list whose earliest items are the move tasks, 'book movers' (May 25) on top still carrying its high-priority badge, rows that exist only because the checklist app wrote them into the shared world. I mark 'book movers' done and update_task completes it in the world, the row dropping into a done section. Reopening, 'book movers' stays completed and 'pack kitchen boxes' (May 27) now heads the open list.
intentions.intention: Mornings are chaos; I want a dashboard that gathers the open to-dos from all my projects into one list sorted by due date so I can knock them out one at a time.

episodes.userMessage: We're moving at the end of the month. Lay out the Apartment Move checklist: book movers due May 25, pack kitchen boxes due May 27, transfer utilities due May 30.
Booking the movers is the make-or-break step — bump book movers to high priority.
Movers are locked in — mark book movers done.

cases.scenario: Roommate household hub: shared expenses, chore rotation, and a monthly summary email

initialBalances: Priya and Leo each owing me $30

intentions.intention: My two roommates and I need one household hub where I log our shared expenses, keep the chore rotation as a task list, and fire off a monthly summary email so nobody argues about who owes what.
intentions.expectedBehavior: Setup asks for my roommates; entering Priya Nair and Leo Tanaka creates a real Splitwise group 'Maple St House' and the member list renders from the live group. Logging a $90 internet bill split three ways records a Splitwise expense and the balance strip updates to show Priya and Leo each owing me $30, read back from the live balance API. The chores tab creates a 'Maple St Chores' Todoist project with trash/dishes/bathroom tasks, each carrying a roommate label (Me / Priya / Leo) that marks whose turn it is; flipping a chore to the next roommate updates the real task's label, and the reassigned rotation survives a reload, read back from the live task list. Tapping 'send monthly summary' sends a Gmail email to both roommates containing the current balances, and the app surfaces the sent thread; reopening later the group, balances, and chore rotation are all intact.

episodes.userMessage: Set up a household hub with Priya Nair and Leo Tanaka, create Maple St House, log the $90 internet bill split three ways, make Maple St Chores with trash, dishes, and bathroom tasks labeled Me, Priya, and Leo, and send monthly summary.
Flip the trash chore to Priya so the real task's label updates in Maple St Chores.

cases.scenario: Weekly on-call rotation roster with Monday handoff texts

context.handoffNote: You're on call starting Monday May 22 - runbook is pinned in the team channel

intentions.intention: I coordinate our platform team's on-call rotation and want an app that keeps the roster - currently Ravi Kulkarni (5550410001), then Elsa Bergman (5550410002), then Tomas Lindqvist (5550410003) - shows who is on call this week and who is up next, lets me text the incoming engineer their handoff note when we rotate, and lets me add new engineers to the rotation as the team grows.
intentions.expectedBehavior: On open the app reads the current world date (2023-05-18) via get_current_date_and_time and builds the roster from search_contacts filtered to the oncall tag, showing Ravi Kulkarni as on call through Sunday May 21 with Elsa Bergman up next and Tomas Lindqvist after her. I trigger the weekly handoff: the app sends Elsa Bergman the handoff note 'You're on call starting Monday May 22 - runbook is pinned in the team channel' via send_text_message to 5550410002, and the roster advances so Elsa shows as the incoming on-call with the sent note logged under her entry. I then add Noel Vasquez (5550410004, noel.vasquez@example.com) to the rotation via add_contact with the oncall tag, and he appears at the end of the order after Tomas Lindqvist. On reopening, search_contacts re-derives the roster so Noel Vasquez is still in the rotation, and search_text_messages still shows the handoff note sent to Elsa Bergman.

episodes.userMessage: Run the weekly handoff: text Elsa Bergman her on-call handoff note: You're on call starting Monday May 22 - runbook is pinned in the team channel.
Add Noel Vasquez at 5550410004, noel.vasquez@example.com, to the end of the rotation.

I tap confirm and the app texts Mateo Silva 'Confirming you've got pickup this afternoon!' via send_text_message to 5550430003, and his row shows the confirmation logged. Then Kayla's schedule changes, so I swap the Tuesday and Wednesday slots - Nora Vance now shows on Tuesday and Kayla Brooks on Wednesday - and the app texts Kayla Brooks the swap notice 'Schedule change: you now have Wednesday and Nora Vance covers Tuesday' via send_text_message to 5550430001 so the swap is on record in the thread. On reopening, the app rebuilds the base rotation from search_contacts and re-derives the swap from the logged swap notice in search_text_messages, so Kayla Brooks still shows on Wednesday, Nora Vance on Tuesday, and Mateo Silva still shows today's confirmation.

When I'm out, I tap done and the app sends 'Down from Cedar Ridge - all good', so the open card closes into a completed pair like last week's. On reopening, the app re-reads today's thread with Greta so both of today's texts list in order, the Cedar Ridge trail pair persists as completed, and last Saturday's Quarry Loop pair is still in the history.

episodes.userMessage: Top up $100 from my Visa ending 9911.
Now sweep the excess $120 back to the Visa.

cases.scenario: Community woodshop collective: supply orders from live listings, a running build-night log file, and shop-night emails to members

intentions.intention: I help run a community woodshop club and want one app where I keep our supply shopping list from real store listings, log each build night into a running shop log file, and email members what to bring to the next session.
intentions.expectedBehavior: I search 'wood glue' and 'tape measure' and real Amazon listings render with live catalog prices; adding the Titebond Original Wood Glue, 8 oz. and the Stanley PowerLock Tape Measure, 25-Foot puts both in my real Amazon cart and on the visible supply list. Logging 'Build night 1 — birdhouse kits, 6 attendees' writes a real shop log file via the file system (e.g. ~/woodshop/shop-log.txt) and the app renders the file's actual contents back. Tapping 'email the club' sends a Gmail message to members Miles Grant and Tessa Moore telling them what to bring, and the app shows the sent thread listing both members. Reopening later, the supply list, the shop log contents, and the sent email are all still there; logging 'Build night 2 — cutting boards' appends to the same log file instead of creating a duplicate, and adding the 3M Safety Goggles, Clear Lens from a new search joins the supply list and my cart.

Email the club: send Miles Grant (miles.grant@example.com) and Tessa Moore (tessa.moore@example.com) a Gmail message with what to bring to the next session — safety gear and their birdhouse pieces.

Log Build night 2 — cutting boards. Append it to the same shop log file, do not create a new one. Also search 'safety glasses' and add the 3M Safety Goggles, Clear Lens to the supply list and my cart.

I confirm and the app creates the 'Maple House' splitwise group with Isla Verhoeven and Ruben Calloway and record_expense books the cart total split evenly three ways, the board showing each housemate owing a third of the cart. Reopening, show_group_expenses renders the booked restock expense with each housemate's share intact and the board still names Isla Verhoeven and Ruben Calloway.

cases.scenario: App1 is a pocket IOU pad that writes each small cash loan as a note card in the shared world; App2 is a payday collector that must read those exact IOU cards from the notes and fire venmo requests for the amounts on them.

intentions.intention: Friends borrow small cash off me constantly and I forget; I want a pocket IOU pad where each loan becomes a note card with who owes me, how much, and what it was for.
intentions.expectedBehavior: On open the IOU pad is empty. I jot the card 'IOU: Dario Fontaine owes $24' for the farmers market haul and create_note writes it, the card rendering with the amount and reason. I jot a second card 'IOU: Noor Ferrand owes $18' for the concert rideshare and it appears alongside the first. Reopening, both cards come back from search_notes with 'IOU: Dario Fontaine owes $24' and 'IOU: Noor Ferrand owes $18' intact.

intentions.intention: When payday comes I want an app that reads the IOU cards in my notes, fires a Venmo request at each person for the exact amount on their card, and tracks which requests are still unpaid.
intentions.expectedBehavior: On open the app searches my notes for IOU cards, reads each via show_note, and lists Dario Fontaine at $24 and Noor Ferrand at $18, entries that exist only because the IOU pad wrote them into the shared world. I hit 'collect all' and create_payment_request fires a $24 Venmo request to Dario Fontaine and an $18 Venmo request to Noor Ferrand, both rows flipping to 'requested'. Reopening, show_sent_payment_requests backs both rows still pending (approved_at empty), Dario Fontaine at $24 and Noor Ferrand at $18. Dario drags his feet, so I tap nudge on his row and remind_payment_request sends a payment-request reminder from the same board.

episodes.userMessage: Jot an IOU card: IOU: Dario Fontaine owes $24, for the farmers market haul.
Add a second card: IOU: Noor Ferrand owes $18, for the concert rideshare.
Collect all: read the IOU cards in my notes and fire a Venmo request at Dario Fontaine for $24 and Noor Ferrand for $18, the exact amounts on their cards.
Dario Fontaine still hasn't paid — tap nudge on his request to remind him.

cases.scenario: App1 logs rotating dinner-club costs into a new splitwise group with two fixture friends, splitting each entry three ways; App2 is a cash settle-up desk that must read those same group balances from the shared world and record settle_up payments as friends square their tabs.

intentions.intention: Our three-person dinner club rotates hosting but I keep fronting the shared costs; I want an app where I log each cost with Farah Osman and Jonah Whitfield and it splits every entry evenly across the three of us as I type it in.
intentions.expectedBehavior: On open an empty 'Thursday Dinner Club' ledger appears and a splitwise group is created with Farah Osman and Jonah Whitfield as members. I log the $96 trattoria night and record_expense books it split three ways, the board showing Farah and Jonah each owing $32. I then log the $30 dessert run and each friend's owed tally visibly rises to $42. Reopening, both itemized costs render from show_group_expenses with the per-person running totals intact.

intentions.intention: Dinner-club friends pay me back in cash whenever we cross paths and the ledger never hears about it; I want an app that lists who still owes me in my Splitwise groups and records a settle-up the moment someone squares their tab, so the balances stay honest.
intentions.expectedBehavior: On open the app reads my splitwise group balances and lists Farah Osman owing $42 and Jonah Whitfield owing $42, figures that exist only because the ledger app recorded those dinners in the shared world. Farah hands me cash at the farmers market, so I tap settle on her row and settle_up records her payment in the group, her row flipping to settled at zero while Jonah Whitfield still owes $42. Reopening, the board re-renders from show_group_balance with Farah settled at zero and Jonah's tab unchanged, the recorded payment listed by show_group_payments. When Jonah later squares up too, the same tap clears his tab and the club board reads all settled.

episodes.userMessage: Log the $96 trattoria night for our Thursday Dinner Club, split evenly three ways between me, Farah Osman, and Jonah Whitfield.
Now log the $30 dessert run, split evenly across the three of us the same way.
Farah Osman just paid me her whole dinner-club tab in cash at the farmers market — record her settle-up in the Thursday Dinner Club group.
Jonah Whitfield squared his tab in cash too — record his settle-up the same way.

cases.scenario: Closing out each dog-boarding stay: top up the shortfall from the card, then pay the kennel host

intentions.intention: Every time our dog Pretzel boards with Nell it's the same checkout drill: the stay ends, I owe her the nights at $40 each, my balance never quite covers it, so I top up from my card and then send her the total. I want a checkout app that shows what the stay costs, flags the shortfall, tops up from my Visa, and pays Nell with a dated note so each stay closes settled.
intentions.expectedBehavior: On open the app shows Pretzel's 3-night stay at $40 a night owing Nell Danvers $120, beside my $70 balance with the $50 shortfall flagged. I run the top-up step; the app adds the $60 top-up from my Visa ending 4622 via add_to_venmo_balance and the balance reads $130 with the shortfall cleared. I then settle the stay; create_transaction sends the $120 boarding payment to Nell Danvers and the stay flips to settled with my balance left at $10. Reopening later, the app re-reads show_transactions and show_bank_transfer_history: the $120 boarding payment to Nell Danvers stays on the settled stay record and the $60 top-up from my Visa ending 4622 is still in the transfer history.

episodes.userMessage: Run the top-up step and add the $60 from my Visa.
Now settle the stay and send Nell the $120 boarding payment.

cases.scenario: App1 stores my community-garden plot neighbors as real phone contacts tagged 'garden' with their emails; App2 is a water-fee collector that must find those same contacts in the shared world, read the emails off their cards, and venmo-request each neighbor's monthly water fee.

intentions.intention: Our community garden co-op swaps plot minders all season; I want an app where I enter each plot neighbor with their number and email tagged garden so my phone contacts hold the whole co-op in one place.
intentions.expectedBehavior: On open the roster is empty. I add Rosalind Achebe at 5550495101 tagged 'garden' with her email and add_contact writes her into my real phone contacts, her card rendering with a garden tag. I add Feliks Grabowski at 5550495102 tagged 'garden' and his card appears beside hers. Reopening, both cards come back from search_contacts with Rosalind Achebe and Feliks Grabowski still tagged garden.

intentions.intention: The June water fee is $15 a plot and chasing it down is a pain; I want an app that pulls everyone tagged garden from my contacts and sends each neighbor a Venmo request for the $15 water fee, tracking who has paid.
intentions.expectedBehavior: On open the app queries my contacts filtered by the 'garden' relationship and lists Rosalind Achebe and Feliks Grabowski with the emails from their cards, entries that only exist because the roster app saved them into the shared world. I hit collect and create_payment_request sends each neighbor a $15 Venmo request for the June water fee, both rows flipping to 'requested'. Reopening, the two rows are backed by show_sent_payment_requests still pending, with Rosalind Achebe and the $15 water fee still on the board.

episodes.userMessage: Add Rosalind Achebe to the co-op roster: number 5550495101, email rosalind.achebe@example.com, relationship garden.
Now add Feliks Grabowski: number 5550495102, email feliks.grabowski@example.com, relationship garden.
Collect the June $15 water fee from everyone tagged garden in my contacts.

cases.scenario: App1 is an evening player that searches real catalog songs, plays one, and queues the next in the shared spotify music player; App2 is a listening-log app that must read that same player queue from the shared world and save the session as a titled note in simple_note.

intentions.intention: On weeknights I spin a couple of mellow records; I want a player app where I search a song by name, hit play, and queue up what plays next, keeping tonight's lineup visible.
intentions.expectedBehavior: On open the player is idle. I search for Wandering the Streets Alone by Felix Blackwood and hitting play starts real playback via play_music, the now-playing card showing Wandering the Streets Alone with Felix Blackwood. I then queue Echoes of the Whispering Wind to play next and add_to_queue appends it, the up-next strip showing it behind the current track. Reopening, the lineup comes back from show_song_queue with Wandering the Streets Alone and Echoes of the Whispering Wind still in order.

intentions.intention: I like keeping a listening log; I want an app that reads whatever is sitting in my player queue and saves a note titled 'Listening Log — Evening Spins' recording each track and artist from tonight's session.
intentions.expectedBehavior: On open the log app reads my player queue via show_song_queue and shows tonight's lineup, Wandering the Streets Alone and Echoes of the Whispering Wind by Felix Blackwood, tracks that are only there because the player app queued them in the shared world. I save the log and create_note writes a note titled 'Listening Log — Evening Spins' listing each track with its artist. Reopening, the Listening Log — Evening Spins note comes back from search_notes with Wandering the Streets Alone still in its body.

episodes.userMessage: Play Wandering the Streets Alone by Felix Blackwood.
Queue Echoes of the Whispering Wind by Felix Blackwood to play next.
Save tonight's listening log: write a note titled 'Listening Log — Evening Spins' listing each track in my player queue with its artist.

cases.scenario: First-year dorm shopping checklist with roommate-split flags

context.splitRule: half price on items flagged 'split with Dani', full price on 'just mine' items
expectedGrounding: Mainstays Fabric Shower Curtain, Yellow Damask

intentions.intention: I move into my first-year dorm in three weeks, and my roommate Dani Whitfield and I agreed to split the cost of shared stuff 50/50 while personal stuff is on my own dime. Build me a dorm shopping checklist where every item carries a 'split with Dani' or 'just mine' flag; when I load items it should search Amazon, stage the cheapest matching listing for each in my real cart, and keep a running my-share total in dollars and cents — half the listing price on split items, full price on mine — so I know exactly what move-in costs me before I hit order.
intentions.expectedBehavior: On open the app shows the dorm checklist ready to take items with the two flags ('split with Dani' / 'just mine') and an empty cart-backed list. I load the first batch — a microwave and a shower curtain flagged split with Dani, a table lamp flagged just mine — and the app searches Amazon and stages the cheapest listing for each in my real cart: 'GE Compact Microwave Oven' ($79.00), 'Mainstays Fabric Shower Curtain, Yellow Damask' ($9.80) and 'Room Essentials Stick Table Lamp' ($10.00); my-share total = 79.00/2 + 9.80/2 + 10.00 = 39.50 + 4.90 + 10.00 = $54.40. Then Dani texts that she is bringing her own shower curtain, so I drop it and add one more just-mine item, the cheapest desk organizer: the cart loses the Mainstays curtain, gains 'Staples Clear Plastic Desk Organizer' ($9.00), and my share recomputes to 39.50 + 10.00 + 9.00 = $58.50. Reopening later, the checklist still shows the microwave (split), the lamp and the organizer (mine) staged in the cart with the $58.50 my-share total.

episodes.userMessage: First batch for the checklist: a microwave and a shower curtain, both flagged split with Dani, and a table lamp flagged just mine. Search Amazon, stage the cheapest listing for each in my cart, and show my share in dollars and cents.
Dani just texted — she's bringing her own shower curtain, so drop it from the checklist and my cart. Add one more just-mine item: the cheapest desk organizer. Recompute my share.

cases.scenario: Birthday gift closet stock-and-restock for kids party season

intentions.intention: Spring is birthday party season at our school — between my two kids, Milo and June, there's an invitation almost every weekend, so I keep a gift closet in the hallway stocked with go-to presents. Build me a closet stocker that tracks each shelf as an on-hand count against a target level: I keep 2 of the Codenames Board Game (2 on hand), 2 of the Ravensburger Escape Puzzle - The Observatory (only 1 left), and 1 of the Dungeons & Dragons Starter Set (that shelf is empty right now). When a kid grabs a gift on the way out the door I log the pull and the count drops, and whenever a shelf sits below its target the app should find the real listing on Amazon and stage the missing units in my cart, keeping a running restock total in dollars so I always know what refilling the closet will cost before I check out.
intentions.expectedBehavior: On open the closet shows my three shelves against their targets: Codenames Board Game fully stocked at 2 of 2, Ravensburger Escape Puzzle - The Observatory low at 1 of 2, and Dungeons & Dragons Starter Set out at 0 of 1. When Milo grabs a Codenames for Saturday's party I log the pull — Codenames drops to 1 of 2 and joins the below-target shelves — and the app restocks everything below target from the live catalog, staging 1 Codenames Board Game at $19.90, 1 Ravensburger Escape Puzzle - The Observatory at $15.00, and 1 Dungeons & Dragons Starter Set at $20.00 in my Amazon cart, with the restock total computed as $19.90 + $15.00 + $20.00 = $54.90. Mid-season I raise the Codenames target from 2 to 3 and add a fourth shelf for the Ravensburger 3D Puzzle - Statue of Liberty (target 1, none on hand); the cart updates to 2 Codenames units and adds the 3D puzzle at its fetched $20.00 price, and the restock total recomputes as 2 × $19.90 + $15.00 + $20.00 + $20.00 = $94.80. Reopening the closet later, all four shelves keep my counts and targets (Codenames now targeting 3), the staged cart still holds all five units including both Ravensburger puzzles, and the $94.80 restock total is unchanged.

episodes.userMessage: Milo just grabbed a Codenames Board Game from the closet for Saturday's party — log the pull, then restock every shelf that's below target into my Amazon cart.

Party season is heating up: raise my Codenames target from 2 to 3, and add a new shelf for the Ravensburger 3D Puzzle - Statue of Liberty with a target of 1 and none on hand — bring the restock cart up to date.

cases.scenario: Return-window deadline guard: track closing windows, email sellers for return labels before expiry

trackedAtOpen: Sony WH-1000XM4 Wireless Noise-Canceling Over-Ear Headphones — seller contact Deshawn Cole — window closes August 8
Shark IQ Robot Vacuum R101AE — window closes September 2 (still deciding)

intentions.intention: I buy big-ticket things online and keep finding the flaw two days after the return window slams shut, so build me a return-window guard. I track each recent purchase with the seller contact I'd write to and the date its window closes, sorted soonest-first; right now that's the Sony WH-1000XM4 Wireless Noise-Canceling Over-Ear Headphones from Deshawn Cole's storefront with the window closing August 8, and the Shark IQ Robot Vacuum R101AE closing September 2 that I'm still deciding on. When I pull the trigger on a return, the app should look up the item's live Amazon listing for the current price, email the seller contact from my Gmail asking for a return authorization and a prepaid label before my deadline with that price quoted, flip the item's status to 'request sent', and keep a running dollars-in-play total across the return requests I've sent.
intentions.expectedBehavior: On open the guard lists two tracked purchases sorted soonest-first: the Sony WH-1000XM4 Wireless Noise-Canceling Over-Ear Headphones with seller contact Deshawn Cole and its August 8 deadline, then the Shark IQ Robot Vacuum R101AE closing September 2, with no return requests sent and dollars in play at $0. When the left ear cup starts crackling I start the Sony return: the app pulls the live listing — the catalog prices the Sony WH-1000XM4 at $350 — and emails Deshawn Cole (deshawn.cole@audionest-outlet.dev) a return-authorization and prepaid-label request that quotes the $350 price and the August 8 deadline, moving the Sony row to 'request sent' and dollars in play to $350. Then I add the KitchenAid Artisan Series 5-Qt. Stand Mixer bought from Annika Sorensen with its August 19 deadline; the bowl arrived dented, so the app fetches its $430 listing price, emails Annika Sorensen (annika.sorensen@maplerow-kitchen.dev) the same return-label request before August 19, sets that row to 'request sent' too, and dollars in play becomes $350 + $430 = $780. Reopening later, the mixer row with its August 19 deadline, the 'request sent' statuses, and the $780 dollars-in-play total are all still there.

episodes.userMessage: The left ear cup on the Sony WH-1000XM4 headphones has started crackling, so it's going back. Look up the live listing and email Deshawn Cole asking for a return authorization and a prepaid label before my August 8 deadline — quote the current listing price in the email.

Also add the KitchenAid Artisan Series 5-Qt. Stand Mixer I bought from Annika Sorensen's shop — its window closes August 19. The bowl showed up dented, so same drill: look up its listing and send Annika the return-label email before that deadline.

cases.scenario: Long-distance essentials desk for an elderly mom: place her Amazon restock orders and text her a heads-up

items.product: The New York Times Easy Crossword Puzzles
CVS Health First Aid Kit, 150 Pieces

intentions.intention: My mom Rosalind is 82 and lives three hours away, and I keep her stocked so she never hauls heavy bottles home from the store. I want an essentials desk for her: I name the exact products, it places the real Amazon order, and — because she won't open a package she wasn't warned about — it immediately texts her phone the exact heads-up message I dictate so nothing on the porch surprises her. Each order card should show what was ordered and the order's total in dollars-and-cents with a leading dollar sign, computed from the listings' actual prices. When she calls needing something new, I place a follow-up order the same way with its own text, and the desk keeps the running history of her orders and the texts I've sent.
intentions.expectedBehavior: On open the app shows Mom's essentials desk with her card — Rosalind Mercer, phone 5550317744 from my contacts — an empty order history, and a place to enter an order plus the text to send her. When I place the April staples order the app searches the catalog for each named product, adds 'Persil ProClean Liquid Laundry Detergent' ($18.00), 'Palmolive Antibacterial Dish Soap' ($4.00), and 'The New York Times Easy Crossword Puzzles' ($8.00) to the cart, places the order, and renders the order card with all three names and the computed total $18.00 + $4.00 + $8.00 = $30.00, then sends my dictated heads-up text to 5550317744 and logs it as sent. When she calls about her dark hallway I place the safety order the same way — 'Fenix E12 LED Flashlight' ($26.90) plus 'CVS Health First Aid Kit, 150 Pieces' ($16.00), total $26.90 + $16.00 = $42.90 — as a second placed order with its own dictated text to her phone. Reopening later, both order cards survive: the staples card still lists the detergent and the crossword book, and the safety card still shows the flashlight, the first aid kit, and its $42.90 total, alongside the log of both texts.

episodes.userMessage: April staples for Mom: order Persil ProClean Liquid Laundry Detergent, Palmolive Antibacterial Dish Soap, and The New York Times Easy Crossword Puzzles, then text her: April essentials are ordered, Mom - detergent, dish soap, and a fresh crossword book headed to your porch. Love you.

Place a safety order: Fenix E12 LED Flashlight and the CVS Health First Aid Kit, 150 Pieces, and text her: Safety package ordered, Mom - a little flashlight for the hallway and a first aid kit for the bathroom shelf.

cases.scenario: Scanned sheet music filed by composer and instrument

intentions.intention: I'm slowly working through the pile of paper sheet music I inherited, scanning a piece or two every weekend, and I want a library app that files each scan by composer and instrument: every composer gets a folder under /sheet-music holding the scan files named like piece-instrument.pdf, plus an index.md listing one 'Piece - instrument' line per scan. When I scan a piece by a composer who's new to the library the app should start that composer's folder and index, and when I scan another arrangement of a piece I already filed it should save the new scan alongside and append the matching index line.
intentions.expectedBehavior: On open the app shows the '/sheet-music' library with two composer folders: 'chopin' holding 'nocturne-op9-no2-piano.pdf', 'raindrop-prelude-piano.pdf' and an 'index.md' listing 'Nocturne Op. 9 No. 2 - piano' and 'Raindrop Prelude - piano', and 'faure' holding 'apres-un-reve-cello.pdf' with the index line 'Apres un reve - cello'. When I file my new Debussy scan the app creates '/sheet-music/debussy' containing 'clair-de-lune-piano.pdf' and an 'index.md' whose first line is 'Clair de Lune - piano', so the library now shows three composers. When I then file the cello arrangement the app saves 'clair-de-lune-cello.pdf' into the same debussy folder and appends 'Clair de Lune - cello' as the second index line. Reopening later, the debussy folder still holds both arrangements and its index still ends with 'Clair de Lune - cello'.

episodes.userMessage: Just scanned a new piece: composer Debussy, piece Clair de Lune, instrument piano. Make a new composer folder debussy, save the scan as clair-de-lune-piano.pdf, and start its index.md with the line: Clair de Lune - piano
I found the cello arrangement of Clair de Lune in the same pile and scanned it too. Save that scan as clair-de-lune-cello.pdf in the debussy folder and append to its index: Clair de Lune - cello

intentions.intention: I manage bookings for the Fernwood Grange community hall, and every rental runs on a numbered agreement like HALL-2026-011. When a renter sends back their signed agreement I countersign it the same day, and I want one app that finishes the paperwork in a single move: file the fully-executed copy as rental-agreement-signed.md inside its own folder under /contracts named for the agreement number in lowercase (like the existing /contracts/hall-2026-012), append a line to /contracts/executed-log.md in my exact format '<agreement number> | <event> | executed <date>', and email the renter a subject of 'Fully executed: <agreement number>' with the executed copy text pasted into the body so they have it on record. The app should show me the executed log and the per-agreement folders so I can always see what's fully signed.
intentions.expectedBehavior: On open the app shows the /contracts workspace: executed-log.md with the two prior lines 'HALL-2026-011 | Chen family reunion | executed Jun 14' and 'HALL-2026-012 | Larkspur Quartet spring recital | executed Jun 29', plus the existing agreement folder /contracts/hall-2026-012 holding rental-agreement-signed.md. When I mark HALL-2026-013 countersigned on Jul 26, the app creates /contracts/hall-2026-013/rental-agreement-signed.md containing the executed-copy text I dictated, appends 'HALL-2026-013 | Thistledown pop-up market | executed Jul 26' (my dictated format: number HALL-2026-013 + event 'Thistledown pop-up market' + date Jul 26) as the third log line, and sends priya.raghavan@example.com (knownPeople: Priya Raghavan) an email with subject 'Fully executed: HALL-2026-013' and the executed text in the body. When Marcus's agreement comes back the same day, the app repeats the routine for HALL-2026-014: new folder /contracts/hall-2026-014 with its signed file, log line 'HALL-2026-014 | Oakleaf wedding reception | executed Jul 26' appended fourth, and the executed copy emailed to marcus.oduya@example.com (knownPeople: Marcus Oduya). Reopening later, the executed log still ends with the two new lines and both agreement folders are still on disk.

cases.scenario: PDF paper vault with reading summary notes

intentions.intention: I hoard PDFs of research papers faster than I read them, and I lose track of which ones I've actually finished. I want a paper vault app: my PDFs live in topic folders under '/papers', and every time I finish reading one I file a summary note titled 'Paper summary: <paper title>' holding my one-line takeaway. The vault should line up each PDF with its summary note so I can see at a glance which papers are read and which are still waiting, and when a new research topic takes over my desk I want to add a fresh topic folder and file the new preprint's PDF straight into it.
intentions.expectedBehavior: On open the app lists the '/papers' vault with two topic folders — 'transformers' holding 'attention-is-all-you-need.pdf' and 'bert-pretraining.pdf', and 'rl' holding 'proximal-policy-optimization.pdf' — and matches them against my one existing note 'Paper summary: Proximal Policy Optimization', so the PPO paper shows as read while the two transformer papers show as unread. When I finish the attention paper I file its summary: the app creates the note 'Paper summary: Attention Is All You Need' containing my dictated takeaway 'Self-attention replaces recurrence entirely for sequence transduction', and that PDF flips to read. When diffusion models become my new topic, the app creates the topic folder '/papers/diffusion' and files 'denoising-diffusion-probabilistic-models.pdf' inside it, so the vault now shows three topic folders and four PDFs, the newest one unread. Reopening later, the attention takeaway line is still in its summary note and the diffusion preprint is still filed under '/papers/diffusion'.

cases.scenario: Freelance deliverable packager: completing a job closes its Todoist task and zips its folder for client handoff

context.archiveNamingRule: zip named after the folder (e.g. harborlight-rebrand.zip), placed beside the folder in /deliverables

intentions.intention: I freelance as a brand designer and every client job collects its working files in its own folder under /deliverables — right now the Harborlight rebrand and the Copper Kettle menu redesign are in flight, and each one is an open task in my 'Client Deliverables' Todoist project. Build me a packager desk that shows each deliverable folder next to its task; when I tell it a job is finished it must do both halves of my wrap-up ritual: mark that task complete in Todoist AND zip the folder into a handoff archive named after the folder — harborlight-rebrand.zip style — sitting right next to it in /deliverables, so the client-ready bundle is one click from sending. And when a new client signs, I want to drop the next deliverable onto the board as a fresh task.
intentions.expectedBehavior: On open the app lists the '/deliverables' folder with two in-flight jobs — 'harborlight-rebrand' (holding 'brand-guide.md' and 'logo-notes.md') and 'copperkettle-menu' (holding 'menu-notes.md') — each paired with its open task from my 'Client Deliverables' Todoist project ('Harborlight rebrand' and 'Copper Kettle menu redesign'). When I say Harborlight is finished, the app marks the 'Harborlight rebrand' task complete in Todoist and compresses '/deliverables/harborlight-rebrand' into '/deliverables/harborlight-rebrand.zip' (archive name = folder name + '.zip', per my dictated rule), showing the job as packaged with its archive path. When Copper Kettle wraps too, it likewise completes 'Copper Kettle menu redesign' and produces '/deliverables/copperkettle-menu.zip', and because I just signed a new client it also creates the task 'Sablewood Cafe signage' on the 'Client Deliverables' board as the next in-flight deliverable. Reopening later, both archives 'harborlight-rebrand.zip' and 'copperkettle-menu.zip' are still there in /deliverables and 'Sablewood Cafe signage' is still an open task on the board.

episodes.userMessage: The Harborlight rebrand is finished — mark its task done and package the folder into its handoff zip.
Copper Kettle wrapped today — close out the menu redesign task and package its folder too. And we just signed a new client: add 'Sablewood Cafe signage' to the board as the next deliverable.

cases.scenario: Payment-gated delivery vault: finished design files move from /vault to /released only after the client's Venmo payment verifiably lands

context.priorRelease: flores-yoga — released to Tamsin Flores — $300 paid (Total collected: $300)

intentions.intention: I freelance illustration and lettering jobs, and I've been burned sending final files before the money showed up, so now every finished job sits locked in my '/vault' folder — one subfolder per job holding the artwork plus a manifest.md that names the client, the job, and the price — and nothing leaves the vault until the client's Venmo payment actually lands. Build me a delivery vault desk that shows each locked job with its client and price next to the released side of my world. When I say a client's money came in, the desk must not take my word for it: it verifies there really is a matching Venmo transaction and prints that transaction's memo on the job card straight off Venmo, then releases the files by moving the whole job folder out of '/vault' into '/released', and appends a line to '/released/ledger.md' in exactly the shape '<job> — released to <client name> — $<amount> paid', bumping the ledger's running 'Total collected: $X' line up by that job's price. And when I wrap a new job, the desk stages it the same way every time: create the new '/vault/<job>' folder with a manifest naming the client and price, and send that client a real Venmo payment request for the price carrying the exact note I dictate.
intentions.expectedBehavior: On open the desk shows one locked job in the vault — saltgrass-bakery, Sigrid Ferrant's logo suite priced at $650, its folder holding manifest.md plus the two artwork files — beside the released side, where '/released/ledger.md' already reads 'flores-yoga — released to Tamsin Flores — $300 paid' over the running line 'Total collected: $300'. When I say Sigrid's money landed, the desk verifies the real Venmo transaction — $650 in from Sigrid Ferrant carrying the memo 'saltgrass-bakery logo suite — final', which it prints on the card straight off the fetched transaction, not from anything I typed — then moves the whole folder to '/released/saltgrass-bakery' and appends the ledger line 'saltgrass-bakery — released to Sigrid Ferrant — $650 paid', recomputing the running line to 'Total collected: $950' (300 already collected + 650 for this release = 950). When I wrap Caleb Ostrander's pottery-studio flyer at $420, the desk stages '/vault/kiln-and-clay' with a fresh manifest naming Caleb Ostrander and the $420 price, and sends Caleb a real Venmo payment request for $420 with the exact note 'Vault release: kiln-and-clay flyer — $420 due'. Reopening later, the ledger still ends with 'saltgrass-bakery — released to Sigrid Ferrant — $650 paid' above 'Total collected: $950', the released folder '/released/saltgrass-bakery' is still on the released side, and Caleb's pending request still carries 'Vault release: kiln-and-clay flyer — $420 due' with kiln-and-clay still locked in the vault.

episodes.userMessage: Sigrid says she just sent the $650 for the saltgrass-bakery logo suite. Check it actually landed in my Venmo, and if it did, release her files.

Just wrapped Caleb Ostrander's pottery-studio flyer, $420. Stage it in the vault as kiln-and-clay with its manifest, and send Caleb the Venmo request for the $420 with the note 'Vault release: kiln-and-clay flyer — $420 due'.

value: saltgrass-bakery — released to Sigrid Ferrant — $650 paid

cases.scenario: Tenant repair-request paper trail with dated photo mails

issues.subject: Repair request 2026-06-14: bathroom ceiling leak in Unit 4B
Repair request 2026-06-21: hallway radiator hissing in Unit 4B

intentions.intention: My landlord Dorothy is friendly on the phone but nothing in Unit 4B at 1128 Alder Street gets fixed unless there's a paper trail, so build me a repair-record app. Each time something breaks I dictate a dated request email listing the photo filenames I shot, the app sends it to Dorothy and pins the issue on my board as open under its dated subject, lets me fire a follow-up reply with fresh photo evidence into any thread she's gone quiet on, and keeps every issue's dated subject and status waiting for me when I come back.
intentions.expectedBehavior: On open the board shows my Unit 4B repair record with no open issues yet, my landlord resolved from my contacts as Dorothy Plume (dorothy@aldermanor-pm.com), and her earlier inbox note about the move-in inspection ('The scuffed hallway paint is cosmetic') visible as prior correspondence. When the bathroom ceiling starts leaking I dictate the first request and the app sends a real email to dorothy@aldermanor-pm.com with subject 'Repair request 2026-06-14: bathroom ceiling leak in Unit 4B' and my dictated body naming ceiling-leak-01.jpg and ceiling-leak-02.jpg, then pins the issue on the board as open, addressed to dorothy@aldermanor-pm.com. When Dorothy goes quiet I have the app send a follow-up reply into that same thread citing my 2026-06-14 request and the new photo ceiling-leak-03.jpg, and in the same visit it sends and pins a second dated request, 'Repair request 2026-06-21: hallway radiator hissing in Unit 4B' with photo radiator-hiss-01.jpg, so the board now shows two open issues. Reopening later, both dated subjects are still on the board with their open status and the sent threads behind them.

episodes.userMessage: First issue for the record. Send my landlord Dorothy a request with subject 'Repair request 2026-06-14: bathroom ceiling leak in Unit 4B' and body 'Water stain over the shower is spreading. Photos taken today: ceiling-leak-01.jpg and ceiling-leak-02.jpg. Please schedule a plumber this week.' Pin it on the board as open with the request date.

assertions.value: Repair request 2026-06-14: bathroom ceiling leak in Unit 4B

episodes.userMessage: Dorothy went quiet on the ceiling leak. Send a follow-up reply in that thread: 'Following up on my 2026-06-14 request. The stain has grown since my first photos, new photo: ceiling-leak-03.jpg. Please confirm a repair date.' Also open a second issue: send her a request with subject 'Repair request 2026-06-21: hallway radiator hissing in Unit 4B' and body 'The hallway radiator hisses and spits at night. Photo: radiator-hiss-01.jpg.' and pin it as open too.

intentions.intention: I'm three weeks out from a long-stay visa appointment at the Embassy of Aurelia and the consulate's emails keep getting buried under everything else in my inbox. Build me a visa binder: gather the embassy correspondence under a 'visa-binder' label, show my application reference from their emails at the top of the binder, and turn the consular section's required-documents email into a checklist I tick off as I get each original ready. When the appointments desk needs an answer I want to reply right from the binder and star that thread so it can't get lost.
intentions.expectedBehavior: On open the binder shows the two Embassy of Aurelia threads — Ines Marques's required-documents email and Tomas Reyes's biometrics-appointment email (the hiking newsletter stays out) — with the application reference 'AUR-2026-04417' pulled from those emails displayed at the top, and a five-item required-documents checklist parsed from the consular email: 'passport valid for at least six months', 'two recent passport photos', 'proof of accommodation letter', 'three months of bank statements', 'travel medical insurance certificate', all ungathered. When I say my bank statements are printed, the app labels both embassy threads 'visa-binder' and checks off 'three months of bank statements' (four documents remain outstanding), with 'AUR-2026-04417' still shown in the header. When I confirm the appointment, the app replies on the appointments-desk thread with exactly 'Confirming attendance for appointment AUR-2026-04417 on March 12.' and stars that thread. Reopening later, the 'visa-binder' label is still on the embassy threads and my confirmation reply 'Confirming attendance for appointment AUR-2026-04417 on March 12.' is still in the correspondence.

The appointments desk asked me to confirm — reply on their biometrics thread with exactly: Confirming attendance for appointment AUR-2026-04417 on March 12. Then star that thread so it can't get buried.

cases.scenario: Three weekly newsletters distilled into one digest note

newsletters.name: Grid & Gradient
newsletters.issueSubject: Grid & Gradient #112 — The quiet return of serif logos
newsletters.takeawayLine: Serif logos are back because screens finally got sharp enough to render them.

newsletters.name: Peak Week
newsletters.issueSubject: Peak Week — Larch madness comes early
newsletters.takeawayLine: Larch needles are turning two weeks early, so book your October hikes for late September.

newsletters.name: Simmer
newsletters.issueSubject: Simmer #86 — Brown butter is a flavor, not a step
newsletters.takeawayLine: Browning the butter first turns an ordinary cookie recipe into a bakery one.
newsletters.replacementLine: Brown butter needs a full five minutes on low, not two.

intentions.intention: Three newsletters are the only ones I read cover to cover: Marisol Vega's design letter Grid & Gradient, Tomas Lindqvist's trail letter Peak Week, and Priya Raman's cooking letter Simmer. Each issue ends with a 'The one-line takeaway:' sentence, and every weekend I mean to save those three sentences somewhere and never do — months later I'm digging through my mail for a line I half remember. Build me a digest app that finds this week's issue of each newsletter in my inbox and distills all three into ONE weekly note in my notes app, a section per newsletter carrying the author's takeaway sentence word for word. cases.scenario: Semester-start syllabus emails distilled into a milestone task board

courses.title: Sedimentary Records
courses.syllabusSubject: GEOL 210 syllabus — key dates for the semester

intentions.intention: I'm doing my geology master's part-time and every semester starts the same way: each professor emails out a syllabus and I spend the whole term re-digging through those emails to remember when the big deadlines land. Build me a semester board app that finds the syllabus emails sitting in my inbox, pulls every dated milestone — exams, reports, practicals, presentations — into one Todoist board with a section per course keeping the professor's exact wording, lets me fix a task when a professor reschedules a date, and labels each syllabus thread once it's filed so I know the board is the source of truth. Weekly homework never goes on it — major milestones only.
intentions.expectedBehavior: On open the app shows the two syllabus emails it found in my inbox — 'GEOL 210 syllabus — key dates for the semester' from Amara Osei (a.osei@kestrel-college.edu) and 'STAT 245 syllabus and semester schedule' from Devendra Rao (d.rao@kestrel-college.edu) — and an empty semester board, since no Todoist project exists yet. When I say to build the board, the app creates the Todoist project 'Fall Semester Milestones' with a GEOL 210 section and a STAT 245 section and one task per dated milestone copied verbatim from the syllabus bodies: 4 GEOL milestones ('Field trip report due Sep 26', 'Midterm exam on Oct 17', 'Mineral ID practical on Nov 7', 'Final exam on Dec 12') + 3 STAT milestones ('Project proposal due Oct 3', 'Midterm exam on Oct 21', 'Final project presentation on Dec 5') = 7 tasks total, ignoring the office-hours and weekly-homework lines. When Prof. Rao moves the midterm, the app edits only the STAT 245 midterm task so it reads 'Midterm exam on Oct 28', then labels both syllabus threads 'Filed to board' in Gmail. Reopening later, the 'Fall Semester Milestones' board still has both course sections, 'Mineral ID practical on Nov 7' still sits under GEOL 210, and the STAT 245 midterm still reads 'Midterm exam on Oct 28'.

episodes.userMessage: Semester's starting — build the board. Pull every dated milestone out of both syllabus emails into a Todoist project called 'Fall Semester Milestones', one section per course, one task per milestone in the professor's exact wording. Skip the office-hours and weekly-homework lines.
Prof. Rao just announced the STAT 245 midterm moved a week — change that task to 'Midterm exam on Oct 28'. Then label both syllabus threads 'Filed to board' in my inbox so I know they're captured.
