cases.scenario: Closing FB Marketplace sales over email and Venmo

intentions.intention: I'm clearing the garage out through FB Marketplace, and the chat haggling is the easy part — actually closing is where my deals die. Once a buyer and I settle on a price I move them to email to pin down pickup, and I collect through Venmo. Build me a sale-closer desk: it shows each listing with its agreed price and buyer — Priya Raman is taking the walnut dresser for $120, Marcus Webb the hybrid commuter bike for $85, and the $60 stand mixer has no takers yet — next to the buyers' Marketplace inquiry emails sitting in my inbox. Closing a sale should fire both halves at once: a pickup-confirmation email to the buyer with the time and my address, plus a Venmo request for the agreed amount. As payments land I mark the sale paid, and the desk keeps a running collected total versus what's still to come.
intentions.expectedBehavior: On open the desk lists three Marketplace sales — the walnut dresser at $120 agreed with Priya Raman, the hybrid commuter bike at $85 agreed with Marcus Webb, and the stand mixer unclaimed at $60 — alongside the buyers' seeded inquiry emails (Priya's 'I can do $120 for the walnut dresser' note about bringing her brother's truck, Marcus's '$85 as discussed in chat'), with $0 collected so far. When I close the dresser sale, the app emails Priya Raman (priya.raman@plumtree-mail.com) that pickup is Saturday 10am at 44 Alder Court and creates a $120 Venmo payment request to her, flipping the dresser card to awaiting payment. On the next turn I mark the dresser paid since her $120 landed, and close the bike sale the same way: Marcus Webb (marcus.webb@rowanpost.net) gets a confirmation email saying pickup is Sunday 4pm at 44 Alder Court plus an $85 Venmo request. The desk now reads $120 collected, and — adding the pending $85 bike request to the unsold $60 mixer ($85 + $60 = $145) — $145 still to come. Reopening later, the dresser still shows paid with its Saturday 10am at 44 Alder Court pickup, the bike still shows Sunday 4pm at 44 Alder Court awaiting Marcus's $85, and the running figures still read $120 collected with $145 still to come.

episodes.userMessage: Close the dresser sale: email Priya Raman that pickup is Saturday 10am at 44 Alder Court, and send her the Venmo request for the $120 we agreed.

Priya's $120 just landed, so mark the dresser paid. Then close the bike sale: email Marcus Webb that pickup is Sunday 4pm at 44 Alder Court and send him the $85 request — that should leave $145 still to come counting the unsold mixer.

cases.scenario: Baby shower hosting hub: invite texts to the guest list, a per-head Venmo stroller fund with a running tally, and vendor email confirmations off the inbox

context.guestOfHonor: my sister Wren, due in October
context.shower: Saturday, August 8 at 2 PM at my place
context.giftFund: $45 per guest toward the stroller, Venmo note 'Wren's stroller fund'

vendors.name: Camille Fortin
vendors.quote: $68 two-tier Lemon-Raspberry cake, flavor needs confirming by reply

vendors.name: Petra Novak
vendors.quote: $95 sage-and-cream balloon arch, delivery hour needs confirming by reply

intentions.intention: My sister Wren is due in October and I'm throwing her baby shower at my place on Saturday, August 8 at 2 PM. The whole production is smeared across three apps: the guest list lives over text, the group gift is a Venmo collection, and both vendors only do email — Camille Fortin at Meadowlark Bakes sent me a cake quote that needs a flavor confirmation, and Petra Novak at Juniper Party Co won't route her van until I reply with a delivery hour for the balloon arch. I want one hosting hub that texts the invites to my guests, fires the $45-a-head Venmo requests for the stroller fund and keeps a running tally of what I've asked for, and lets me answer the vendor emails right from the board so I can see both vendors confirmed with their quoted prices and what the party is costing me.
intentions.expectedBehavior: On open the hub shows the shower framed around Wren's big day — Saturday, August 8 at 2 PM — with the guest list, the stroller fund, and the two vendor threads from my inbox waiting for answers. Submitting sends real invite texts to Nadia Osei, Marcus Webb and Iris Kwan with the Saturday August 8 at 2 PM details and fires each of them a real $45 Venmo payment request with the note 'Wren's stroller fund'; the fund tally shows $135 total requested ($45 × 3 = $135). Answering the vendors replies on Camille Fortin's Meadowlark Bakes thread confirming the Lemon-Raspberry cake at her quoted $68 and on Petra Novak's Juniper Party Co thread locking the balloon-arch delivery at 11 AM at her quoted $95; the vendor board shows both confirmed with their prices and a combined vendor bill of $163 ($68 + $95 = $163). Reopening the app later, the guests, the 'Wren's stroller fund' tally at $135 and the $163 vendor bill are still shown. When my cousin Talia Reyes wants in late, the hub texts her the invite, sends her the same $45 request with the 'Wren's stroller fund' note, and the fund tally moves to $180 ($135 + $45 = $180).

episodes.userMessage: Text the invites to my three guests — Nadia Osei, Marcus Webb and Iris Kwan — for the shower Saturday August 8 at 2 PM at my place, and send each of them a $45 Venmo request with the note 'Wren's stroller fund'. Show me the fund tally of everything requested so far.

Now answer the vendors: reply on Camille Fortin's Meadowlark Bakes thread confirming the Lemon-Raspberry cake at her quoted price, and reply on Petra Novak's thread telling her to deliver the balloon arch at 11 AM. Mark both vendors confirmed on the board with their quoted prices and show me the combined vendor bill.

My cousin Talia Reyes just heard about the shower and wants in on the gift. Text her the invite for Saturday August 8 at 2 PM, send her the $45 Venmo request with the same 'Wren's stroller fund' note, and update the fund tally.

cases.scenario: Co-owned cabin communal pantry: living inventory board from a shared note, real-listing restock cart, and an even three-way cost split among the co-owners

expectedGrounding: Pyrex Ultimate 10-Piece Glass Food Storage Set

intentions.intention: Three of us co-own a little cabin at Birch Hollow and share one communal pantry; whoever drives up last scribbles what's running low into my 'Cabin Pantry Inventory' note. I want one app that turns that note into a pantry board, builds the restock order from real Amazon listings for whatever's marked low or out, and logs each restock into a Splitwise group so the cost always splits evenly three ways between me, Priya Raman, and Wes Calloway.
intentions.expectedBehavior: The app loads my saved 'Cabin Pantry Inventory' note and renders every pantry line with its status — AA batteries OUT, dish soap LOW, food storage containers LOW with cracked lids, plus the fine items like firewood and coffee filters. When I ask it to restock the out/low items it searches real Amazon listings and carts the Duracell CopperTop AA Batteries (24-Pack) at $16.00, the Palmolive Antibacterial Dish Soap at $4.00, and the Pyrex Ultimate 10-Piece Glass Food Storage Set at $40.00, each shown with its live catalog price beside its pantry line. When I say to log the cost, it creates the real Splitwise group 'Birch Hollow Pantry' with Priya Raman and Wes Calloway and records the cart total as one 'Pantry restock run' expense split evenly three ways — the total is 16.00 + 4.00 + 40.00 = 60.00 and each co-owner's share is 60.00 / 3 = 20.00 — and the who-owes-what strip renders from the live group balance. Reopening the app rebuilds the board, the carted items, and the group balances from the real accounts. Finally I have it append my dictated restock log line to the pantry note and mark the three restocked lines on the board, so the note history matches the ledger.

episodes.userMessage: Pull up my 'Cabin Pantry Inventory' note and turn it into the pantry board, every item with its status. Then restock what's marked out or low: search Amazon and add the 24-pack of Duracell CopperTop AA batteries, the Palmolive Antibacterial Dish Soap, and the 10-piece Pyrex glass food storage set to my cart, with each listing's live price next to its pantry line.

assertions.value: Pyrex Ultimate 10-Piece Glass Food Storage Set

episodes.userMessage: Now log the cost: create a Splitwise group called 'Birch Hollow Pantry' with Priya Raman (priya.raman@example.com) and Wes Calloway (wes.calloway@example.com), record the cart total as one 'Pantry restock run' expense split evenly three ways among us, and show who owes what from the live group balance.

assertions.value: Pyrex Ultimate 10-Piece Glass Food Storage Set

episodes.userMessage: We placed the order — append this line to my Cabin Pantry Inventory note: 'Restocked July: AA batteries, dish soap, storage set — 60.00 split three ways, 20.00 each' and mark those three pantry lines as Restocked on the board.

cases.scenario: Backyard chicken coop build HQ: build-phase task checklist, real Amazon hardware cart, and a running flock note about the hens

expectedGrounding: Makita 18V LXT Lithium-Ion Cordless Drill Kit
Behr Premium Plus Satin Enamel Exterior Paint (5-Gallon)

intentions.intention: I'm finally building the backyard chicken coop for my three hens — Clementine, Butterscotch, and Pepper — and I want one build headquarters app: my coop build phases kept as a real task checklist, the hardware I still need staged in my real Amazon cart, and a running flock note where I jot down how the girls are doing.
intentions.expectedBehavior: I dictate the build checklist and the app creates a real Todoist project named 'Chicken Coop Build' containing my four phase tasks — 'Frame the floor and walls', 'Build three nesting boxes', 'Hang the coop door', and 'Paint and weatherproof' — and shows them as live tasks. For the hardware run I ask for the Makita 18V drill kit, Titebond III wood glue, and the Behr 5-gallon exterior paint; the app fetches the real listings 'Makita 18V LXT Lithium-Ion Cordless Drill Kit' ($150.00), 'Titebond III Ultimate Wood Glue, 16-Ounces #1414' ($8.00), and 'Behr Premium Plus Satin Enamel Exterior Paint (5-Gallon)' ($108.00), puts all three in my real Amazon cart, and shows the hardware subtotal $266.00 (150 + 8 + 108 = 266). It also starts my 'Flock Notes' note in Simple Note listing Clementine, Butterscotch, and Pepper. Reopening the app later, the project with its tasks, the three cart items, and the flock note are still shown. When my neighbor lends me a full bottle of wood glue, removing the Titebond from the cart leaves the drill kit and the paint (150 + 108 = 258.00 left in hardware), and logging 'Pepper laid her first egg' appends that line to the flock note.

Now the hardware run: add the Makita 18V drill kit, Titebond III wood glue, and the Behr 5-gallon exterior paint to my Amazon cart. And start my flock note — title it 'Flock Notes' and list my three hens: Clementine, Butterscotch, and Pepper.

Behr Premium Plus Satin Enamel Exterior Paint

cases.scenario: Climbing gym crew hub: fronted day passes split on Splitwise, a shared beta notebook, and a Venmo gear fund for the crew crash pad

intentions.intention: Twice a week I climb at Basalt Bloc with Tessa and Rowan, and I'm always the one who fronts the day passes at the front desk. I want one app that runs the crew: it keeps every cost I front in a Splitwise group split evenly three ways with a running total of what the crew owes me, holds our shared beta notebook where I jot the sequence that finally unlocked a problem, and runs our gear fund over Venmo — requesting each climber's chip-in when we pool for shared gear and nudging whoever sits on their request.
intentions.expectedBehavior: On open the crew hub is ready for me, Tessa Marchetti and Rowan Doyle, nothing logged yet. I log the $57 day-pass buy I fronted: the app creates the 'Basalt Bloc Crew' Splitwise group with Tessa Marchetti and Rowan Doyle, records the $57 expense split evenly — 57 / 3 = $19 a head — and shows the crew owing me 2 × 19 = $38; it also creates the 'Basalt Beta Notes' note opening with my dictated line 'Orange V4 on the arete: high right heel, dead-point to the crimp rail'. When we pool $126 for the crew crash pad, the app sends Tessa and Rowan each a real Venmo payment request for their third — 126 / 3 = $42 — with the note 'Basalt gear fund — crash pad', shows both requests pending, and appends my new line 'Black V5 in the cave: knee-bar rest before the lip, commit to the sloper' to the notebook. Reopening later, the group ledger, the notebook with both beta lines, and the two pending $42 gear-fund requests all rebuild from live state. After the next session Rowan hands me $19 in cash, so I record his $19 payment in the group; I also log the $33 chalk-bucket refill and finger tape I fronted, split evenly three ways — 33 / 3 = $11 a head — so the ledger shows Tessa at 19 + 11 = $30, Rowan at 0 + 11 = $11, and the crew total owed to me at 30 + 11 = $41; Tessa still hasn't paid the gear fund, so the app fires a Venmo reminder on her pending $42 request.

episodes.userMessage: I fronted today's day passes at Basalt Bloc — $57 for the three of us. Set up the 'Basalt Bloc Crew' Splitwise group with Tessa Marchetti and Rowan Doyle, record the $57 day-pass expense split evenly three ways so I can see what the crew owes me, and start our 'Basalt Beta Notes' note with today's beta: 'Orange V4 on the arete: high right heel, dead-point to the crimp rail'.

We're pooling $126 for the crew crash pad. Send Tessa and Rowan each a Venmo payment request for their third of it with the note 'Basalt gear fund — crash pad', and add tonight's beta to the notebook: 'Black V5 in the cave: knee-bar rest before the lip, commit to the sloper'.

Rowan squared up his day pass with $19 cash — record his $19 payment in the Basalt Bloc Crew group. I also fronted $33 for the chalk-bucket refill and finger tape — record that split evenly three ways and show me the updated crew total. Tessa hasn't touched her gear-fund request, so send her a Venmo reminder on it.

intentions.intention: My daughter is a senior this year and I've somehow become her college application coach. Her school counselor Dana Whitfield emails me the dates that actually matter, my daughter only responds to text messages, and the essay planning lives wherever I last scribbled it. I want one desk where I pull each school's deadline out of Dana's emails onto a deadline board, keep a living notes page for the personal statement, text my kid a nudge when a date is coming, and send Dana quick status emails so she knows we're on track.
intentions.expectedBehavior: The app reads counselor Dana Whitfield's two seeded emails in my inbox and puts the real dates on the deadline board: Maplewood College early action closes November 1, Harrington University regular decision closes January 5, and the personal statement draft is due to Dana by October 20. It also creates a real note titled 'Elise Personal Statement — Working Notes' seeded with that October 20 draft deadline and the essay angle from Dana's second email — the robotics team story about rebuilding the drivetrain. When I ask, it texts my daughter Elise Tran (5550118207) a nudge that includes the November 1 Maplewood date and the October 20 draft date, and sends Dana a fresh email with subject 'Elise deadline plan — on track'. Reopening the desk later still shows both schools' deadlines, the essay notes page, and the sent status update. When Elise finishes her draft, the app appends 'Draft v1 done — 648 words, sent for counselor review.' to the notes page and texts Elise that Harrington University is next along with its January 5 regular-decision date pulled from Dana's email.

Now text my daughter Elise Tran (5550118207) her first nudge — it should include the Maplewood College early-action date and the draft deadline from Dana's email. Then send Dana Whitfield a fresh email with subject 'Elise deadline plan — on track' telling her the board is up and the draft is on schedule.

Elise finished her personal statement tonight. Append this line to the essay notes page: 'Draft v1 done — 648 words, sent for counselor review.' Then text Elise that the draft is in and Harrington University is next — include its regular-decision date from Dana's email.

cases.scenario: Co-op preschool supply desk: ledger the four-family supply fund in Splitwise, file a typed receipt for every run, and email the parents the settle-up

intentions.intention: I do the supply runs for Little Sprouts, the four-family co-op preschool we run out of the church basement, and I front all the money. I want one supply desk where I keep a Splitwise group with the other three parents — Greta Lindqvist, Bea Solano, and Owen Marchetti — and log every run split evenly across the four families, type each paper receipt into a file in a receipts folder so the co-op has a paper trail, and at month end email the parents exactly what each family owes me.
intentions.expectedBehavior: Setup creates the real Splitwise group 'Little Sprouts Co-op' with Greta Lindqvist, Bea Solano and Owen Marchetti as members, and logging the art run records a $96 expense paid by me split evenly four ways — deterministic arithmetic $96 / 4 = $24, so the live balance shows each of the other three families owing me $24. Filing the paperwork creates the /coop_receipts directory and writes real files /coop_receipts/art_run_receipt.txt and /coop_receipts/snack_run_receipt.txt containing the item lines I dictate, while the $52 snack run is recorded in the same group split the same four ways ($52 / 4 = $13 a family). Reopening later, the group, both recorded runs and both receipt files are still on screen. At settle-up the app resolves the parents from my contacts and sends a real Gmail email to greta.lindqvist@example.com, bea.solano@example.com and owen.marchetti@example.com with subject 'Little Sprouts supply settle up' telling each family it owes me $37 — exact arithmetic $24 + $13 = $37 per family, and I cover my own share so only the other three owe — and the app surfaces the sent thread.

episodes.userMessage: Set up the fund first: create a Splitwise group called 'Little Sprouts Co-op' with the other three parents — Greta Lindqvist, Bea Solano, and Owen Marchetti. Then log yesterday's art supply run: I paid $96 for construction paper, washable paint, and glue sticks, split evenly across the four families — that's $24 a family.

Now the paper trail and today's run. Make a /coop_receipts folder and type up yesterday's receipt as /coop_receipts/art_run_receipt.txt — list construction paper, washable paint, and glue sticks, $96 total, paid by me. Then log today's snack run in the same group: $52 for crackers, apple juice, and fruit cups, split the same four ways — $13 a family — and file its receipt as /coop_receipts/snack_run_receipt.txt with those item lines and the $52 total.

Month's done, time to settle. Each family's share is $24 from the art run plus $13 from the snack run, so $37 a family, and I cover my own share — the other three each owe me $37. Email Greta, Bea, and Owen with the subject 'Little Sprouts supply settle up' and tell each family it owes me $37 for this month's supply runs.

intentions.intention: I run the media desk for our dance studio's Spring Showcase. The revise turn creates the Todoist project 'Spring Showcase Cues' with tasks 'Cue 4: blackout after Ballet 3 final chord' and 'Cue 7: crossfade into Hip-Hop Juniors entrance', plus a second playlist 'Hip-Hop Juniors Showcase' with 'Dancing in the Rain of Tears' and 'Ephemeral Beauty'. Reopening later still shows the filed v1 edit, both playlists with their tracks, and the cue tasks. intentions.intention: I walk dogs for a living and my three-dog weekday roster deserves better than the soggy sticky note in my jacket pocket. Churro the dachshund (Ingrid Yardley's) goes Monday, Wednesday and Friday at $18 a walk; Mochi the goldendoodle (Owen Ferris's) goes Tuesday and Thursday at $22; and Ziggy the border collie (Carmen Voss's) gets his big Monday outing at $25. Carmen settles up the same day after each walk; Ingrid and Owen get one invoice when the week wraps. Build me my dog-walking empire HQ: when I lay the week down it creates a real Todoist project with one task per walk plus a real behavior-log note per dog that I append observations to after walks, and as walks get done it checks off the tasks, appends my log entries, and fires the real Venmo payment requests — per-walk for Carmen, end-of-week invoices for the other two — keeping a requested-so-far tally so I always know what the week is worth.
intentions.expectedBehavior: On open the HQ shows my three-dog roster with each dog, owner, rate and walk days — Churro / Ingrid Yardley / $18 / Mon-Wed-Fri, Mochi / Owen Ferris / $22 / Tue-Thu, Ziggy / Carmen Voss / $25 / Mon — with $0 requested so far. Laying the week down creates the real Todoist project 'Empire Walk Board' with six tasks named '<Day> - Walk <Dog> (<Owner>)' — 'Mon - Walk Churro (Ingrid Yardley)', 'Mon - Walk Ziggy (Carmen Voss)', 'Tue - Walk Mochi (Owen Ferris)', 'Wed - Walk Churro (Ingrid Yardley)', 'Thu - Walk Mochi (Owen Ferris)', 'Fri - Walk Churro (Ingrid Yardley)' — and creates the three real Simple Note behavior logs 'Behavior Log - Churro', 'Behavior Log - Mochi', 'Behavior Log - Ziggy'. When Monday's walks are done, the HQ completes both Monday tasks, appends my dictated entries to Churro's log ('Mon: pulled hard the first block, settled the moment I switched him to the front-clip harness.') and Ziggy's log ('Mon: two clean off-leash recalls at Miller Pond - best session yet.'), and — because Carmen pays per walk — creates the real $25 payment request to Carmen Voss with note 'Dog walk - Ziggy - Monday', with the requested-so-far tally reading $25. cases.scenario: Estate sale prep desk: room-by-room photographed item lists filed under /estate-sale with computed subtotals, family claim texts to siblings, and a sale-prep task board

expectedGrounding: reply by Sunday or they get tagged

intentions.intention: We're clearing out my mom's house at 41 Maple Street for an estate sale and I'm the sibling on the ground. My routine is the same every visit: I photograph a room shelf by shelf, dictate the item list with my asking prices, and then lose the list somewhere in my camera roll. Build me an estate sale prep desk that files each room's dictated item list under /estate-sale/<room>/inventory.md exactly as I speak it, keeps a running banner totaling every priced line across all room lists formatted exactly 'Priced so far: $NNN', runs my sale-prep task board in Todoist, and can text my sister Nora and my brother Calvin whenever something needs a family claim before it gets tagged for sale. I already filed the dining room list on my first visit — it should be sitting there when I open the app.
intentions.expectedBehavior: On open the app shows my /estate-sale folder with the dining-room inventory I filed on my first visit ('walnut dining table with six chairs — $300' and 'china hutch — needs appraisal') and no task board yet, since no Todoist project exists. When I finish photographing the study and dictate its three items, the app creates /estate-sale/study, writes inventory.md with exactly my lines ('oak rolltop desk — $220', 'manual typewriter — $85', 'brass banker's lamp — $40') and ends the file with the computed line 'Study subtotal: $345' (220 + 85 + 40 = 345); it also creates the Todoist project 'Estate Sale — 41 Maple Street' with my three prep tasks, including 'Book the appraiser for the china cabinet'. When I find dad's coin albums, the app appends 'coin albums (2) — ask Calvin first' to the study list (no price, so no total changes), adds the board task 'Get coin albums appraised before pricing', texts Nora Whitfield and Calvin Whitfield my claim message verbatim, and refreshes the banner to 'Priced so far: $645' — the $300 dining table price is read from the dining-room file I seeded on my first visit (it appears in no message of mine) and added to the study subtotal (300 + 345 = 645). Reopening later, the board, the study list with the coin-album line, the subtotal and the sent claim texts are still shown. When Calvin claims the typewriter, the app removes that line from the study inventory, recomputes 'Study subtotal: $260' (220 + 40 = 260) and 'Priced so far: $560' (300 + 260 = 560), and texts Calvin my exact confirmation.

episodes.userMessage: Study's photographed. Create /estate-sale/study and file the list as inventory.md with exactly these lines: 'oak rolltop desk — $220', 'manual typewriter — $85', 'brass banker's lamp — $40', then end the file with a line formatted exactly 'Study subtotal: $NNN' where NNN is the sum of those three prices. Also set up my prep board: a Todoist project called 'Estate Sale — 41 Maple Street' with three tasks — 'Price every remaining room', 'Order sale-day price stickers', 'Book the appraiser for the china cabinet'.

assertions.value: Book the appraiser for the china cabinet

episodes.userMessage: Found dad's coin albums in the study closet. Append 'coin albums (2) — ask Calvin first' to the study inventory — no price yet, so it changes no totals — and add a board task 'Get coin albums appraised before pricing'. Then text both Nora Whitfield and Calvin Whitfield exactly this: 'Claim day: mom's china hutch and anything else you want is up for family claims — reply by Sunday or they get tagged.' And refresh my Priced so far banner across both room lists.

assertions.value: Get coin albums appraised before pricing
reply by Sunday or they get tagged

episodes.userMessage: Calvin texted back — the manual typewriter is his. Remove that line from the study inventory, recompute the study subtotal and the Priced so far banner, and text Calvin exactly: 'The typewriter is yours — I'll set it in the hall closet before tagging weekend.'

cases.scenario: Family history archive desk: Sunday interview notes with Grandma saved verbatim, relatives' emailed finds distilled into a facts note, and scanner-dump records renamed out of the flat /scans pile into /family-archive

intentions.intention: My grandmother Hazel Whitfield turns 90 in October and I'm racing to assemble the family history before the party. Right now it's three messes: my Sunday interview notes with her live in Simple Note, my aunt Doreen and cousin Silas keep emailing me finds I'm terrified of losing, and my scanner dumps every old record into one flat /scans pile with names like scan_0041.jpg. Build me a family history archive desk that shows my interview notes, the relatives' emails, and the /scans pile next to my /family-archive folders. After each visit I'll dictate the new interview as a titled note in exactly my words; I want the facts from the relatives' emails saved into a 'Confirmed record facts' note in their exact wording so nothing slips away; I'll tell it how to rename and file each scan; and when the records folder is ready I want to zip it up and reply to the relative right from the desk.
intentions.expectedBehavior: On open the desk shows my two existing interview notes ('Interview #1 — Hazel — Duluth childhood' and 'Interview #2 — Hazel — meeting Grandpa'), the relatives' emails it found in my inbox — 'Grandma's wedding details for the archive' from Doreen Abernathy and 'Found the ship manifest!' from Silas Whitfield (the Heritage Quarterly newsletter is not family material) — and the flat /scans pile of three scan files alongside a not-yet-created /family-archive area. When I dictate Sunday's session, the app creates the note 'Interview #3 — Hazel — the bakery years' with my sentence verbatim, and creates a 'Confirmed record facts' note whose lines are pulled from the email bodies in the relatives' exact wording: from Doreen's email the wedding on June 3, 1957 at St. Ambrose Church in Duluth and the maiden name Hazel Marie Calloway; from Silas's email that Elias Calloway arrived at Ellis Island on the SS Verbania in March 1921. When I file the scans, the app creates /family-archive/records and /family-archive/photos and does 3 moves (2 into records + 1 into photos = all 3 scans, leaving /scans empty): scan_0041.jpg becomes /family-archive/records/birth-certificate-hazel-calloway-1936.jpg, scan_0042.jpg becomes /family-archive/records/fremont-street-deed-1948.jpg, scan_0043.jpg becomes /family-archive/photos/bakery-storefront.jpg; it also appends my dictated line 'Confirmed for Silas: the Fremont Street bakery was hers.' to the Interview #3 note. Reopening later, the Interview #3 note, the SS Verbania line in the facts note, the appended confirmation, and the renamed birth-certificate file are all still there. Finally the app compresses /family-archive/records into a zip archive and replies on Silas's ship-manifest thread with my exact sentence, showing the sent reply addressed to Silas Whitfield.

episodes.userMessage: Just back from Sunday's visit. Save the new interview as a note titled 'Interview #3 — Hazel — the bakery years' with exactly this: 'Hazel ran the Calloway Bakery on Fremont Street from 1954 until the fire in 1961; she bought the building with her brother Walter using their father's savings.' Then make the 'Confirmed record facts' note: pull every family fact out of Doreen's and Silas's emails, one line per fact, in their exact wording.

Now file the scans. Create /family-archive/records and /family-archive/photos. Move /scans/scan_0041.jpg into /family-archive/records as birth-certificate-hazel-calloway-1936.jpg, move /scans/scan_0042.jpg into /family-archive/records as fremont-street-deed-1948.jpg, and move /scans/scan_0043.jpg into /family-archive/photos as bakery-storefront.jpg. Grandma also settled Silas's question today, so append this line to the 'Interview #3 — Hazel — the bakery years' note: 'Confirmed for Silas: the Fremont Street bakery was hers.'

assertions.value: Confirmed for Silas: the Fremont Street bakery was hers.

episodes.userMessage: The records folder is ready for Silas. Zip up /family-archive/records, then reply to his 'Found the ship manifest!' email with exactly this: 'Grandma confirmed the Fremont Street bakery was hers — the deed and her birth certificate are filed in the archive, zip coming your way.'

assertions.value: the deed and her birth certificate are filed in the archive

cases.scenario: Fantasy baseball commissioner desk: weekly dues ledger in Splitwise, winner-takes-all Venmo pot payout, and the ceremonial trash-talk text to last place

expectedGrounding: my bench outscored your entire starting lineup
context.potMath: 3 managers x $10 dues = $30 weekly pot; winner takes all; commish dues waived
context.settleMath: $30 owed - $10 Beau cash settle = $20 still outstanding

intentions.intention: I run our four-team fantasy baseball league, the Cellar Dwellers, and every Monday the commissioner grind is the same: chase the week's $10 dues from my three managers, pay the weekly high score the whole pot, and send last place his ceremonial trash-talk text. My commish salary is that my own dues are waived, so the pot is the other three's money and I front the payout. I want one app that keeps the dues ledger as a real Splitwise group, pays the winner straight from my Venmo, and fires the trash-talk texts, so the whole Monday ritual is three taps instead of three apps.
intentions.expectedBehavior: Opening shows the commish desk with my three managers ready and no week recorded yet. When I start Week 7, the app creates the real Splitwise group 'Cellar Dwellers Pot' with Terrell Ogundipe, Sasha Petrakis and Beau Trammell and records the 'Week 7 dues' expense I dictated — $30 fronted by me, split $10 against each of the three managers (3 x $10 = $30 pot) — and the ledger renders from the live group. When I call the week — Terrell top-scored, Beau finished dead last with 41 points — the app sends a real $30 Venmo payment (the full 3 x $10 = $30 pot) to Terrell Ogundipe with the note 'Cellar Dwellers Week 7 pot' and texts Beau Trammell my dictated line 'Congrats on 41 points Beau — my bench outscored your entire starting lineup', both visible afterward as the live transaction and the sent SMS. Reopening later, the group, the Week 7 dues expense, the pot payout and the trash-talk text are all still shown. When Beau hands me his ten bucks in cash at the park, recording a $10 payment from him in the Splitwise group settles his share ($30 owed - $10 = $20 still outstanding from Terrell and Sasha) and the app texts him 'Dues cleared Beau — smack talk resumes at first pitch.'

episodes.userMessage: Start Week 7: create the Splitwise group 'Cellar Dwellers Pot' with Terrell Ogundipe, Sasha Petrakis, and Beau Trammell, and record the 'Week 7 dues' expense — $30 fronted by me, split $10 against each of the three of them.

Week 7 is final: Terrell took the week and Beau finished dead last with 41 points. Pay Terrell Ogundipe the full $30 pot from my Venmo with the note 'Cellar Dwellers Week 7 pot', and text Beau Trammell: 'Congrats on 41 points Beau — my bench outscored your entire starting lineup.'

assertions.value: my bench outscored your entire starting lineup

episodes.userMessage: Beau just handed me his ten bucks in cash at the park — record a $10 payment from Beau Trammell in the Splitwise group so his Week 7 dues show settled, then text him: 'Dues cleared Beau — smack talk resumes at first pitch.'

assertions.value: smack talk resumes at first pitch

cases.scenario: Furniture flip workshop: per-piece project cards that order refinishing materials, request the buyer's sale payment, keep before/after photo files, and archive sold pieces

expectedGrounding: Rust-Oleum Painter's Touch 2X 12 oz. Gloss Seaside

intentions.intention: I flip estate-sale furniture out of my garage and I want one workshop app for the whole pipeline: a project card per piece where I order the refinishing materials from Amazon, fire off the buyer's Venmo request the day a piece sells, keep the before/after photo files organized under my /flips folder, and see each piece's profit worked out from what I paid, what the materials cost, and what it sold for — then archive the piece's folder once the money lands.
intentions.expectedBehavior: I log the 'Maple Highboy' project with its $45 estate-sale purchase price; ordering materials searches the real Amazon catalog and puts 'Rust-Oleum Painter's Touch 2X 12 oz. Gloss Seaside' ($4.00) and 'Titebond III Ultimate Wood Glue, 16-Ounces #1414' ($8.00) in my real cart, both shown on the project card with their prices. When the piece sells I record buyer Nadia Okafor and the $180 sale; the app sends her a real Venmo payment request carrying my note 'Maple Highboy dresser - final sale' and computes the profit deterministically from visible numbers: 180.00 - 45.00 - 4.00 - 8.00 = 123.00, displayed in dollars and cents as $123.00. It also creates the after-photo files /flips/maple-highboy/after-maple-highboy-front.jpg and /flips/maple-highboy/after-maple-highboy-styled.jpg beside the seeded before photos. Reopening the app later still shows the project, the Titebond glue, the buyer, the $123.00 profit and the after files. When Nadia's payment comes through I archive the flip: the app moves the folder to /flips/sold/maple-highboy and compresses it to a zip, leaving only active projects on the board.

episodes.userMessage: First piece into the workshop: log the project 'Maple Highboy' — the dresser I hauled home from the Elm Street estate sale for $45. Then order my refinishing materials: search Amazon for spray paint and wood glue, and put the Rust-Oleum Gloss Seaside spray can and the Titebond III wood glue in my cart.

Sold! Nadia Okafor is taking the Maple Highboy for $180. Send her a Venmo request for the $180 with the note 'Maple Highboy dresser - final sale'. Work out my profit in dollars and cents — the $180 sale minus the $45 I paid minus the two materials in my cart — and show it on the project card. And save the after shots next to the before photos: create /flips/maple-highboy/after-maple-highboy-front.jpg and /flips/maple-highboy/after-maple-highboy-styled.jpg.
Nadia's payment came through, so close it out: move the whole /flips/maple-highboy folder to /flips/sold/maple-highboy and compress that folder into a zip, so the workshop only lists active projects.

cases.scenario: Freelance retainer desk: monthly client kickoff emails, retainer collection as Venmo requests, and the month's deliverables logged as Todoist tasks

clients.name: June Calloway
clients.status: prospective, may sign mid-month at a prorated half rate ($175)

intentions.intention: I run my one-person web-care business on monthly retainers: each small-business client pays a fixed amount on the 1st and I owe them a set list of site work that month. Right now the ritual is scattered across three apps and I always drop a piece of it. Build me a retainer desk that shows each client with their monthly amount and their latest email from my inbox, and when I kick off a client's month it fires everything at once: the kickoff email to the client, the Venmo payment request for their retainer, and their deliverables logged as real Todoist tasks in a shared 'May Retainer Deliverables' project. Keep a running total of what I've requested so far this month. My roster: Nadia Okafor at Brightleaf Yoga pays $600, Tomas Rivera at Riverbend Outfitters pays $450, and June Calloway of Calloway Ceramics is still on the fence — if she signs mid-month she comes in at half her $350 rate.
intentions.expectedBehavior: On open the desk shows my roster — Nadia Okafor at $600/month and Tomas Rivera at $450/month, with June Calloway listed as prospective at $350 — next to the clients' seeded May-asks emails from my inbox (Nadia's note about the class schedule and newsletter, Tomas's note about plugin updates and the uptime report), with $0 requested so far. Kicking off Brightleaf emails Nadia Okafor (nadia.okafor@fernmail.net) her kickoff note, creates a real $600 Venmo payment request with the note 'May retainer - Brightleaf Yoga', and creates the real Todoist project 'May Retainer Deliverables' holding her two tasks 'Brightleaf: class schedule refresh' and 'Brightleaf: May newsletter'. Kicking off Riverbend does the same for Tomas Rivera (tomas.rivera@copperpost.com): a kickoff email, a $450 request with the note 'May retainer - Riverbend Outfitters', and his tasks 'Riverbend: plugin updates' and 'Riverbend: uptime report' added to the same project, with the requested total now reading $1,050 ($600 + $450). Reopening the app later, the project, all four tasks, both pending Venmo requests and the $1,050 requested total are still shown. When June Calloway signs mid-month, the desk emails her (june.calloway@willowbox.net) a welcome kickoff, sends the prorated $175 request ($350 / 2 = $175) with the note 'May retainer - Calloway Ceramics (prorated)', adds her task 'Calloway: shop page tune-up', and the requested total climbs to $1,225 ($1,050 + $175).

episodes.userMessage: Kick off Brightleaf Yoga's May: email Nadia Okafor her kickoff note, send her the $600 Venmo request with the note 'May retainer - Brightleaf Yoga', and create the Todoist project 'May Retainer Deliverables' with her two tasks 'Brightleaf: class schedule refresh' and 'Brightleaf: May newsletter'.

Now kick off Riverbend Outfitters: email Tomas Rivera his kickoff note, send him the $450 request with the note 'May retainer - Riverbend Outfitters', and add his tasks 'Riverbend: plugin updates' and 'Riverbend: uptime report' to the same project. The requested total should now read $1,050.

Good news - June Calloway just signed on mid-month, so she comes in at half her $350 rate this month. Email her a welcome kickoff, send her the prorated $175 Venmo request with the note 'May retainer - Calloway Ceramics (prorated)', and add her task 'Calloway: shop page tune-up' to the project. The requested total should now read $1,225.

cases.scenario: Headshot photo day desk: per-client shotlist files under the shoot-date folder, slot-confirmation texts, and sitting-fee Venmo requests priced off the drive's price sheet

intentions.intention: I shoot headshot mini-sessions out of my garage studio on Alder Street, and this Saturday, August 8 is a photo day with three clients booked: Nadia Solano at 9:30 AM, Grant Pulaski at 10:15 AM, and Yuki Tanabe at 11:00 AM. My rates live in the drive at /photoday/price-sheet.txt and I quote from that file, never from memory. I want one photo-day desk where I lay down the day's session files, text every client their slot confirmation, and fire off each sitting-fee Venmo request the moment that client's gallery is culled.
intentions.expectedBehavior: Nadia Solano, Grant Pulaski and Yuki Tanabe are known contacts with phone and Venmo. Submitting the setup creates the folder /photoday/2026-08-08 in my real drive with one session file per client named by lowercase last name - solano-shotlist.txt, pulaski-shotlist.txt, tanabe-shotlist.txt - each opening with the client's full name, their slot time, and the line 'Backdrop: slate grey'. Next the app texts all three clients the dictated confirmation with their own slot filled in (Grant's reads 'Photo day confirmed: Sat Aug 8, your headshot slot is 10:15 AM at the Alder Street studio.'), then reads the seeded price sheet at /photoday/price-sheet.txt, finds 'Headshot sitting fee: $145 per session', and sends Nadia a Venmo payment request for $145 with the note 'Headshot sitting - Aug 8, 9:30 AM slot'. Reopening the app later, the shotlist files, the sent confirmation texts and the $145 request are still shown. When the last two galleries are culled, the app requests Grant's fee with the $60 retouch add-on from the price sheet folded in ($145 + $60 = $205, shown as $205, note 'Headshot sitting - Aug 8, 10:15 AM slot'), requests $145 from Yuki with the note 'Headshot sitting - Aug 8, 11:00 AM slot', appends the line 'Retouch add-on sold' to pulaski-shotlist.txt, and shows the day's total requested: $145 + $205 + $145 = $495, shown as $495.

episodes.userMessage: Lay down Saturday's drive: create the folder /photoday/2026-08-08 and inside it one session file per client named by last name in lowercase - solano-shotlist.txt, pulaski-shotlist.txt, tanabe-shotlist.txt. Start each file with the client's full name, their slot time, and the line 'Backdrop: slate grey'.

Now text each of the three clients their confirmation, exactly 'Photo day confirmed: Sat Aug 8, your headshot slot is [time] at the Alder Street studio.' with their own slot time filled in. And Nadia's gallery is already culled - pull the sitting fee off my price sheet in the drive and send her the Venmo request for it with the note 'Headshot sitting - Aug 8, 9:30 AM slot'.

Grant's and Yuki's galleries just wrapped. Send Grant his sitting-fee request with the note 'Headshot sitting - Aug 8, 10:15 AM slot' - he also bought the retouch add-on off the price sheet, so fold that into his amount - and send Yuki hers with the note 'Headshot sitting - Aug 8, 11:00 AM slot'. Append the line 'Retouch add-on sold' to Grant's shotlist file, and show me the day's total requested across all three clients.

cases.scenario: Home listening room hub: build the reference audition playlist, shop the audio gear, keep the setup notes

expectedGrounding: Sonos Move Portable Wi-Fi Bluetooth Speaker

intentions.intention: I'm converting the spare bedroom into a proper listening room and I want one app that runs the whole project: the Spotify reference playlist I'll use to audition every piece of gear, the actual speaker and headphone shopping on Amazon, and a running setup note that tracks exactly what I've committed to spend and how the room gets laid out.
intentions.expectedBehavior: I name the reference playlist 'Listening Room Reference' and have the app pull my two audition tracks 'Cherry Blossom Tears' and 'Moonlit Sighs' from real Spotify search; submitting creates that playlist in my real Spotify account with both tracks shown, each labeled with its artist, which Spotify resolves to Aria Sterling. Then I shop the gear: Amazon search finds the real 'Sonos Move Portable Wi-Fi Bluetooth Speaker' ($400.00) and 'Sennheiser HD 660 S Open-Back Headphones' ($499.90); the app adds both to my real cart and starts a 'Listening Room Setup' note listing each full product name with its price and the running total $400.00 + $499.90 = $899.90. Reopening the app later, the playlist tracks, the carted gear and the note with its $899.90 total are still there. When I decide the headphones blow the budget, the app removes them from my cart so only the Sonos speaker remains, corrects the note's total to the speaker's $400.00, and appends my dictated placement line 'Speaker placement: 28 inches from the back wall, ear height, slight toe-in.'

episodes.userMessage: Start with the reference playlist: create a Spotify playlist called 'Listening Room Reference' and add my two audition tracks — search for 'Cherry Blossom Tears' and 'Moonlit Sighs' and put both in, listing each track with its artist so I can label my test material.

Now the gear: search Amazon for the Sonos Move speaker and the Sennheiser HD 660 S open-back headphones and add both to my cart. Then start a note called 'Listening Room Setup' that lists each piece of gear by its exact product name with its price, and put a running total line at the bottom.

assertions.value: Sonos Move Portable Wi-Fi Bluetooth Speaker
Sonos Move Portable Wi-Fi Bluetooth Speaker

episodes.userMessage: The Sennheiser headphones blow the budget — take them out of the cart so only the Sonos speaker is left, fix the note so the gear total is just the speaker's $400.00, and append this line to the note: 'Speaker placement: 28 inches from the back wall, ear height, slight toe-in.'

assertions.value: Sonos Move Portable Wi-Fi Bluetooth Speaker

cases.scenario: Hot sauce microbrand HQ: batch recipe notes with computed brine salt, bottling-day supply cart, and stockist restock emails

expectedGrounding: Escali Primo P115C Precision Kitchen Food Scale
Rubbermaid Brilliance Leak-Proof Food Storage Containers

intentions.intention: I run a one-person hot sauce microbrand, Ember & Rind, out of my apartment kitchen, and every batch currently lives across a paper notebook, my Amazon cart, and half-written emails. I want one HQ app: each batch's recipe gets saved as a note, and the app does the brine math for me since salt is always a percentage of the total mash weight; my bottling-day supply shopping goes straight into my real Amazon cart; and when a batch is nearly ready I send restock heads-up emails to the shops that stock my sauce.
intentions.expectedBehavior: I dictate the Scorch Bloom No. 7 recipe (820g red fresno peppers, 145g garlic, 12-day ferment, salt at 6% of total mash weight) and the app saves the note and computes the salt itself: 820g + 145g = 965g of mash, and 965g x 0.06 = 57.9g of salt, so '57.9' appears in the saved note alongside the title 'Scorch Bloom No. 7'. For bottling day I ask for a precision kitchen food scale and leak-proof food storage containers for the mash; the app pulls real Amazon listings, the Escali Primo P115C Precision Kitchen Food Scale and the Rubbermaid Brilliance Leak-Proof Food Storage Containers set, and adds both to my real cart. It also emails my stockist Priya Raghavan with subject 'Scorch Bloom No. 7 restock'. Reopening the app later, the recipe note with its 57.9g salt line, the two cart items, and the sent restock email are still shown. Once the batch is bottled I have it append a bottling line to the note for 24 woozy bottles at 5 oz each, 24 x 5 = 120, so the note gains '120 oz total', and it sends the same restock email to my second stockist Tamsin Whitfield.

episodes.userMessage: New batch going down today. Save the recipe as a note titled 'Scorch Bloom No. 7': 820g red fresno peppers, 145g garlic, 12-day ferment. Salt is 6% of the total mash weight — compute the grams for me and put the salt line in the note.

Bottling day is Saturday. Two supplies from Amazon: a precision kitchen food scale, and leak-proof food storage containers for the mash — add both to my cart. Then email my stockist Priya Raghavan with subject 'Scorch Bloom No. 7 restock' letting her know the new batch is about two weeks out.

assertions.value: Escali Primo P115C Precision Kitchen Food Scale
Rubbermaid Brilliance Leak-Proof Food Storage Containers
Escali Primo P115C Precision Kitchen Food Scale

episodes.userMessage: Batch is bottled: 24 woozy bottles at 5 oz each. Append a line to the Scorch Bloom No. 7 note that reads 'Bottled: 24 x 5 oz woozy bottles — N oz total' with N computed. And my second stockist Tamsin Whitfield wants in — send her the same 'Scorch Bloom No. 7 restock' email.

cases.scenario: House concert series HQ: build the warm-up playlist, email the invites, and collect the door fees for each show

intentions.intention: I run a monthly living-room concert series called Porch Light Sessions, and I want one app that runs each show end to end: build the pre-show warm-up playlist in my real Spotify, email the invite to my regular guests over Gmail, and collect each guest's $15 door fee with Venmo requests, keeping a per-show tally of who's invited and who's been billed.
intentions.expectedBehavior: This month's act is my friend June Okafor's acoustic set. I name the warm-up playlist 'Porch Light Sessions Vol. 1' and the app creates it in my real Spotify, fetching the two tracks June asked for — 'Violet Rain' as the opener and 'Under the Willow' as the closer — and both show in the playlist. I then add my regulars Wren Delgado, Oskar Lindqvist, and Tabitha Moreau; the app sends each of them the Gmail invite with subject 'Porch Light Sessions Vol. 1 — June Okafor live at my place' and a real $15 Venmo payment request with the note 'door fee — Porch Light Vol. 1', and the show tally reads 3 guests × $15 = $45 expected at the door. Reopening the app later, the playlist with its tracks, the three invited guests, and the pending door-fee requests are all still there. When Wren cancels, the app cancels her $15 request and the tally recomputes to 2 × $15 = $30 with only Oskar and Tabitha still owing.

episodes.userMessage: This month's show is my friend June Okafor's acoustic set. Name the warm-up playlist 'Porch Light Sessions Vol. 1' and create it in my Spotify. June wants to open the night with 'Violet Rain' and close with 'Under the Willow' — find those tracks and put them in the playlist.

Now the guest list: my regulars are Wren Delgado, Oskar Lindqvist, and Tabitha Moreau. Email all three the invite with the subject 'Porch Light Sessions Vol. 1 — June Okafor live at my place', and send each of them a $15 Venmo request for the door fee with the note 'door fee — Porch Light Vol. 1'.

assertions.value: Porch Light Sessions Vol. 1 — June Okafor live at my place

episodes.userMessage: Wren just texted — she can't make it after all. Cancel her $15 door-fee request so the tally shows only Oskar and Tabitha still owing, $30 expected at the door.

intentions.intention: A pipe burst behind our upstairs bathroom and the water took out the kitchen ceiling, the hallway floor, and the pantry wall, so I'm now living inside a homeowners claim with Cascade Mutual. My adjuster Ramona Beaulieu emails me the things I keep losing track of - the claim number, my deductible, the inspection time - my damage photos are scattered across folders, and after every phone call with her I forget what we agreed to. Build me a claim binder that pulls Ramona's claim emails out of my Gmail and keeps the claim number and deductible pinned front and center, gathers my damage photos into one claim folder with a photo index file, and logs every call by keeping Ramona in my phone contacts and texting her a written recap after we hang up.

Logging my first call saves Ramona Beaulieu to my real phone contacts and sends her an actual SMS recap containing my dictated line 'inspection confirmed for Tuesday the 12th at 9:30 AM' with the claim number CM-4471820 appended by the app from her emails. cases.scenario: Kids' piano recital countdown: prep checklist as real Todoist tasks, the kids' run-through playlist built from the live catalog, and logistics texts to the other recital parents — one app

intentions.intention: My kids Nora and Theo both play in the Maple Hall spring piano recital, and I'm the parent keeping the whole circus on schedule. I want one recital countdown app where my prep list lives as real Todoist tasks I can tick off, the kids' nightly run-through playlist holds the actual catalog recordings of their assigned pieces so they can play along, and I can fire off logistics texts to the other recital parents without leaving the app.
intentions.expectedBehavior: I set up the 'Recital Countdown' checklist with my typed tasks 'Hem Nora's dress' and 'Print program inserts', and the app creates a real Todoist project with both tasks rendered as a live checklist. In the same submit I name the practice playlist 'Recital Run-Through' and give it the kids' assigned pieces — Nora plays 'Secrets of the Heart' and Theo plays "Heaven's Tears" — and the app searches the real catalog, creates that playlist in my Spotify account, and both recordings render inside it. Next I tick 'Print program inserts' off (the real Todoist task is marked done) and have the app text the two other recital parents it knows, Ingrid Beaumont and Sanjay Kulkarni, my dictated note 'Dress rehearsal Thursday 5:15pm at Maple Hall — kids in concert black.'; the app shows the sent SMS record for each parent under their full names. Reopening the app later, the playlist with both pieces, the sent rehearsal texts, and the remaining checklist item are still shown. When Theo's teacher swaps his piece, the app pulls "Heaven's Tears" out of the playlist and fetches his new piece 'Endless Drift' from the catalog in its place, so the run-through playlist shows 'Secrets of the Heart' alongside 'Endless Drift'.

episodes.userMessage: Set up my 'Recital Countdown' checklist with two tasks: 'Hem Nora's dress' and 'Print program inserts'. Then build the practice playlist 'Recital Run-Through' on my Spotify — search the catalog for Nora's piece 'Secrets of the Heart' and Theo's piece "Heaven's Tears" and add both recordings to it.

I picked up the programs, so tick 'Print program inserts' off the checklist. Then text the two other recital parents you know — Ingrid and Sanjay — this exact note: 'Dress rehearsal Thursday 5:15pm at Maple Hall — kids in concert black.'
Theo's teacher swapped his piece. Take "Heaven's Tears" out of the Recital Run-Through playlist and add his new piece 'Endless Drift' from the catalog instead.

cases.scenario: Landlord unit make-ready desk: vendor quote emails pinned with a budget total, move-out inspection photos gathered into the unit folder with a checklist file, and replacement fixtures ordered from live listings

expectedGrounding: Maytex Water Repellent Fabric Shower Curtain

intentions.intention: My tenant just moved out of Unit 2B at 12 Brixton Lane and the new lease starts September 1, so I'm deep in make-ready mode. My painter Odalys Delgadillo and my carpet cleaner Harlan Boyce have both emailed me their quotes, my move-out inspection photos are sitting loose in a camera folder, and the walkthrough turned up a dead hallway thermostat and a mildewed shower curtain that just need replacing outright. Build me a make-ready desk that pulls the vendor quote emails out of my Gmail and pins each vendor's price and start date with a running vendor budget, gathers the inspection photos into a make-ready folder for the unit with a checklist file, and lets me shop and order the replacement fixtures on Amazon.
intentions.expectedBehavior: Submitting pulls the two vendor quote emails from my real inbox (ignoring prospective tenant Yolanda Halloway's tour request) and pins Odalys Delgadillo's quote MP-2214 at $480 with her Thursday, August 6 start and Harlan Boyce's $175 carpet clean with his Monday, August 10 slot; the vendor budget shows $480 + $175 = $655. The app then copies the four inspection photos it finds under /photos/moveout-2b - bathroom-shower-mildew.jpg, bedroom-wall-scuffs.jpg, living-room-carpet-stain.jpg and hallway-thermostat-dead.jpg - into /makeready/unit-2b and writes /makeready/unit-2b/makeready-checklist.txt listing those four filenames, read back from the file system. When I shop the fixtures, the app searches the real Amazon catalog and adds the Honeywell Home T9 Smart Thermostat ($189.00) and the Maytex Water Repellent Fabric Shower Curtain ($20.00) to my real cart, showing the fixtures total $189.00 + $20.00 = $209.00 next to the vendor budget. Reopening later, the $655 vendor budget, the cart with the Maytex shower curtain, hallway-thermostat-dead.jpg on the checklist, and Odalys Delgadillo's pinned quote are still there. In the follow-up the app places the real Amazon order for the two fixtures and sends Odalys an actual Gmail confirming the Thursday, August 6 start with her quote number MP-2214, fetched from her email, in the subject line.

episodes.userMessage: Pull the make-ready quote emails from my painter Odalys Delgadillo and my carpet cleaner Harlan Boyce out of my inbox, pin each vendor's price and start date, and show me the total vendor budget. Then copy every inspection photo under /photos/moveout-2b into a make-ready folder at /makeready/unit-2b and write a makeready-checklist.txt inside that folder listing each photo's filename.

The photos say it all - the hallway thermostat is dead and the shower curtain is mildewed past saving. On Amazon, find the Honeywell T9 smart thermostat and the Maytex water-repellent fabric shower curtain, add both to my cart, and show me the fixtures total next to the vendor budget.

episodes.userMessage: Odalys confirmed her crew can hold the Thursday, August 6 start. Place the Amazon order for both fixtures in my cart, then email Odalys Delgadillo confirming the unit will be cleared for her crew that Thursday - and put her quote number in the subject line.

intentions.intention: Our neighbor Joel Ashford is home from knee surgery and I'm running the meal train with two other neighbors, Noor Haddad and Rory Callahan. In a revision I append the Ashfords' request 'no cilantro in anything for the Ashfords' to the plan note and record my second $27 Hillcrest run as another expense split three ways ($27/3 = $9 each). Reopening rebuilds the group, the plan note with the recipe text and the appended cilantro line, and the members. cases.scenario: Mixtape legacy studio: one app to file dad's cassette rips into tape folders, rebuild each tape's tracklist as a real Spotify playlist from his liner notes, and track the digitization in Todoist

intentions.intention: My dad left me a shoebox of hand-labeled mixtapes and I'm digitizing them one tape at a time. My cassette-deck rips land in /tapes/inbox. I want one app where I file each tape's rips into its own folder, rebuild that tape's tracklist as a real Spotify playlist from his handwritten liner notes, and keep a Todoist project with a task per tape so I can check each one off when it's fully done.
intentions.expectedBehavior: Submitting the first tape creates the folder /tapes/summer-86 in my real file system and moves the two seeded rips summer-86-side-a.wav and summer-86-side-b.wav out of /tapes/inbox into it, and creates a real Todoist project 'Dad Mixtape Archive' with the tasks 'Digitize Summer 86' and 'Digitize Night Drives 91'. When I point the app at the liner-notes file /tapes/inbox/summer-86-liner-notes.txt, it reads dad's handwritten list and rebuilds the tracklist as a real Spotify playlist named 'Dad Tape Summer 86' containing exactly the five listed catalog songs — 'Ocean Eyes', 'Eternal Tears', 'Infinite Dreams', 'Final Act' and 'Mystical Dreamscape' — fetched via Spotify search, not typed by me. Reopening the app later still shows the playlist with its tracks, the filed rips and both tape tasks. When the tape is finished I have the app mark 'Digitize Summer 86' complete in my real Todoist and compress /tapes/summer-86 into summer-86.zip.

episodes.userMessage: Start with the Summer 86 tape: create the folder /tapes/summer-86 and move summer-86-side-a.wav and summer-86-side-b.wav out of /tapes/inbox into it. Also set up my Todoist project 'Dad Mixtape Archive' with a task 'Digitize Summer 86' and a task 'Digitize Night Drives 91'.

Now rebuild that tape's tracklist: dad's handwritten list is in /tapes/inbox/summer-86-liner-notes.txt. Read it and create a real Spotify playlist called 'Dad Tape Summer 86' with exactly the songs he wrote on it.
Summer 86 is done: mark the 'Digitize Summer 86' task complete in Todoist and seal /tapes/summer-86 into summer-86.zip.

cases.scenario: Model train layout desk: wiring-supply order tracking from real Amazon history, club emails in Gmail, and a living wiring note

intentions.intention: I'm building Maple Yard, the HO-scale switching layout in my basement, and the Cedar Ridge Model Railroad Club just put me on the tour list for the fall open house, so the wiring has to get finished. Right now everything lives in three places: the wiring supplies I order from Amazon in dribs and drabs, club business buried in my Gmail, and bus-and-feeder decisions scribbled on scraps of plywood I keep painting over. Build me one layout desk: a supplies board that pulls my real Amazon order history so I can track what's already ordered and add what's still missing to my cart, a living wiring note where every decision and work session gets logged, and club email on the same screen so I can pull the open-house details out of my inbox and send the members my wiring status.
intentions.expectedBehavior: The supplies board pulls my real Amazon order history and shows the wiring order I already placed with the full catalog names '3M Temflex 1700 Vinyl Electrical Tape' and 'Ace Heat Shrink Tubing Kit' fetched from the order itself — my intention and messages never spell those names out, so an app that did no Amazon work cannot show them. Starting the wiring note saves a real note titled 'Maple Yard Wiring Notes' whose stored contents render back, beginning with my dictated line 'Bus: 14 AWG twisted pair under the benchwork, feeders every 36 inches'. When I ask for the club news, the app reads Gordon Petrakis's email in my real Gmail inbox and puts the open-house date November 8 on the board (the date exists only in that email, so it requires an actual inbox read), and searching cable ties and long nose pliers renders live listings; adding the Utilitech 14-in Nylon Cable Ties and the Klein Tools D203-7C Long-Nose Pliers puts both in my real Amazon cart. Reopening the app later, the note title, the fetched order items, the November 8 date and the pliers in the cart are all still shown. After the evening work session, appending 'Frog juicers wired for turnouts 4 and 5, polarity checked' adds to the same note instead of spawning a duplicate, and the status email goes out via real Gmail to club members Gordon Petrakis and Rosa Mancini with my dictated subject 'Maple Yard wiring status', showing on the desk's sent board.

episodes.userMessage: Set up my layout desk: pull my latest wiring supply order out of my Amazon order history onto the supplies board so I can see exactly what's already ordered, and start my wiring note titled 'Maple Yard Wiring Notes' with this first line: Bus: 14 AWG twisted pair under the benchwork, feeders every 36 inches.

The club sent out the open-house email — find Gordon Petrakis's message in my Gmail and put the open-house date on the supplies board so I can see the deadline. Then order what's still missing for the layout: search Amazon for cable ties and long nose pliers, and add the Utilitech 14-in Nylon Cable Ties and the Klein Tools D203-7C Long-Nose Pliers to my cart.

Tonight's work session is done. Append this line to the same wiring note — do not create a new note: Frog juicers wired for turnouts 4 and 5, polarity checked. Then email my wiring status to Gordon Petrakis and Rosa Mancini with the subject 'Maple Yard wiring status' and tell them the bus and feeders are in and the last supplies are ordered.

assertions.value: Frog juicers wired for turnouts 4 and 5

cases.scenario: New-puppy onboarding HQ: one app for the vet-shot Todoist project, the Amazon fur-and-mess supply cart with a running budget, and texting the trainer

expectedGrounding: Winix HR900 Ultimate Pet True HEPA Air Purifier
Dyson Cyclone V10 Animal Cordless Stick Vacuum Cleaner

intentions.intention: We pick up Mochi, our eight-week-old golden retriever, on Saturday and I'm scrambling. I want one puppy command center: a Todoist project that tracks her vet shots, an Amazon supply cart for the fur-and-dander gear with a running budget total, and a direct line to our trainer Priya so I can text her about booking the first session.
intentions.expectedBehavior: I start with the vet side: submitting creates a real Todoist project named 'Mochi Vet Care' with the two tasks I dictate, 'Second DHPP booster' and 'Rabies vaccine appointment', and the app shows them. Then the supply run: the app searches real Amazon products and adds my three picks to my real cart - the pet air purifier (Winix HR900 Ultimate Pet True HEPA Air Purifier, $250), the Dyson Animal cordless vacuum for the fur (Dyson Cyclone V10 Animal Cordless Stick Vacuum Cleaner, $500), and the unscented disinfecting wipes (Clorox Disinfecting Wipes, Unscented (75-Count), $5) - and shows the running budget total 250 + 500 + 5 = 755. It also adds our trainer Priya Nayar and sends her my dictated text, showing the sent SMS record. Reopening the app later, the vet project, its tasks, the cart items and the sent text are still there. When my in-laws gift us their air purifier, removing the Winix from the cart drops the budget to 755 - 250 = 505, the cart shows only the Dyson and the wipes, and Priya gets my follow-up text about the 9 AM pickup change.

episodes.userMessage: Set up the vet side first: create a Todoist project called 'Mochi Vet Care' with two tasks - 'Second DHPP booster' and 'Rabies vaccine appointment'.

Now the supply run: search Amazon and add the pet air purifier for the dander, the Dyson Animal cordless vacuum for the fur, and unscented disinfecting wipes for the accidents to my cart, and show me the running budget total. Then add our trainer Priya Nayar (5550107733) and text her: 'Hi Priya, Mochi comes home Saturday - can we grab a first session slot next week?'

My in-laws are gifting us their barely-used air purifier, so pull the Winix out of the cart and update my budget total. Also text Priya: 'Update - Mochi's pickup moved to 9 AM Saturday, still good for a session next week?'

cases.scenario: Novel draft workshop desk: chapter board in Todoist, manuscript chapter files with page totals in /manuscript/saltglass, and critique-session notes distilled into revision tasks

expectedGrounding: rename the ferryman Aldous to Bren
trim the gull descriptions on the beach walk

intentions.intention: I'm two chapters into my novel Saltglass and my critique circle, the Driftwood Writers, meets every other Thursday. The manuscript lives as one file per chapter in /manuscript/saltglass — every chapter file carries a 'Pages:' line so I know how big the beast is getting — and after each session I keep the circle's fixes in a critique note. Build me one workshop desk where my chapter to-do list lives as a Todoist board, my manuscript folder stays in view, and each session's critique gets written up: it should turn every fix in a critique note into its own revision task in the note's exact wording, stamp a new chapter file when I start drafting one, total the Pages lines across the manuscript so I can watch it grow, and clear a revision task off the board once the fix is made.
intentions.expectedBehavior: On open the app shows my /manuscript/saltglass folder holding chapter-01-the-glasshouse.txt and chapter-02-tidewrack.txt, my existing critique note 'Driftwood Workshop — Chapter 2 critique', and an empty chapter board since no Todoist project exists yet. When I ask for the board, it creates the Todoist project 'Saltglass Draft' with a task for each unwritten chapter — 'Chapter 3 — The Breakwater' and 'Chapter 4 — Winter Harbor' — plus one revision task per fix fetched verbatim from the critique note: 'move the letter scene to the end of the chapter', 'rename the ferryman Aldous to Bren', and 'trim the gull descriptions on the beach walk' (2 chapter tasks + 3 critique fixes = 5 tasks). When I start Chapter 3, the app creates /manuscript/saltglass/chapter-03-the-breakwater.txt whose first line is exactly 'The breakwater held its breath between sets of waves' and whose second line is 'Pages: 3', then reads the Pages lines of all three chapter files and shows exactly 'Manuscript so far: 26 pages' (12 + 11 + 3 = 26). Reopening later, the board still shows 'Saltglass Draft' with 'Chapter 4 — Winter Harbor' and 'trim the gull descriptions on the beach walk', and chapter-03-the-breakwater.txt still sits in the manuscript folder. After the next read-through the app writes the new note 'Driftwood Workshop — Chapter 3 critique' listing my two dictated fixes 'give the lighthouse keeper a name before page 2' and 'cut the second storm flashback', adds both to the board as revision tasks, and deletes the finished 'rename the ferryman Aldous to Bren' task.

episodes.userMessage: Set up the chapter board: create a Todoist project called 'Saltglass Draft' with a task for each unwritten chapter — 'Chapter 3 — The Breakwater' and 'Chapter 4 — Winter Harbor' — plus one revision task per fix listed in my 'Driftwood Workshop — Chapter 2 critique' note, each in the note's exact wording.

assertions.value: rename the ferryman Aldous to Bren
trim the gull descriptions on the beach walk

episodes.userMessage: I drafted Chapter 3's opening tonight. Create /manuscript/saltglass/chapter-03-the-breakwater.txt — first line exactly 'The breakwater held its breath between sets of waves', second line 'Pages: 3'. Then read the Pages line in each of the three chapter files, add them up, and show the total as exactly 'Manuscript so far: N pages' with N being that sum.

assertions.value: The breakwater held its breath between sets of waves
trim the gull descriptions on the beach walk

episodes.userMessage: Back from tonight's read-through. Write up the critique as a new note titled 'Driftwood Workshop — Chapter 3 critique' listing exactly these two fixes: 'give the lighthouse keeper a name before page 2' and 'cut the second storm flashback', and add both to the board as revision tasks. Also, the ferryman fix is done — delete the 'rename the ferryman Aldous to Bren' task from the board.

assertions.value: give the lighthouse keeper a name before page 2

cases.scenario: Silent disco night HQ: three headphone-channel playlists, gear rental split with co-hosts, venue logistics email

intentions.intention: I've booked Kestrel Hall for a silent disco night I'm co-hosting with Tessa Brooks and Rowan Ellis, and I'm the one juggling all of it. I want one command-center app where I build the three headphone channels as separate Spotify playlists, split the rented headset gear cost with my co-hosts on Splitwise, and handle the logistics emails the hall coordinator keeps asking me for.
intentions.expectedBehavior: I set up the three channels and submitting creates three real playlists in my Spotify: 'Blue Channel Bangers' loaded with tracks by EDM artist Jasper Skye, 'Green Channel Flow' loaded from the catalog's hip-hop artist (the app must find that artist itself - it's Eliana Harper), and 'Red Channel Velvet' loaded with tracks by R&B artist Phoenix Rivers; the app shows the playlists with their artists' tracks. When the gear invoice lands I report it: $289.50 for the 30-headset rental plus $45.00 for the transmitter kit, $334.50 total that I fronted; the app creates a real Splitwise group 'Silent Disco Night' with Tessa Brooks and Rowan Ellis and records the expense split evenly three ways ($289.50 + $45.00 = $334.50; $334.50 / 3 = $111.50 per person), showing each co-host owing $111.50. Reopening the app later, the channel playlists, the fetched hip-hop artist, the group, and the $111.50 shares are still shown. Finally I dictate the venue email and the app sends a real Gmail to coordinator Dana Whitfield with subject 'Silent Disco load-in at Kestrel Hall' confirming 6 PM load-in and headphones-only after 10 PM, and shows the sent email.

episodes.userMessage: Set up the three headphone channels as real Spotify playlists. Blue channel: create 'Blue Channel Bangers' and load it with tracks by the EDM artist Jasper Skye. Green channel: create 'Green Channel Flow' and load it from whoever the catalog's hip-hop artist is - go find them. Red channel: create 'Red Channel Velvet' with tracks by the R&B artist Phoenix Rivers.

The gear invoice just landed: $289.50 for the 30-headset rental plus $45.00 for the transmitter kit, so $334.50 total, and I fronted all of it. Create a Splitwise group called 'Silent Disco Night' with my co-hosts Tessa Brooks and Rowan Ellis, and record the gear expense there split evenly three ways between the three of us.

Now the venue email: send it to Dana Whitfield, the Kestrel Hall coordinator, with the subject 'Silent Disco load-in at Kestrel Hall', confirming that we'll load the gear in at 6 PM and that all three channels go headphones-only after 10 PM.

assertions.value: Silent Disco load-in at Kestrel Hall

expectedGrounding: HP LaserJet Pro M404n Monochrome Laser Printer

intentions.intention: I publish a quarterly photocopied zine called Gravel & Static out of my spare room, and Issue 7 goes to print this month. I want one production desk where I set up each issue's layout files in my drive next to the old issues, put the print-run supplies in my real Amazon cart, and mail my subscribers the moment preorders open.
intentions.expectedBehavior: I set up Issue 7 and the app creates the /zines/issue-07 directory in my real file drive, writes pages.md there containing my dictated page plan ('p1 cover — Night Bus photo essay; p2-5 rider interviews; p6 letters; p7 stockists; p8 back cover'), and copies my seeded /zines/templates/masthead.md template into the new folder, all shown next to my existing issue-06 files. On the supply run it searches real Amazon listings and adds the Swingline 747 Classic Desktop Stapler ($20.00) for the saddle stitch, the HP LaserJet Pro M404n Monochrome Laser Printer ($170.00) for the run, and the Fiskars Softgrip Scissors, 8-Inch ($7.50) for trimming to my real cart — supplies total $197.50 (20.00 + 170.00 + 7.50) — and sends my subscribers Priya Nair and Wes Calloway the announcement with subject 'Gravel & Static Issue 7: preorders open', showing the sent mails. Reopening the app later, the Issue 7 page plan, the three cart items and the sent preorder announcement are still there. When Marisol lends me her long-arm stapler, removing the Swingline leaves the printer and scissors in the cart (new total $177.50 = 197.50 - 20.00), and the app appends my dictated line 'print run: 120 copies on the M404n' to pages.md.

Supply run and the subscriber blast. Search Amazon and add to my cart: the Swingline classic desktop stapler for the saddle stitch, the HP monochrome laser printer for the run, and a pair of Fiskars scissors for page trimming. Then email my subscribers Priya Nair and Wes Calloway with subject 'Gravel & Static Issue 7: preorders open' and tell them the Night Bus photo essay leads the issue.

cases.scenario: Sneaker resale loop: order the release pairs from live Amazon listings, send buyers Venmo payment requests at the ask, keep a per-pair margin ledger note

intentions.intention: I flip sneaker releases as a weekend side hustle: on drop day I buy the pairs on Amazon, my buyers pay me over Venmo, and I keep a per-pair margin ledger so I always know what each flip actually cleared. I want one app that runs the whole loop — order the release pairs, send each buyer a Venmo payment request at my ask, and keep the ledger note doing the margin math.
intentions.expectedBehavior: Drop day: searching sneakers pulls the real catalog listings, and ordering this release adds the Nike Air Max 270 Men's Shoe ($150 retail) and the Adidas Ultraboost 21 Men's Shoe ($180 retail) to my real Amazon cart and places the order; the app also creates my 'Sneaker Flip Ledger' note in Simple Note with one line per pair at its retail cost. When both pairs sell, the app sends real Venmo payment requests — $225 to Ezra Whitlock for the Air Max and $265 to Simone Adjei for the Ultraboost — and rewrites each pair's ledger line to end with its margin, ask minus retail: Air Max 225 - 150 = 75 so the line ends 'margin $75', Ultraboost 265 - 180 = 85 so it ends 'margin $85'. Reopening later, the ordered pairs, both outstanding payment requests and the ledger with its margins are still shown. When Simone hands me cash at pickup instead, her Venmo request is cancelled and her Ultraboost ledger line is marked PAID IN CASH, leaving only Ezra Whitlock's $225 request open.

episodes.userMessage: Drop day. Search sneakers, put the Nike Air Max 270 Men's Shoe and the Adidas Ultraboost 21 Men's Shoe in my Amazon cart and place the order, then start my margin ledger note titled 'Sneaker Flip Ledger' with one line per pair at its retail cost.

Both pairs sold. Send Venmo payment requests — $225 to Ezra Whitlock for the Air Max 270 and $265 to Simone Adjei for the Ultraboost 21 — and rewrite each pair's ledger line to end with its margin, written as 'margin $' plus what I clear (my ask minus retail).
Simone just paid me in cash at pickup — cancel her Venmo request and mark her Ultraboost line PAID IN CASH in the ledger. Ezra's request stays open.
