cases.scenario: Snow plow dispatch board: storm route laid down as Todoist tasks per driveway, real heads-up and all-clear texts to customers, and a Venmo payment request fired as each driveway is called done

customers.name: Walt Jensen
customers.addOn: sidewalk apron +$15 (he texted asking for it tonight)

intentions.intention: I plow driveways with my pickup during winter storms — three regulars on a fixed loop: Hank Delgado at 12 Foxglove Lane pays $50 a push, Priya Nair at 31 Juniper Hollow Road pays $55, and Walt Jensen's double-wide at 6 Tamarack Circle runs $65, plus $15 more if he wants the sidewalk apron cleared, which he just texted me about tonight. Storm nights I'm juggling the route in my head, texting customers with frozen thumbs, and forgetting who I've billed. Build me a plow dispatch board: when a storm hits it lays the route down as a real Todoist project with one task per driveway in plow order and texts every customer the heads-up for real; then as I call each driveway done it checks off that task, texts the customer their all-clear, and fires the real Venmo payment request for that driveway's rate — keeping a requested-so-far tally so I know what the storm was worth.
intentions.expectedBehavior: On open the board shows my three-stop loop with each customer's name, address, phone number and per-push rate — Hank Delgado / 12 Foxglove Lane / $50, Priya Nair / 31 Juniper Hollow Road / $55, Walt Jensen / 6 Tamarack Circle / $65 — plus Walt's seeded text asking to add the $15 sidewalk apron, with $0 requested so far. Kicking off the storm creates the real Todoist project 'Storm Plow Route' holding the three tasks in plow order — 'Plow 12 Foxglove Lane - Hank Delgado', 'Plow 31 Juniper Hollow Road - Priya Nair', 'Plow 6 Tamarack Circle - Walt Jensen' — and sends all three customers the real heads-up text 'Snow tonight - your driveway is on my plow route, first pass after midnight.' When I call the first two driveways done, the board completes Hank's and Priya's tasks, texts each of them 'Your driveway is clear - Venmo request on the way.', and creates the real payment requests — $50 to Hank Delgado with note 'Snow plow - 12 Foxglove Lane' and $55 to Priya Nair with note 'Snow plow - 31 Juniper Hollow Road' — with the tally reading $105 ($50 + $55). Reopening the app later, the project, Walt's still-open task, both pending requests and the $105 tally are still shown. When I finish Walt's driveway plus the sidewalk apron he asked for, the board completes his task, texts him 'Driveway and sidewalk apron are both clear.', sends Walt Jensen the $80 request ($65 + $15 = $80) with note 'Snow plow + sidewalk apron - 6 Tamarack Circle', and the tally climbs to $185 ($105 + $80).

episodes.userMessage: Storm's on for tonight — lay the route down. Create the Todoist project 'Storm Plow Route' with the three driveway tasks in plow order: 'Plow 12 Foxglove Lane - Hank Delgado', 'Plow 31 Juniper Hollow Road - Priya Nair', 'Plow 6 Tamarack Circle - Walt Jensen'. Then text all three customers the heads-up: 'Snow tonight - your driveway is on my plow route, first pass after midnight.'

assertions.value: Plow 31 Juniper Hollow Road - Priya Nair

episodes.userMessage: Foxglove and Juniper Hollow are done. Check off Hank's and Priya's tasks, text each of them 'Your driveway is clear - Venmo request on the way.', and send the requests: $50 to Hank Delgado with note 'Snow plow - 12 Foxglove Lane' and $55 to Priya Nair with note 'Snow plow - 31 Juniper Hollow Road'. The requested-so-far tally should read $105.

Just finished Walt's — and I cleared the sidewalk apron he texted about, so it's his $65 plus the $15 add-on. Check off his task, text him 'Driveway and sidewalk apron are both clear.', and send Walt Jensen the $80 request with note 'Snow plow + sidewalk apron - 6 Tamarack Circle'. The tally should now read $185.

assertions.value: Snow plow + sidewalk apron - 6 Tamarack Circle

cases.scenario: Storm-prep command center: water-shortfall math from a seeded pantry file, live-priced Amazon supply cart with a running kit total, family alert texts, and a go-bag document checklist filed under /storm-prep/go-bag

intentions.intention: Tropical Storm Verena is three days out and our county just went under a watch, so I want one storm-prep command center instead of six open tabs. It should read my pantry inventory file at /storm-prep/pantry-inventory.txt and do the water math for the four of us against the five-day rule — one gallon per person per day, minus whatever the file says we already have — shown as a line exactly like 'Water shortfall: N gallons'. It builds the supply cart from real Amazon listings and keeps a running banner formatted exactly like 'Kit total: $0.00' — dollar sign, two decimals, nothing else. It sends the family alert texts to my sister Camille Fontaine and my dad Roy Fontaine. And it keeps the go-bag document checklist filed under /storm-prep/go-bag so nobody is hunting for the passports while the sirens run.
intentions.expectedBehavior: On submit the app reads /storm-prep/pantry-inventory.txt from my real file drive, finds 'bottled water on hand: 9 gallons', and computes 4 people x 5 days x 1 gallon = 20 gallons needed, 20 - 9 = 11, showing 'Water shortfall: 11 gallons'. It then searches live Amazon listings and carts the cheapest camping lantern in the catalog — 'Black Diamond Moji Lantern' at 19.90, beating the 35.00 Voyager, 50.00 Apollo and 80.00 Coleman Quad — plus 'Energizer MAX AA Batteries (24-Pack)' (16.20) and 'Aquatabs Water Purification Tablets (100 Tablets)' (9.00), so the banner reads 'Kit total: $45.10' (19.90 + 16.20 + 9.00 = 45.10). On revise it texts Camille Fontaine and Roy Fontaine my dictated alert ('Storm update: if the county calls an evacuation we leave Friday 7am. Meet at our place, bring your meds.'), creates /storm-prep/go-bag, and files documents-checklist.txt with my three dictated lines including 'homeowners policy HO-4471002 — blue folder'. Reopening later still shows the 45.10 kit, the shortfall line, the filed checklist and the sent alerts. When the warning lands, the followup carts 'Anker PowerCore Slim 10000 PD' (30.00) and 'CVS Health Family First Aid Kit, 300 Pieces' (30.00) so the banner reads 'Kit total: $105.10' (45.10 + 30.00 + 30.00 = 105.10), appends 'car title — glovebox' to the checklist, and texts only Dad 'Upgraded to a warning. Gas up the truck tonight.'

episodes.userMessage: The watch is official — start the supply run. Pull my pantry file at /storm-prep/pantry-inventory.txt and do the water math: four of us, five days, one gallon per person per day, minus what the file says we have on hand — show it as a line exactly like 'Water shortfall: N gallons'. Then cart the basics on Amazon: the cheapest camping lantern they carry, the Energizer MAX AA Batteries 24-pack, and the 100-tablet pack of Aquatabs. Keep the kit total banner running.

Now the family side. Text my sister Camille Fontaine and my dad Roy Fontaine the same alert: 'Storm update: if the county calls an evacuation we leave Friday 7am. Meet at our place, bring your meds.' Then set up the go-bag: create /storm-prep/go-bag and file the checklist there as documents-checklist.txt with exactly these lines: 'passports — fire safe, top shelf', 'homeowners policy HO-4471002 — blue folder', 'vaccination records — filing cabinet, drawer 2'.

It's a hurricane warning now, not a watch. Add the Anker PowerCore Slim 10000 PD and the CVS Health Family First Aid Kit, 300 Pieces to the cart and update the kit total. Append 'car title — glovebox' to the go-bag checklist. And text Dad only: 'Upgraded to a warning. Gas up the truck tonight.'

assertions.value: CVS Health Family First Aid Kit, 300 Pieces

intentions.intention: Saturday afternoon I'm hosting a terrarium-building workshop on my back porch — four of us building, and I'm supplying everything. I want one prep hub for the whole thing: a supplies section that puts the real items into my Amazon cart and keeps a whole-dollar running budget, a build-notes section that saves my layering recipe to my real Simple Note so I can read it off my phone while I demo, and a prep checklist that lives in my real Todoist — including the moss pickup I already scribbled into a note a while back.
intentions.expectedBehavior: The supplies turn searches real Amazon and puts 4 of the IKEA KAFFEBÖNA Plant Pot ($8 each; searching 'plant pot' resolves uniquely to that catalog item) and 2 pairs of Fiskars Softgrip Scissors, 8-Inch ($7.50 a pair; 'Fiskars softgrip' resolves uniquely) into my real cart, and shows the whole-dollar running budget 4 x 8 + 2 x 7.50 = 32 + 15 = 47. The prep turn saves my dictated layering text to my real Simple Note as 'Terrarium Layering Recipe', creates the real Todoist project 'Terrarium Workshop Prep' with my dictated tasks 'Wipe down the porch table' and 'Print four care cards', and reads my seeded moss note to add the pickup task — surfacing Fern & Frond, the shop where the moss is reserved, which appears nowhere but inside that note. Reopening the app later still shows the IKEA KAFFEBÖNA Plant Pot cart line, the Terrarium Layering Recipe note, the Terrarium Workshop Prep project and the Fern & Frond pickup. When one builder cancels, updating the plant pot cart quantity down to 3 recomputes the budget 3 x 8 + 15 = 24 + 15 = 39, with both scissors pairs kept.

episodes.userMessage: Start with supplies: search Amazon for plant pots and add 4 of the plant pot it finds to my real cart, plus 2 pairs of the Fiskars softgrip scissors for the trimming stations, and show me a whole-dollar running budget for the supplies.

Now the prep side: save my layering recipe to Simple Note as a note titled 'Terrarium Layering Recipe' with this text: 'Gravel first for drainage, then a charcoal sprinkle, then potting mix, plant it, moss on top.' Then build a Todoist project called 'Terrarium Workshop Prep' with tasks 'Wipe down the porch table' and 'Print four care cards' — and dig up my old moss note in Simple Note and add the pickup as a third task naming the shop and the time.
One of our builders just canceled, so update the plant pot quantity in my cart down to 3 and recompute the supplies budget. Leave both pairs of scissors as they are.

cases.scenario: Triathlon race-week HQ: race-week checklist as Todoist tasks, logistics texts to my relay teammates, and a transition-area setup note

intentions.intention: Race week for the Lakeshore Sprint Triathlon is finally here — I'm the run leg of relay team Sharkbait and I want one app for the whole week: my race-week checklist kept as real Todoist tasks, logistics texts out to my two relay teammates, and a transition-area setup note I keep appending to as the details firm up.
intentions.expectedBehavior: Submitting my checklist creates a real Todoist project 'Lakeshore Race Week' with the tasks I dictate, including 'Pick up race packet' and 'Rack bike in transition Saturday 4pm', and shows them back to me. Adding teammates Nora Bell (5550138604, swim leg) and Felix Grant (5550138719, bike leg) and sending the packet-pickup text produces real sent SMS records for both naming Harbor Pavilion, and starting my transition note creates a real Simple Note whose body has my 'Row 12' rack-at-the-bike-out-end setup. Reopening the app later, the project, its tasks, the sent texts and the note are all still shown. For race-morning math the app computes the times itself: wave 8:10 AM minus 35 minutes = transition closes 7:35 AM, and 7:35 AM minus 50 minutes = on site by 6:45 AM; it appends the line 'Transition closes at 7:35 AM' to the note and adds the checklist task 'Arrive by 6:45 AM'.

episodes.userMessage: Set up my race-week checklist: a Todoist project called 'Lakeshore Race Week' with the tasks 'Pick up race packet', 'Restock gels and Body Glide', and 'Rack bike in transition Saturday 4pm'.

Now the team texts: Nora Bell (5550138604) swims and Felix Grant (5550138719) bikes. Send them both this message: 'Sharkbait relay: packet pickup Saturday 2-6pm at Harbor Pavilion, wear team blue.' Also start my transition note titled 'Transition Setup' with this content: 'Row 12, rack at the bike-out end. Helmet clipped on aero bars, run shoes at the back wheel.'

Last thing, race-morning math: my wave goes off at 8:10 AM, transition closes 35 minutes before the wave, and I want to be on site 50 minutes before transition closes. Append a line to my Transition Setup note that reads 'Transition closes at H:MM AM' with the actual closing time filled in, and add a checklist task named 'Arrive by H:MM AM' with my on-site time filled in.

cases.scenario: Used-car sale closer: buyer inquiry emails, test-drive scheduling texts, and a Venmo holding-deposit to lock the sale

intentions.intention: I'm selling my 2016 Honda Fit — asking $7,800 — and the sale is smeared across three apps: buyer inquiries land in my email, test-drive logistics happen over text, and the money moves through Venmo. Build me a sale-closer desk that shows the car with its asking price and each interested buyer with their offer next to their inquiry email from my inbox. Two buyers have written so far: Marisol Vega offered $7,400 and wants a Saturday-morning test drive; Grant Foley will pay full asking $7,800 but is only free on Sundays. When I schedule a test drive the desk should reply on that buyer's email thread AND text them the meet details — I do every test drive at the Fairview Commuter Lot. context.gala: Moonflower Gala (Wrenfield Youth Orchestra annual fundraiser)

donors.name: Soraya Merritt
donors.status: late pledge, phoned in after gala night

intentions.intention: I co-chair the volunteer committee for the Moonflower Gala, the Wrenfield Youth Orchestra's big annual fundraiser, and every year the same three messes eat my week: the prep checklist lives on a legal pad, donors who raised a paddle wait weeks for any confirmation, and the pledges trickle in however people remember to pay. Build me one committee desk that keeps the gala prep board as real Todoist tasks, and when I log a paddle pledge it fires everything at once — the confirmation email to the donor with the subject 'Your Moonflower Gala pledge', and a Venmo request for the amount with the note 'Moonflower Gala pledge - ' followed by the donor's name — while keeping a running pledge tally against our $5,000 goal. Saturday's paddle cards so far: Imogen Pemberton pledged $250 and Cormac Bankole pledged $150.
intentions.expectedBehavior: Setup creates the real Todoist project 'Moonflower Gala Prep' holding the three tasks I dictate — 'Stage the silent auction table', 'Print 140 seating cards', and 'Confirm the caterer's final headcount' — rendered as the prep board. Logging Saturday's two paddle cards emails Imogen Pemberton (imogen.pemberton@thistlepost.net) and Cormac Bankole (cormac.bankole@driftmail.org) their 'Your Moonflower Gala pledge' confirmations, creates real Venmo payment requests of $250 and $150 carrying the notes 'Moonflower Gala pledge - Imogen Pemberton' and 'Moonflower Gala pledge - Cormac Bankole', and the pledge tally reads $400 ($250 + $150) against the $5,000 goal. Reopening the app later, the prep board, both donors with their pending requests, and the $400 tally are still shown. When Soraya Merritt phones in a late $300 pledge, the desk emails her (soraya.merritt@quillbox.net) the same confirmation, sends the $300 Venmo request with the note 'Moonflower Gala pledge - Soraya Merritt', checks off the delivered 'Print 140 seating cards' task on the real board, and the tally climbs to $700 ($400 + $300).

episodes.userMessage: Lay down the gala prep board first: create the Todoist project 'Moonflower Gala Prep' with three tasks — 'Stage the silent auction table', 'Print 140 seating cards', and 'Confirm the caterer's final headcount'.

Now log Saturday's two paddle cards: Imogen Pemberton pledged $250 and Cormac Bankole pledged $150. For each donor send the 'Your Moonflower Gala pledge' confirmation email and the Venmo request for their amount with the note 'Moonflower Gala pledge - ' plus their name, and update the pledge tally toward our $5,000 goal.

A late pledge just landed — Soraya Merritt phoned in $300. Email her the same 'Your Moonflower Gala pledge' confirmation, send her the Venmo request with the note 'Moonflower Gala pledge - Soraya Merritt', and update the tally. Also check off 'Print 140 seating cards' — the print shop delivered them this morning.

cases.scenario: Warranty claim runner: Amazon order proof, the support email thread, and callback alarms for one broken espresso machine

intentions.intention: The espresso machine I bought on Amazon in early April has started losing pump pressure halfway through every shot, and I've opened a warranty claim with Meridian Appliance Care — their warranty desk rep Yusuf Grantham emailed me a claim reference last week. I keep losing track of which proof they still need, what I've already sent, and when they promised to call me back. Build me a claim-runner app: one claim card that pulls my real Amazon order in as the proof of purchase, digs the claim reference out of Yusuf's email in my Gmail, sends the follow-up emails he asks for, and keeps a callback log where every promised call gets a phone alarm so I never miss one.
intentions.expectedBehavior: The claim card pulls my real Amazon order history and shows the espresso machine order as proof of purchase with the full catalog product name 'Breville Barista Pro Espresso Machine' fetched from the order (the intention and my messages never spell that full name out — only the order itself has it), and it reads Yusuf Grantham's message in my Gmail inbox to put the claim reference WCR-58213 on the card (again only obtainable by actually reading the inbox). When I ask for the proof in writing, it sends a real Gmail email to yusuf.grantham@meridianappliancecare.com with my dictated subject 'Claim WCR-58213 proof of purchase', quoting the product name from the order and my note that the pump loses pressure, and the sent email shows on the claim timeline. When Yusuf calls and promises a decision callback for Thursday morning, the app logs the decision callback on the timeline and creates a real phone alarm at 09:30 labeled 'Warranty callback - Yusuf'. Reopening the app later, the claim card still shows WCR-58213, the Breville Barista Pro Espresso Machine proof line, Yusuf Grantham as the desk contact, and the sent 'Claim WCR-58213 proof of purchase' email on the timeline.

episodes.userMessage: Set up the claim card: pull my espresso machine order out of my Amazon history as the proof of purchase, and find Yusuf Grantham's claim email in my Gmail so the claim reference is on the card.

Yusuf wants the proof in writing. Email him on the claim: subject 'Claim WCR-58213 proof of purchase', and in the body quote the full product name from my Amazon order and tell him the pump loses pressure halfway through every shot.

Yusuf just called — no decision yet, but he promised a decision callback on Thursday at 9:30 in the morning. Log the decision callback on the claim timeline and set a phone alarm for 09:30 labeled 'Warranty callback - Yusuf' so I don't miss it.

cases.scenario: Youth team treasurer hub: the league's emailed invoice split across four families in a real Splitwise group, parent share texts, and a paid-in-full reply to the registrar

intentions.intention: I'm the volunteer treasurer for my daughter's U11 soccer team, the Brookfield Comets, and every team dollar runs through me. The Harborside Youth League just emailed me the fall registration invoice, and I want one app that pulls that invoice out of my inbox, splits the fee evenly across our four team families in a real Splitwise group, texts the other parents what their family owes, and replies to the league registrar once we're squared away.
intentions.expectedBehavior: Submitting creates a real Splitwise group 'Comets Team Fund' with parents Colleen Alcaraz, Samir Bishara, and Yuki Amemiya as members, and the app digs the Harborside Youth League invoice out of my Gmail inbox: the board shows the $360 team registration fee and invoice reference HYL2214 read from that email (I never state either value), records the $360 as an expense I paid split evenly across the four families, and shows each of the three parents owing me $90 ($360 / 4 = $90, exact). In a revision it texts all three parents my dictated reminder that their family's share of the league fee is $90, and the sent SMS records are shown. Reopening later, the group, the $90 shares, and the HYL2214 reference are still on screen. In a follow-up Colleen and Samir hand me cash, so the app records their two $90 payments in the Comets Team Fund group, leaving only Yuki's family owing $90, and replies to Lenore Fairbanks's invoice email saying the Brookfield Comets registration fee is paid in full, quoting reference HYL2214.

episodes.userMessage: Set up the Comets treasury: create a Splitwise group called 'Comets Team Fund' with the other three team families as members, Colleen Alcaraz (colleen.alcaraz@example.com), Samir Bishara (samir.bishara@example.com), and Yuki Amemiya (yuki.amemiya@example.com). Then find the Harborside Youth League registration invoice email in my inbox, show the fee amount and the invoice reference number on the board, record that fee as an expense I paid split evenly across our four families, and show what each family owes.

Now text each parent their reminder. Send Colleen (5550946201), Samir (5550946202), and Yuki (5550946203) exactly this: 'Comets update: your family's share of the league fee is $90, please settle up in our Splitwise group by Friday.'

assertions.value: your family's share of the league fee is $90

episodes.userMessage: Colleen and Samir just handed me cash for their $90 shares, so record their two $90 payments in the Comets Team Fund group; only Yuki's family should still show as owing. Then reply to Lenore Fairbanks's invoice email that the Brookfield Comets registration fee is paid in full, and quote her invoice reference number in the reply.

cases.scenario: Teen supervised-driving hours log with weather notes, synced by text to the co-parent

context.teenDriver: Mabel, my daughter, on her learner's permit
context.requirement: 50 supervised hours total, 10 of them at night, before her road test
context.nightRule: any session line containing 'at night' counts toward the 10 night hours
context.totalsFormat: headers 'Total: X.X of 50 hours' and 'Night: X.X of 10 hours', always one decimal place
priorSessions: 2023-05-06 17:30 'Drive log 2023-05-06: 1.5 hours, neighborhood loops, sunny and dry'
2023-05-10 20:45 'Drive log 2023-05-10: 1.0 hours, River Road at night, clear night'
2023-05-14 16:10 'Drive log 2023-05-14: 2.0 hours, highway merges, light rain'
todaySessions: Drive log 2023-05-18: 1.5 hours, downtown parallel parking practice, steady rain
Drive log 2023-05-18: 1.0 hours, River Road at night, clear and cool

intentions.intention: My daughter Mabel just got her learner's permit and the state wants 50 supervised practice hours, 10 of them at night, before her road test. After every drive I text my husband Rohan one session line so we both hold the record, always in the shape 'Drive log <date>: <hours> hours, <what we practiced>, <weather>' — the weather note matters because her examiner can ask about rain experience. I want an app that rebuilds her whole log from my text thread with Rohan, lists each session with its weather note, keeps two headers I can read at a glance — 'Total: X.X of 50 hours' and 'Night: X.X of 10 hours', always one decimal place — counts any line that says 'at night' toward the night hours, and when I dictate a fresh session line it texts it to Rohan and rolls it into both totals.
intentions.expectedBehavior: On open the app pulls my text thread with Rohan Acharya (5550620001) via search_text_messages and rebuilds Mabel's log from the three sessions already texted: 'Drive log 2023-05-06: 1.5 hours, neighborhood loops, sunny and dry', 'Drive log 2023-05-10: 1.0 hours, River Road at night, clear night', and 'Drive log 2023-05-14: 2.0 hours, highway merges, light rain', so the headers read 'Total: 4.5 of 50 hours' (1.5 + 1.0 + 2.0 = 4.5) and 'Night: 1.0 of 10 hours' (only the River Road at night line counts). When we get back from today's rainy session I dictate the line 'Drive log 2023-05-18: 1.5 hours, downtown parallel parking practice, steady rain'; the app sends exactly that text to Rohan at 5550620001 and the headers move to 'Total: 6.0 of 50 hours' (4.5 + 1.5 = 6.0) with night unchanged at 'Night: 1.0 of 10 hours'. After dinner Mabel drives again and I dictate 'Drive log 2023-05-18: 1.0 hours, River Road at night, clear and cool'; the app texts it to Rohan too and, because the line says 'at night', both headers advance — 'Total: 7.0 of 50 hours' (6.0 + 1.0 = 7.0) and 'Night: 2.0 of 10 hours' (1.0 + 1.0 = 2.0). Reopening later, the app re-reads the thread, now five texts deep, and the log still shows the downtown parallel parking practice session with its steady-rain note and the same recomputed headers 'Total: 7.0 of 50 hours' and 'Night: 2.0 of 10 hours'.

episodes.userMessage: We're back from today's session. Log it and text Rohan: Drive log 2023-05-18: 1.5 hours, downtown parallel parking practice, steady rain
Mabel drove again after dinner. Log it and text Rohan: Drive log 2023-05-18: 1.0 hours, River Road at night, clear and cool

cases.scenario: Sunday grandpa-call recaps appended to the family note and texted to siblings

priorEntries: Jun 14 - Walt fixed the porch screen himself; hip feeling steadier
Jun 21 - County fair stories; he wants everyone to visit in August

intentions.intention: Every Sunday evening I call my grandpa Walt for a check-in, and my siblings usually can't join. I want an app built around our running 'Sunday Calls with Grandpa Walt' note — one dated recap line per call. After each call I dictate the recap, the app appends it as a new line to that note, and it texts the same recap line to everyone on the recap list — right now just my brother Miles. The recap list should show each sibling with their phone number, and I need to be able to add another sibling to the list later and have them get the recap too.
intentions.expectedBehavior: On open the app shows the note 'Sunday Calls with Grandpa Walt' with its two seeded lines — 'Jun 14 - Walt fixed the porch screen himself; hip feeling steadier' and 'Jun 21 - County fair stories; he wants everyone to visit in August' — and the recap list with Miles Beckstrom and his number 5550472218 (from knownPeople). After this Sunday's call I dictate 'Jun 28 - Tomatoes finally ripened; Dr. Feld cleared his knee for stairs'; the app appends that exact line as the note's third entry and sends it as a text to Miles at 5550472218. When I revise, the app extends the Jun 28 entry with 'we picked Saturday August 8 for the family visit', adds my sister Nora Beckstrom (5550472219, from knownPeople) to the recap list, and texts her the updated Jun 28 recap. Reopening later, the note still contains the Jun 28 line with 'Dr. Feld cleared his knee for stairs' and 'Saturday August 8'.

episodes.userMessage: Just hung up with Grandpa Walt. Log today's recap: Jun 28 - Tomatoes finally ripened; Dr. Feld cleared his knee for stairs. Text it to Miles.

assertions.value: Dr. Feld cleared his knee for stairs

episodes.userMessage: Add to today's entry: we picked Saturday August 8 for the family visit. Also put my sister Nora on the recap list and text her today's full recap too.

value: Dr. Feld cleared his knee for stairs

seededConfirmationTexts.message: Parkview Dental: You're confirmed with Dr. Hoffbauer on Mon May 22 at 7:45 AM. Please arrive 15 minutes early and bring a photo ID. Reply C to confirm.
Cedarline Veterinary: Biscuit is booked with Dr. Ravindran on Wed May 24 at 9:10 AM. No food after midnight before the visit. Reply YES to confirm.

intentions.intention: Every appointment in my life arrives as a confirmation text — the dental office, the vet — and the prep always slips: forms I was supposed to print, the cat I was supposed to fast. I want an app that reads the confirmation texts on my phone and shows each upcoming appointment as a card with the office, the doctor, the date and time, and any instructions pulled straight from the text. When I pick an appointment and dictate its prep steps, the app turns them into a checklist project in my todoist named after the office — always '<office name> prep', like 'Parkview Dental prep' — with one task per step, and in the same motion it texts the office back the exact confirmation keyword their message asked for (they all want a 'Reply C' or 'Reply YES'), so I book in and get my prep list without leaving the app.
intentions.expectedBehavior: On open the app reads my texts and shows two appointment cards parsed from the seeded confirmation messages: Parkview Dental with Dr. Hoffbauer on Mon May 22 at 7:45 AM (arrive 15 minutes early, bring a photo ID, reply keyword C) and Cedarline Veterinary for Biscuit with Dr. Ravindran on Wed May 24 at 9:10 AM (no food after midnight, reply keyword YES); neither has a prep list yet. When I hand it the dental prep — 'Print the new-patient forms', 'Pack my night guard', 'Transfer $80 for the copay' — it creates the todoist project 'Parkview Dental prep' (the dictated '<office name> prep' naming) holding those three tasks and texts the keyword C back to Parkview Dental's number 5550731001, and the dental card now shows the checklist beside Dr. Hoffbauer's 7:45 AM slot. When I follow with Biscuit's vet prep — 'Fast Biscuit after midnight', 'Dig out the vaccine folder', 'Wipe down the carrier' — it creates 'Cedarline Veterinary prep' with those tasks and texts YES to 5550731002, so both appointments sit confirmed with checklists. Reopening later, both survive: 'Parkview Dental prep' still holds 'Pack my night guard', and 'Cedarline Veterinary prep' still sits under Dr. Ravindran's Wed May 24 9:10 AM card.

episodes.userMessage: Start with the dental one. Prep steps: 'Print the new-patient forms', 'Pack my night guard', and 'Transfer $80 for the copay' — and send Parkview Dental the confirmation reply their text asked for.
Now Biscuit's vet visit: 'Fast Biscuit after midnight', 'Dig out the vaccine folder', and 'Wipe down the carrier' — and send Cedarline Veterinary their confirmation reply too.

cases.scenario: Weekly reef tank water test log with rule-based dosing math

context.targets: alkalinity 8.5 dKH, calcium 400-440 ppm, nitrate under 10 ppm
context.dosingRule: 5 ml buffer for every 0.1 dKH below the alkalinity target
priorWeeks: Week of Mar 3 — alkalinity 8.4 dKH, calcium 420 ppm, nitrate 8 ppm — dosed 5 ml buffer
Week of Mar 10 — alkalinity 8.2 dKH, calcium 415 ppm, nitrate 9 ppm — dosed 15 ml buffer

intentions.intention: I keep a 15-gallon reef cube and test the water every Sunday — alkalinity, calcium, nitrate — and I want an app that keeps the running weekly log in one note and does the dosing math for me: my rule is 5 ml of alkalinity buffer for every 0.1 dKH the tank sits below my target, so each week's entry should record the readings plus the dose the rule calls for, and I also want to jot the corrective decisions when something drifts past my nitrate line.
intentions.expectedBehavior: On open the app shows my reef cube test log read from the saved note: targets of alkalinity 8.5 dKH, calcium 400-440 ppm, nitrate under 10 ppm, the dosing rule of 5 ml buffer per 0.1 dKH below target, and the two prior weeks — Week of Mar 3 (alkalinity 8.4 dKH, dosed 5 ml buffer) and Week of Mar 10 (alkalinity 8.2 dKH, dosed 15 ml buffer). When I submit this Sunday's readings of alkalinity 8.1 dKH, calcium 410 ppm, nitrate 12 ppm, the app applies my rule — 8.5 − 8.1 = 0.4 dKH low, 0.4 ÷ 0.1 = 4 steps, 4 × 5 ml = 20 ml — and appends the new week's entry in the same style as past weeks, ending in 'dosed 20 ml buffer'. When I then raise the alkalinity target to 8.7 dKH for my new coral, it redoes this week's math — 8.7 − 8.1 = 0.6 dKH low, 6 × 5 ml = 30 ml — so the entry now reads 'dosed 30 ml buffer', and since nitrate 12 ppm is over my 10 ppm line it also records my decision '20% water change Saturday' on the entry. Reopening later, the note still shows the 8.7 dKH target, this week's 30 ml buffer dose, and the 20% water change Saturday plan.

episodes.userMessage: Sunday tests for the cube: alkalinity 8.1 dKH, calcium 410 ppm, nitrate 12 ppm. Work out the buffer dose from my rule and log the week's entry the same way as past weeks.

My new torch coral wants more alk — raise my alkalinity target to 8.7 dKH and redo this week's dose from the rule. And nitrate is over my line, so add my decision to this week's entry: 20% water change Saturday.

cases.scenario: School carpool with weekly full-tank payer rotation

context.rotation: Raghunathans -> Delgados -> Tanakas -> my own week free

intentions.intention: Four families on my street share the morning run to Maplebrook Elementary and I'm the one behind the wheel every day — it's my minivan and my card at the pump. To keep it fair we rotate the fuel bill week by week: one week the Raghunathans cover my Friday fill-up, then the Delgados, then the Tanakas, and every fourth week the tank's on me. I want an app that keeps a 'Maplebrook Carpool Gas' Splitwise group with Priya Raghunathan, Marcus Delgado, and Ren Tanaka, where I log each Friday fill-up from the Peppertree Fuel Stop against whichever family's week it is so that family owes me the tank, shows the running total the families owe me, and lets me record it when someone hands me cash for their week.
intentions.expectedBehavior: On open the app shows the carpool gas ledger ready to log fill-ups, naming the three families and the weekly payer rotation. When I log the first two Friday fill-ups from Peppertree Fuel Stop — week 1 the Raghunathans' turn at $52.40 and week 2 the Delgados' at $46.30 — it records both expenses in the 'Maplebrook Carpool Gas' group with each tank owed in full by that week's family, so Priya Raghunathan owes $52.40, Marcus Delgado owes $46.30, and the running total owed to me is 52.40 + 46.30 = $98.70. Week 3 is the Tanakas' turn with a $49.80 tank, but their daughter missed the Wednesday-through-Friday runs so we agreed they cover half: I log Ren Tanaka's share as 49.80 / 2 = $24.90, and I also record the $52.40 cash Priya handed me for her week, so the outstanding total becomes 98.70 + 24.90 − 52.40 = $71.20. Reopening later, the group still shows the Peppertree Fuel Stop fill-ups and the $71.20 still outstanding.

episodes.userMessage: Create the Maplebrook Carpool Gas group with Priya Raghunathan, Marcus Delgado, and Ren Tanaka, and log the first two Friday fill-ups from Peppertree Fuel Stop: week 1 was the Raghunathans' turn, $52.40, and week 2 the Delgados', $46.30 — each tank owed in full by that week's family. Show me the running total owed to me.

Week 3 was the Tanakas' turn — a $49.80 tank at Peppertree, but their daughter missed the Wednesday-through-Friday runs, so we agreed they only cover half the tank; log Ren's share at half. Also Priya handed me cash for her full $52.40 — record that payment and show me what's still outstanding.

cases.scenario: Self-managed HOA small shared expenses split four ways in Splitwise, with receipt emails sent to the neighbors

context.hoa: Rowanberry Court — four self-managed townhomes around a shared courtyard, no management company
context.splitRule: every shared expense I front splits evenly four ways (me + 3 neighbors)
context.receiptRule: each logged expense also emails all three neighbors a receipt with subject 'HOA receipt: <what it was>'

intentions.intention: I'm the volunteer treasurer for the four townhomes on Rowanberry Court — our HOA is just us, no management company, so when the mailbox lock breaks or the courtyard needs mulch somebody fronts the cost and I'm supposed to keep the books straight. I want an app that keeps a 'Rowanberry Court HOA' Splitwise group with my three neighbors Priya Raghunathan, Walt Kowalczyk, and Ines Barbosa, where every small shared expense I front gets logged and split evenly four ways, and each logged expense also emails all three of them a receipt — subject 'HOA receipt: <what it was>' with the total, the per-unit share, and what it covered — and when a neighbor hands me cash for a share I can record the payment, so the running number for what the HOA still owes me stays honest.
intentions.expectedBehavior: On open the app shows the HOA expense book ready with my three neighbors and the even four-way split rule, nothing logged yet. I log the broken mailbox-cluster lock I paid to replace — $52, and 52 / 4 = $13 a unit — and the app creates the 'Rowanberry Court HOA' Splitwise group with Priya Raghunathan, Walt Kowalczyk and Ines Barbosa, records the $52 expense with each neighbor owing $13, and emails all three a receipt with the subject 'HOA receipt: mailbox lock' spelling out the $52 total and the $13 per-unit share, so the neighbors owe me 3 × 13 = $39. Next I log the courtyard mulch delivery — $96, and 96 / 4 = $24 a unit — which adds a second expense to the group and a second receipt email with the subject 'HOA receipt: courtyard mulch', lifting what's owed to 39 + 3 × 24 = $111; Walt Kowalczyk also hands me $13 in cash for his mailbox share, so I record that payment in the group and the outstanding total reads 111 − 13 = $98. Reopening later, the group still holds both expenses, both sent receipts are still on record, and the outstanding total still shows $98.

episodes.userMessage: Set up the Rowanberry Court HOA group with Priya Raghunathan, Walt Kowalczyk, and Ines Barbosa, and log the mailbox-cluster lock replacement I fronted — $52 split evenly four ways, so $13 a unit. Email all three of them the receipt with the subject 'HOA receipt: mailbox lock' covering the $52 total and their $13 share, and show me what the neighbors owe me.

The courtyard mulch delivery came to $96 — log it split the same four ways at $24 a unit and email all three the receipt with the subject 'HOA receipt: courtyard mulch'. Also Walt Kowalczyk handed me $13 in cash for his mailbox share, so record that payment in the group and show me what's still outstanding.

cases.scenario: Rotating supper club: a menu card per night plus an even four-way grocery split, kept in lockstep

context.rotation: host cooks the whole menu and fronts the grocery bill; everyone owes an even quarter

intentions.intention: Four of us run a rotating Thursday supper club — me, Imani Okafor, Theo Lindqvist, and Marisol Vega — and whoever hosts cooks the whole menu and fronts the grocery bill. I've been keeping a menu card in my notes for every night, titled 'Table #<number> — <theme>' with the host, the menu lines, and a final cost line in my exact format 'Groceries $<total> — $<per head> each' where per-head is the total divided evenly among the four of us; but the money side has only ever been IOUs scribbled on the fridge. I want one app that closes out each night in a single move: write the night's menu card in that same format, and record the same grocery bill as an expense split evenly four ways in a 'Thursday Table Supper Club' Splitwise group — setting the group up with the other three the first time I log a night. The app should show the archive of past menu cards alongside who owes what, and when a stray receipt from a night turns up later it should fix both sides — bump the Splitwise expense and rewrite that card's menu and cost line — so the card archive and the ledger never disagree.
intentions.expectedBehavior: On open the app shows the two archived menu cards from my notes — 'Table #11 — Hand-Pulled Noodle Night' ending 'Groceries $74.00 — $18.50 each' and 'Table #12 — Cast-Iron Paella' ending 'Groceries $96.20 — $24.05 each' — plus the club roster, ready to log my night. When I log Table #13, theme 'Georgian Feast', with a $101.80 grocery bill, the app creates the 'Thursday Table Supper Club' Splitwise group with Imani Okafor, Theo Lindqvist, and Marisol Vega, records the $101.80 expense split evenly four ways, and writes the note titled 'Table #13 — Georgian Feast' whose menu lists cheese khachapuri, chicken shkmeruli, and badrijani eggplant rolls and whose cost line reads 'Groceries $101.80 — $25.45 each' (101.80 / 4 = 25.45). When the forgotten $22.60 wine-run receipt surfaces, the app fixes both sides: the Splitwise expense is updated to 101.80 + 22.60 = $124.40, saperavi wine joins the card's menu, and the cost line is corrected to 'Groceries $124.40 — $31.10 each' (124.40 / 4 = 31.10). Reopening later, the 'Thursday Table Supper Club' group is still there and the Table #13 card still reads 'Table #13 — Georgian Feast' with the corrected line 'Groceries $124.40 — $31.10 each'.

episodes.userMessage: Last night was my turn — Table #13, theme Georgian Feast. Menu: cheese khachapuri, chicken shkmeruli, badrijani eggplant rolls. The grocery bill came to $101.80. Set up the Thursday Table Supper Club group with Imani Okafor, Theo Lindqvist, and Marisol Vega, record the bill split evenly among the four of us, and write the menu card.

Found a second receipt in my coat pocket — the saperavi wine run for Georgian night, another $22.60 I fronted. Fold it into Table #13: bump the Splitwise expense to cover it, add saperavi wine to the card's menu, and correct the card's cost line.

cases.scenario: Church choir warm-up ladder with slow-to-brisk tempo progression

context.choir: St. Bartholomew church choir, Thursday-evening rehearsal
stages: Stage 1 slow — breathing and gentle humming
Stage 2 moderate — scales and range work
Stage 3 brisk — energizer before the anthems
context.openingState: empty three-stage ladder, no songs picked yet

intentions.intention: I direct our small church choir and every Thursday-evening rehearsal opens with a warm-up set that has to climb in tempo: a slow piece for breathing and gentle humming first, a moderate one for scales and range work in the middle, and a brisk closer that wakes everybody up before we start the anthems. I want an app that keeps this warm-up ladder as a real playlist in my music library in exact slow-to-brisk order, shows each stage's track with its artist and length in seconds plus a combined 'Total: N seconds' line so I can keep us inside our fifteen-minute window, and lets me swap out a single stage's song when the choir grows tired of it without breaking the tempo order.
intentions.expectedBehavior: On open the app shows the empty three-stage ladder (slow / moderate / brisk) with an input for my picks. When I give this week's picks it searches the catalog and finds 'Whispers of the Soul' (270 s, Mia Sullivan & Carter Knight) for the slow stage, 'Serenade of the Silver Moon' (232 s, Oceanic Odyssey) for the moderate stage and 'Hearts on Fire' (183 s, Grace Harrison) for the brisk stage, creates the playlist 'Thursday Warm-Up Ladder' with the three songs added in that stage order, and shows each stage with artist and length plus the combined line 'Total: 685 seconds' (270+232+183=685). When the sopranos tire of the moderate piece I swap only that stage for 'Waiting for the Morning Light' (204 s, Grace Harrison): the app removes 'Serenade of the Silver Moon' from the playlist, adds the replacement into the middle stage keeping slow-to-brisk order, and refreshes the line to 'Total: 657 seconds' (270+204+183=657). Reopening later, the ladder still shows 'Thursday Warm-Up Ladder' with 'Whispers of the Soul', 'Waiting for the Morning Light' and 'Hearts on Fire' in stage order.

episodes.userMessage: This week's picks — slow stage: Whispers of the Soul, moderate stage: Serenade of the Silver Moon, brisk stage: Hearts on Fire. Build the playlist in that order, name it Thursday Warm-Up Ladder, and show me each stage's artist and length plus the combined 'Total: N seconds' line.
The sopranos are tired of the moderate piece — swap Serenade of the Silver Moon out for Waiting for the Morning Light, keep the slow and brisk stages exactly as they are, and refresh the total.

cases.scenario: Vinyl collection migrated to streaming one crate at a time

intentions.intention: My new apartment has no room for the turntable, so my vinyl collection is going into storage and I want an app that migrates it into my streaming account one crate at a time. Each session I type a crate's label and the records inside it; the app finds each album in the catalog, builds a playlist named 'Crate N: <label>' holding every track from those records, and also saves each album to my album library so my digital shelf mirrors the physical crates. It should keep a running list of finished crates so I can see how far through the collection I am.
intentions.expectedBehavior: On open the migrator shows zero finished crates and invites me to enter my first crate. I enter crate label 'Den Jazz' with records 'Velvet Underground', 'Mystical Crescendo', and 'Dreamscape Delights'; the app searches the catalog for each album, shows that all three are by Aria Sterling (a fact I never typed - it must fetch the albums to learn it), creates the playlist 'Crate 1: Den Jazz', adds every track from the three albums to it, and saves all three albums to my album library, marking the crate finished with 3 records. Next session I enter crate 'Garage Rock' with records 'Astral Journey', 'Midnight Serenade', and 'Electric Dreamscape'; the app does the same drill - playlist 'Crate 2: Garage Rock' with all their tracks, albums saved to my library - and the finished list now shows two crates, 3 + 3 = 6 records migrated. Reopening later, both playlists are still in my playlist library and the migrated albums are still in my album library, so the migrator re-lists 'Crate 1: Den Jazz' and 'Crate 2: Garage Rock' with their records, including 'Dreamscape Delights' and 'Midnight Serenade'.

episodes.userMessage: First crate. Label: Den Jazz. Records inside: Velvet Underground, Mystical Crescendo, Dreamscape Delights. Find each album in the catalog, make the playlist 'Crate 1: Den Jazz' with every track from those three albums, save each album to my library, and show me who the artist is on each record.

Next crate. Label: Garage Rock. Records inside: Astral Journey, Midnight Serenade, Electric Dreamscape. Same drill: playlist 'Crate 2: Garage Rock' with all their tracks, and save the albums to my library.

cases.scenario: Concert night coordinator: warm-up playlist plus plan email to the crew

context.concert: Nova Harmony at the Harborlight Pavilion, Saturday

intentions.intention: My two concert buddies and I finally grabbed tickets to the Nova Harmony show, and somehow I'm always the one herding everyone over group text. I want a concert-night coordinator where I build our pre-show warm-up playlist in my Spotify - I name it and feed it the exact tracks I want the crew to have on repeat all week - and once the plan is locked it emails both buddies the full rundown: where and when we meet plus the final tracklist. If I rework the playlist before the email goes out, the rundown has to carry the final version, not my first draft.
intentions.expectedBehavior: On open the app shows my concert crew - Callie Brennan and Dario Fontaine from my contacts - with no warm-up playlist yet and the plan email marked unsent. When I kick things off it creates the playlist 'Nova Night Warm-Up' in my Spotify and pulls the real catalog tracks 'Violet Rain', 'Kaleidoscope Heart', and 'Trapped in a Daydream' into it, listing all three. Then I swap 'Trapped in a Daydream' for 'Mystic Voyage to Avalon', so the playlist reads Violet Rain / Kaleidoscope Heart / Mystic Voyage to Avalon, and the app emails callie.brennan@copperkite.net and dario.fontaine@lanternhill.io with subject 'Nova Harmony night: the plan', the Saturday 6:30 pm meetup at the Harborlight Pavilion main gate, and that final three-track list in the body. Reopening later, 'Nova Night Warm-Up' still holds the final tracklist ending in 'Mystic Voyage to Avalon' and the sent plan email is still on record.

episodes.userMessage: Kick off our warm-up playlist for the Nova Harmony show: call it Nova Night Warm-Up and load it with Violet Rain, Kaleidoscope Heart, and Trapped in a Daydream.

Swap Trapped in a Daydream out for Mystic Voyage to Avalon, then email the plan to Callie and Dario with subject 'Nova Harmony night: the plan' - we meet Saturday 6:30 pm at the Harborlight Pavilion main gate, and include the final tracklist.

cases.scenario: Morning alarms paired with genre wake-up playlists

intentions.intention: I cannot drag myself out of bed to a beeping alarm, so each weekday I care about gets a proper music wake-up: a phone alarm at the time I choose, paired with a small genre playlist of songs I name from the catalog. I want one app that keeps these day pairings together — when I set up a day it creates the alarm on my phone and builds the named playlist in my spotify, and I can add another day's pairing later when I decide, say, that Wednesdays deserve reggae.
intentions.expectedBehavior: On open the app shows an empty wake-up pairing board with a way to enter a day, an alarm time, a genre, a playlist name, and the songs I want. When I set up Monday — alarm at 6:20 AM, jazz, playlist 'Monday Jazz Sunrise' with 'Whispers of Destiny', 'Moonlit Sighs', and 'Mystic Rhythms' — the app creates the 6:20 AM phone alarm, searches each named song in the spotify catalog to get its track, creates the 'Monday Jazz Sunrise' playlist and adds all three, and the Monday card shows the alarm time alongside the three titles. When I then give Wednesday to reggae — alarm at 6:50 AM, playlist 'Wednesday Reggae Lift' with 'Midnight Train', 'Serenity in the Rain', and 'Stardust Serenade' — a second phone alarm is created and the reggae playlist is built the same way, so the board now shows both day pairings. Reopening later, both pairings survive: 'Monday Jazz Sunrise' still holds 'Whispers of Destiny', 'Moonlit Sighs', and 'Mystic Rhythms', and the 6:50 AM Wednesday alarm still pairs with 'Wednesday Reggae Lift' ending in 'Stardust Serenade'.

episodes.userMessage: Set up Monday: alarm at 6:20 AM and a jazz wake-up playlist named Monday Jazz Sunrise with Whispers of Destiny, Moonlit Sighs, and Mystic Rhythms.
Wednesdays deserve reggae: alarm at 6:50 AM, playlist named Wednesday Reggae Lift with Midnight Train, Serenity in the Rain, and Stardust Serenade.

cases.scenario: Lyric interpretation journal paired with liked Spotify favorites

seededNote.title: Lyric Notes - The Fragrance of Fading Roses
seededNote.content: First pass: nostalgia is the perfume, not the flower - the roses fade because memory keeps embellishing their scent.

annotatedSongs: Reflections in a Pool of Regret

intentions.intention: I obsess over what songs actually mean, so I want a lyric journal app that shows my Spotify favorites side by side with my interpretation notes. When a song gets under my skin I tell the app: it likes the track in my real Spotify and starts a note titled 'Lyric Notes - <song title>' holding my reading of the lyrics, and on later listens I can dictate a follow-up line that gets appended to that song's note so each interpretation grows over time. I already keep one of these notes for 'The Fragrance of Fading Roses' and want it on the board from day one.
intentions.expectedBehavior: On open the journal shows my one existing note 'Lyric Notes - The Fragrance of Fading Roses' with its line 'First pass: nostalgia is the perfume, not the flower - the roses fade because memory keeps embellishing their scent.' When I bring in 'Reflections in a Pool of Regret', the app finds that real catalog track, likes it in my Spotify, and creates 'Lyric Notes - Reflections in a Pool of Regret' containing my dictated take 'Regret here is a choice, not a haunting - the pool only ripples because the singer keeps reaching back into it.', so the board shows the song title next to that line. When I add 'Rust and Stardust', the app likes that track too and creates its note with 'Two portraits of the same long love - rust is what the years corroded, stardust is what still glitters underneath.', and in the same turn appends 'Second listen - the final chorus forgives the exact mistake the first verse keeps rehearsing.' to the Reflections note, which now shows both lines. Reopening later, both liked favorites are still on the board with their notes intact: the Reflections note still ends with the second-listen line and the Rust and Stardust note still holds its reading.

episodes.userMessage: 'Reflections in a Pool of Regret' has been stuck in my head all week. Like it on Spotify and start its lyric note with my take: Regret here is a choice, not a haunting - the pool only ripples because the singer keeps reaching back into it.

cases.scenario: Cello repertoire ladder with per-piece mastery rungs

seededLadderTasks: Serenade of the Silver Moon - Polishing

intentions.intention: I'm an adult cello student slowly building a real repertoire, and I picture it as a ladder: every piece I'm working up is one task in my Todoist 'Repertoire Ladder' project titled '<Song> - <Rung>', where the rung climbs from Learning to Polishing to Mastered. I want an app that shows my ladder grouped by rung and works it with me: when a piece climbs a rung I rewrite its task title to the new rung, when a piece is finally mastered its task gets checked off as done and the song's recording is filed into a 'Mastered Repertoire' playlist on Spotify (created the first time I master something), and when a new piece joins at the bottom it gets a fresh Learning task plus a like on its recording so the reference version is waiting in my Liked Songs.
intentions.expectedBehavior: On open the app loads my 'Repertoire Ladder' Todoist project and shows the two pieces currently on the ladder grouped by rung — 'Serenade of the Silver Moon - Polishing' and 'Cherry Blossom Tears - Learning' — with no Mastered Repertoire playlist yet. When I report Serenade of the Silver Moon mastered, the app marks that ladder task done in Todoist, searches Spotify for the recording, creates the 'Mastered Repertoire' playlist and adds the track as its first entry. Next I bump Cherry Blossom Tears a rung, so its task title is rewritten to 'Cherry Blossom Tears - Polishing', and I add Whispers of the Enchanted Forest at the bottom: a new task 'Whispers of the Enchanted Forest - Learning' is created and its recording is liked on Spotify. Reopening later, the Mastered Repertoire playlist still holds Serenade of the Silver Moon, and the ladder still shows Cherry Blossom Tears at Polishing and Whispers of the Enchanted Forest at Learning.

episodes.userMessage: Serenade of the Silver Moon is finally mastered — check its ladder task off as done, then create my 'Mastered Repertoire' playlist on Spotify and add its recording as the first track.

Bump Cherry Blossom Tears up a rung — rewrite its task title to 'Cherry Blossom Tears - Polishing' — and put Whispers of the Enchanted Forest on the bottom rung: create the task 'Whispers of the Enchanted Forest - Learning' and like its recording on Spotify.

assertions.value: Whispers of the Enchanted Forest - Learning

value: Whispers of the Enchanted Forest - Learning

cases.scenario: DJ tip jar: party song requests honored only after the venmo tip lands

paidRequest.song: Dancing in a Field of Thorns
paidRequest.seededTipDescription: DJ tip: Dancing in a Field of Thorns

unpaidRequest.requestNote: DJ tip jar: City of Fallen Angels

intentions.intention: I DJ the rooftop parties at my building on Juniper Street and I run the decks on a strict tip-jar rule: five bucks in the venmo jar or your song does not get played. I want a request-board app that keeps me honest — when a guest names a song and claims they tipped, it checks my venmo for their $5 before the song earns a spot on the night's request playlist, and when someone begs without paying, it parks their request as unpaid and fires off a $5 venmo request with the song named in the note so they can settle up from the dance floor.
intentions.expectedBehavior: On open the app shows an empty request board for tonight's set with the $5-per-request tip-jar rule and a way to log a guest, the song they want, and whether they claim to have tipped. When Priya Raghunathan requests 'Dancing in a Field of Thorns' and says her tip landed, the app reads my venmo transactions and finds her $5 payment described 'DJ tip: Dancing in a Field of Thorns' (seeded in the fixture), then honors the request: it creates the 'Juniper Street Request Line' playlist in spotify, searches the catalog for the track to get its song id, adds it, and marks Priya's card paid and queued. When Marcus Ostrowski begs for 'City of Fallen Angels' without tipping, the app does NOT touch the playlist — it parks his card as unpaid and sends him a $5 venmo payment request with the note 'DJ tip jar: City of Fallen Angels'. Reopening later, 'Juniper Street Request Line' still holds 'Dancing in a Field of Thorns', and Marcus Ostrowski's unpaid 'City of Fallen Angels' request is still waiting on the outstanding $5.

episodes.userMessage: First request of the night: Priya Raghunathan wants Dancing in a Field of Thorns and swears her $5 tip just hit my venmo. Verify her $5 actually landed in the jar, then start the party playlist Juniper Street Request Line and add her song.

assertions.value: Dancing in a Field of Thorns

episodes.userMessage: Marcus Ostrowski is begging for City of Fallen Angels but hasn't tipped. Park it as unpaid — do not add it to the playlist yet — and send him a $5 venmo request with the note DJ tip jar: City of Fallen Angels.

assertions.value: DJ tip jar: City of Fallen Angels

cases.scenario: Foster kitten feeding, vet and adoption task board

context.formulaRule: 20 ml of formula per 100 grams of body weight per feeding
seededTasks: Spay surgery consult at Cedar Hollow Animal Clinic - Clover

intentions.intention: I'm a bottle-baby foster for Willow Bend Cat Rescue and my current pair is the Maple Litter - Clover and Bramble, both still on formula. Their care already lives in my 'Maple Litter Foster Board' project and I want an app that runs it as my one board for feeding, vet, and adoption work. Each kitten's feeding task always follows the shape 'Bottle-feed <kitten> - <amount> ml every 4 hours', and after every weigh-in the amount is recomputed by the rescue's rule of 20 ml of formula per 100 grams of body weight per feeding - I tell the app the new weight and it rewrites that kitten's feeding line. Vet items like deworming rounds and surgery consults sit alongside the feeding tasks, and the moment a kitten gets matched with an adopter the board grows an Adoption section that holds the handoff steps.
intentions.expectedBehavior: On open the app shows my seeded 'Maple Litter Foster Board' project with its four care tasks: 'Bottle-feed Clover - 70 ml every 4 hours', 'Bottle-feed Bramble - 65 ml every 4 hours', 'Deworming round 2 - both kittens', and 'Spay surgery consult at Cedar Hollow Animal Clinic - Clover'. After Bramble's morning weigh-in I report 410 grams; the app applies the rescue's rule (410 g x 20 ml per 100 g = 82 ml) and updates his feeding task to read 'Bottle-feed Bramble - 82 ml every 4 hours' while Clover's line stays at 70 ml. When Clover's adoption application is approved I have the app add an 'Adoption' section holding the new task 'Meet-and-greet with the Delgado family', so the adoption lane now sits next to the care tasks. Reopening later, Bramble's line still reads 'Bottle-feed Bramble - 82 ml every 4 hours' and the Adoption section still holds 'Meet-and-greet with the Delgado family'.

episodes.userMessage: Bramble's morning weigh-in came to 410 grams. With our rule of 20 ml per 100 grams per feeding, update his bottle-feed line to the new amount.
Great news - Clover's adoption application was approved. Add an Adoption section to the board and put this task in it: Meet-and-greet with the Delgado family

cases.scenario: Roommate security-deposit escrow: collect shares, then split the landlord refund

context.split: equal three-way between me and the two roommates
context.refundFunding: the landlord's refund check lands in my bank, so my Visa on file pulls it onto my Venmo balance before I pay the shares out

intentions.intention: When we signed the lease at 44 Corliss Ave I fronted the whole $2,400 security deposit for the three of us, and I refuse to let that money dissolve into roommate vibes. Build me a deposit escrow board that tracks the deposit's whole life: it shows the $2,400 I put up against a clean three-way split with Priya and Owen, fires off a Venmo request to each of them for their share when I say collect, and at move-out — after the landlord docks whatever he docks — it computes each person's refund share of what actually came back and pays my roommates theirs out of my balance, so the math lives on a screen instead of in our group chat.
intentions.expectedBehavior: On open the escrow board shows the 44 Corliss Ave deposit at $2,400 fronted by me, split three ways with Priya Natarajan and Owen Gallagher each owing a one-third share, refund column pending, my $40 balance float and Visa on file. When I say collect, the app computes each share as $2,400 / 3 = $800 and sends both roommates a Venmo payment request noted '44 Corliss deposit share' via create_payment_request, so each roommate's row flips from unpaid to requested and reads '$800 deposit share' — for Priya Natarajan and for Owen Gallagher. At move-out I report the landlord returned $2,100 after a $300 repaint deduction; the app pulls the $2,100 onto my balance from my Visa via add_to_venmo_balance, computes each refund share as $2,100 / 3 = $700 (equivalently ($2,400 - $300) / 3 = $700), and sends Priya and Owen $700 each noted '44 Corliss deposit refund' via create_transaction, so each row shows its '$700 refund share' sent and my own $700 share stays parked in my balance ($40 + $2,100 - 2 x $700 = $740). Reopening later, the board re-reads my sent requests and transactions and still shows both '$800 deposit share' requests and both '$700 refund share' payouts.

episodes.userMessage: The lease is signed and I'm out the full $2,400 — send Priya and Owen each a Venmo request for their one-third deposit share, noted '44 Corliss deposit share'.

Move-out inspection came back: the landlord returned $2,100 after docking $300 for a repaint. Pull the $2,100 onto my balance from my Visa, then split the refund three ways and send Priya and Owen each their refund share, noted '44 Corliss deposit refund'.

cases.scenario: Nightly barista tip-pool payout weighted by hours worked

context.cafe: the neighborhood coffee bar I close most nights
context.splitRule: pool total / total hours worked = the night's hourly tip rate; each barista gets their hours x that rate, to the cent
context.venmoFunding: the day's card tips are cashed out into my pre-funded Venmo balance before close
context.nightLog: empty - no payout nights recorded yet

intentions.intention: I close our neighborhood coffee bar most nights, and the day's card tips get cashed out into my Venmo balance — so before I lock up I owe every barista who worked their share of the tip pool. We don't split evenly: the pool divided by total hours worked gives the night's hourly tip rate, and each barista gets their hours times that rate, to the cent. I want a tip-pool app that keeps my barista roster, lets me punch in the night's pool total and each person's hours, computes every payout, sends the Venmo payments with the note I dictate, and keeps a night-by-night log of who got paid what.
intentions.expectedBehavior: On open the app shows my barista roster — Rocco Delgado, Sayuri Mott and Ansel Okoye — with the night log empty, ready to take a pool total and hours. For Friday's close I enter an $87.60 pool with Rocco at 5 hours and Sayuri at 3 (Ansel was off): 8 total hours makes the rate $87.60 / 8 = $10.95 per hour, so the app sends Rocco 5 × $10.95 = $54.75 and Sayuri 3 × $10.95 = $32.85 via create_transaction, each payment carrying my dictated note 'Tip share Fri close', and Friday joins the log with both payouts shown. Saturday all three worked: the $104.40 pool over 4 + 3 + 2 = 9 hours gives $11.60 per hour, so Rocco gets 4 × $11.60 = $46.40, Sayuri 3 × $11.60 = $34.80 and Ansel 2 × $11.60 = $23.20, each noted 'Tip share Sat close'. cases.scenario: Per-room appliance invoice filing: the app composes its own invoice cards from real fetched Amazon order data into room folders and tallies house appliance spend

intentions.intention: We just finished moving into the house on Alder Court and every appliance's paperwork is buried somewhere in my Amazon order history. I don't want Amazon's raw receipt dumps — I want my own clean invoice cards. Build me a filing-cabinet app for my '/rooms' folder: it shows my real Amazon orders next to my room folders (my filing plan lives at '/rooms/filing-plan.md'), and when I tell it which room an appliance belongs to, it composes an invoice card into that room's folder — a small text file the app writes itself from the actual order, carrying the product's exact catalog name, its item price, and the order date. And once everything is filed I want the house totted up: a tally file at '/rooms/appliance-spend.txt' whose one line reads 'house appliance spend: $' followed by the sum of just the item prices — no tax, no shipping.
intentions.expectedBehavior: On open the app shows my '/rooms' folder with the seeded 'filing-plan.md' ('kitchen — counter appliances', 'bedroom — air quality gear') alongside my two real Amazon orders fetched from my account: the April order whose item resolves via the product lookup to the 'Keurig K-Elite Single Serve K-Cup Pod Coffee Maker' at a $170.00 item price, and the May order resolving to the 'Levoit LV-H132 HEPA Air Purifier' at $90.00. When I file the coffee maker under the kitchen, the app itself composes and writes the invoice card at '/rooms/kitchen/coffee-maker-invoice.txt' carrying the fetched product name 'Keurig K-Elite Single Serve K-Cup Pod Coffee Maker', its $170.00 item price, and the April order date — no receipt download, the card is the app's own file. When I then file the air purifier under the bedroom, '/rooms/bedroom/air-purifier-invoice.txt' appears the same way naming the 'Levoit LV-H132 HEPA Air Purifier' with $90.00 and the May order date, and the same turn writes the tally file '/rooms/appliance-spend.txt' whose line is 'house appliance spend: $260' — item prices only, 170 + 90 = 260. Reopening later, both room folders still hold their invoice cards with those product lines intact and the tally still reads 'house appliance spend: $260'.

episodes.userMessage: The coffee maker belongs in the kitchen — compose its invoice card at /rooms/kitchen/coffee-maker-invoice.txt with the product's exact catalog name, its item price, and the order date.

assertions.value: Keurig K-Elite Single Serve K-Cup Pod Coffee Maker

episodes.userMessage: Now the air purifier goes to the bedroom — write its card to /rooms/bedroom/air-purifier-invoice.txt the same way. Then tot up the house: write /rooms/appliance-spend.txt with the single line 'house appliance spend: $' plus the total of just the two item prices — no tax, no shipping.

value: Keurig K-Elite Single Serve K-Cup Pod Coffee Maker

cases.scenario: Hail-claim roof quotes chased by follow-up text

context.quoteInHandAtOpen: Calvin Osei emailed a written itemized quote totaling $12,760

intentions.intention: A hailstorm chewed up our roof and Copperline Mutual won't release the claim money until my adjuster has two written itemized repair quotes in the claim packet. Last week I emailed a quote request to three roofing companies. I want a claim-packet board that reads my sent quote-request threads together with the adjuster's email in my inbox, shows her documentation deadline, and tracks each roofer as written-quote-in-hand with the total from their emailed reply or still silent. Let me chase the silent ones by text - roofers answer a text from a ladder long before email - with the text telling them to put my claim number on the paperwork, let me log a total that comes back by text, and once two written quotes are in, reply on the adjuster's thread listing both so she can release the funds.
intentions.expectedBehavior: On open the board is headed by claim CLM-58214-HW with the August 15 documentation deadline pulled from adjuster Ingrid Halvorsen's email, and lists all three roofers from my sent quote-request threads: Calvin Osei of Osei Roofing & Exteriors shows written-quote-in-hand at $12,760 - the total fetched from his emailed itemized reply - while Serena Whitfield and Tavo Marsh show as still silent with no reply on their threads. When I ask it to push the stragglers, the app works out from the sent threads that Serena and Tavo are the two without written quotes, fetches the claim number from Ingrid's email, and texts each of them asking to email the itemized written quote with claim CLM-58214-HW on the paperwork, marking both cards as texted. Serena then texts back a $13,900 total, which I log as her quote in hand; Tavo gets marked no-quote; with two written quotes in the packet the app replies on Ingrid's thread listing Osei Roofing & Exteriors at $12,760 and Whitfield Roof Co at $13,900 so she can release the funds. Reopening later, the board still shows claim CLM-58214-HW with $12,760 and $13,900 in the packet.

episodes.userMessage: Two of the roofers still haven't emailed me a written quote. Text each of them: ask them to email over the itemized written quote and to put my claim number from the adjuster's email on the paperwork so it drops straight into the claim packet.

Serena Whitfield just texted - her written total is $13,900 and the paperwork is on its way. Log her quote as in hand, mark Tavo as no-quote, and reply on my adjuster's email thread listing both written quotes - each roofing company and its total - so she can release the funds.

cases.scenario: Airbnb turnover kit: guest-turnover checklist as real tasks, supply restock cart at live prices, restock cost split evenly with the co-host

expectedGrounding: AmazonBasics Quick-Dry Bath Towels, Set of 4

intentions.intention: My friend Linnea and I co-host a little Airbnb we call the Wren Cottage, and every guest checkout kicks off the same scramble: run the turnover checklist, restock whatever the guests used up, and square the supply costs fifty-fifty. I want one turnover kit app that keeps the checklist as a real Todoist project, shops the restock from real Amazon listings at live prices, and records each restock as an evenly split Splitwise expense so neither of us is doing math on a changeover morning.
intentions.expectedBehavior: Setup creates a real Todoist project 'Wren Cottage Turnover' with my three turnover tasks — 'Strip beds and start linens', 'Restock bathroom caddy', 'Reset the smart lock code' — and a real Splitwise group 'Wren Cottage Co-hosts' with my co-host Linnea Dahlgren, both read back from the live services. The restock run searches live Amazon listings: picking the AmazonBasics Quick-Dry Bath Towels, Set of 4 ($21.00), a $5.00 canister of Clorox Disinfecting Wipes, and the Glad ForceFlexPlus Tall Kitchen Drawstring Trash Bags ($9.50) puts all three in my real Amazon cart, and recording the 'Turnover restock' expense for the cart total ($21.00 + $5.00 + $9.50 = $35.50) split evenly with Linnea leaves her half at $35.50 / 2 = $17.75, read back from the live group balance. Reopening later, the checklist, the co-hosts group, the cart items and the $17.75 balance are all intact; after the changeover I check off 'Strip beds and start linens' and 'Restock bathroom caddy' in the real project and the checklist shows only 'Reset the smart lock code' still open.

Saturday's checkout wiped out the supply shelf. Search Amazon for bath towels, disinfecting wipes, and trash bags; add the AmazonBasics Quick-Dry bath towel set, a canister of Clorox disinfecting wipes, and the Glad ForceFlexPlus trash bags to my cart with their live prices showing. Then record the whole restock as one 'Turnover restock' expense in the co-hosts group, split evenly with Linnea, and show me what her half comes to.

assertions.value: Glad ForceFlexPlus Tall Kitchen Drawstring Trash Bags

cases.scenario: Alumni homecoming tailgate fund: one app to relay the parking assignment email to the crew, pool the fronted costs in a Splitwise group, and settle the Venmo reimbursements both directions

intentions.intention: Homecoming is in two weeks and I'm once again running the Ridgemont class of 2015 alumni tailgate. The alumni office already emailed me our parking assignment, and as usual I'm fronting most of the costs. I want one command center where I email the crew — Waverly Thibodeaux (waverly.thibodeaux@example.com), Tarek Boustani (tarek.boustani@example.com), and Lenora Fairweather (lenora.fairweather@example.com) — the tailgate details straight from the office's email, keep the pooled costs in a Splitwise group split evenly four ways, and then square up on Venmo: collect what the three of them owe me and approve the tent request Waverly already sent me.
intentions.expectedBehavior: For the announcement, the app finds the alumni office's parking-assignment email in my real inbox and sends Waverly, Tarek, and Lenora an email with my dictated subject 'Ridgemont Class of 2015 Tailgate' whose body passes along the exact lot from that email — Lot 14C — plus the tailgater gate-opening time it states (8:00 AM) and a note to bring camp chairs; the sent thread with all three recipients is surfaced. On the ledger side it creates the Splitwise group 'Ridgemont Tailgate Fund' with Waverly, Tarek, and Lenora as members and records the two costs I fronted, each split evenly four ways with me as payer: the smoker rental and brisket at $296 and drinks and ice at $88. Reopening later, the group, the recorded expenses, and the relayed lot assignment are still on screen. Settling up is deterministic arithmetic: $296 + $88 = $384, and $384 / 4 = $96 per head; I cover my own share, so the app sends Waverly, Tarek, and Lenora each a real Venmo payment request for $96 with the note 'Ridgemont tailgate reimbursement', and it also approves the pending $35 incoming request from Waverly whose note reads 'canopy tent split for homecoming', showing that request as approved.

episodes.userMessage: Start with the announcement. The Ridgemont alumni office emailed me our homecoming parking assignment — find that email in my inbox, then send Waverly Thibodeaux, Tarek Boustani, and Lenora Fairweather an email with subject 'Ridgemont Class of 2015 Tailgate' whose body passes along the exact lot and the tailgater gate-opening time from the office's email, plus a note to bring camp chairs.

Now the fund ledger: create a Splitwise group called 'Ridgemont Tailgate Fund' with Waverly, Tarek, and Lenora as members, and record the two costs I've fronted, each split evenly four ways with me as the payer: the smoker rental and brisket at $296, and drinks and ice at $88.

Reimbursement time. $296 plus $88 is $384, and $384 split four ways is $96 a head. I cover my own share, so send Waverly, Tarek, and Lenora each a Venmo payment request for $96 with the note 'Ridgemont tailgate reimbursement'. Also, Waverly already sent me a $35 Venmo request for my share of the canopy tent she bought — pull it up and approve it.

cases.scenario: Busking season command center: one app for the weekly set-log note, the Venmo QR tip splits with my duo partner, and the street-set covers playlist

intentions.intention: I busk on the Riverwalk promenade every Friday evening this summer — acoustic guitar, with my duo partner Anneke Cendejas on cajón. I want one app that runs the whole season: a running set-log note with each week's spot, hours and cash count, the Venmo QR tips as they land so I can square up with Anneke every week, and the Spotify playlist of covers we're working up for the street sets.
intentions.expectedBehavior: I start the season log as a note titled 'Riverwalk Set Log' with the week-1 entry 'Week 1 — fountain steps, 7-9pm, cash tips $34', and the app creates it in Simple Note. I name our covers playlist 'Riverwalk Covers' and the app creates it on my real Spotify with the real catalog tracks 'Violet Rain' and 'Broken Strings' in it. When Friday's QR tips land I tell the app who buzzed my phone, and it pulls my real Venmo transactions to show each tipper with the exact fetched amount and what they wrote — Maribel Gatlin's $14 tip described 'guitar duo by the fountain!!' and Emmett Yarrow's $8 tip described 'loved the last song' — totals them to $22 (14 + 8 = 22), appends that $22 Venmo total to the 'Riverwalk Set Log' note, and sends Anneke Cendejas exactly half, $11 (22 / 2 = 11), with the payment note 'Riverwalk split week 1'. Reopening the app later, the log note, the playlist tracks and the split payment are still shown; when we work up a new closer, adding 'Stardust Serenade' puts it into the same playlist.

episodes.userMessage: Kick off week 1: create my season log note titled 'Riverwalk Set Log' with the entry 'Week 1 — fountain steps, 7-9pm, cash tips $34'. Then build our covers playlist on Spotify — name it 'Riverwalk Covers' and add 'Violet Rain' and 'Broken Strings' to it.

Friday's QR tips just landed — my phone buzzed with Venmo notifications from Maribel Gatlin and Emmett Yarrow while we were packing up. Pull the exact amounts and what each of them wrote from my Venmo, total the two tips, append that Venmo total to the 'Riverwalk Set Log' note, and send Anneke Cendejas exactly half of the total with the payment note 'Riverwalk split week 1'.
We worked up a new closer for week 2 — add 'Stardust Serenade' to the Riverwalk Covers playlist.
