cases.scenario: Community raffle desk: assemble the spa prize basket from live Amazon listings, thank the donors who emailed pledges, and chase ticket money over Venmo

expectedGrounding: Bath & Body Works Eucalyptus Spearmint Candle
AmazonBasics Luxury Spa Bath Towels, Set of 2

intentions.intention: I'm running the prize raffle for the Maplewood Elementary Spring Fair and the whole thing is scattered across three apps. I want one raffle desk that assembles the spa prize basket from real Amazon listings with a running cost total, pulls the donation pledge emails neighbors keep sending me out of my inbox so I can thank each donor and confirm their amount, and collects the ticket money by sending Venmo requests to the neighbors who bought tickets from me.
intentions.expectedBehavior: I ask for a wicker picnic basket, a eucalyptus candle, and the AmazonBasics spa bath towels; the app fetches the real listings, Crate & Barrel Wicker Picnic Basket ($50.00), Bath & Body Works Eucalyptus Spearmint Candle ($25.00), and AmazonBasics Luxury Spa Bath Towels, Set of 2 ($30.00), adds all three to my real Amazon cart, and shows the $105 basket total (50.00 + 25.00 + 30.00 = 105.00). Next it digs the donors' pledge emails out of my Gmail inbox and puts each amount beside the donor's name, a $20 pledge from Marjorie Tovar and a $12 pledge from Desmond Ikande (figures that appear only inside their emails, $32 pledged in all), and replies to both thanking them and confirming their amount. Reopening later, the three cart items, the $105 basket total, and Marjorie's $20 pledge are still on the board. Finally the ticket money: Kendra Boyle took 3 tickets and Jerome Ferrell took 2 at $5 each, so over Venmo the app sends a $15 ticket request to Kendra Boyle (3 x 5 = 15) and a $10 ticket request to Jerome Ferrell (2 x 5 = 10), each carrying the note 'Spring Fair raffle tickets', and both sent requests show on the board.

episodes.userMessage: Start the prize basket: find a wicker picnic basket, a eucalyptus candle, and the AmazonBasics spa bath towels on Amazon, add all three to my cart, and show me the running basket total.

assertions.value: Bath & Body Works Eucalyptus Spearmint Candle

episodes.userMessage: Now the donors: Marjorie Tovar and Desmond Ikande both emailed me pledges for the basket fund. Pull their pledge emails from my inbox, show each pledge amount next to the donor's name, and reply to both thanking them and confirming the amount they pledged.

Ticket money time: Kendra Boyle bought 3 raffle tickets and Jerome Ferrell bought 2, and tickets are $5 each. Send each of them a Venmo payment request for what they owe with the note 'Spring Fair raffle tickets'.

assertions.value: a $15 ticket request to Kendra Boyle
a $10 ticket request to Jerome Ferrell

cases.scenario: Immigration paperwork desk: the law firm's evidence checklist read from the inbox, anonymous form scans sorted into a named packet folder with the missing items flagged, a growing green-card timeline note, and replies to the paralegal from one desk

expectedGrounding: Two years of federal tax transcripts
Form I-864 Affidavit of Support signed by your sponsor
I-485 interview evidence checklist — case ALB-2419

intentions.intention: My marriage-based green card case is drowning me in paper. Our attorney Rosa Alvarez and her paralegal Marcus Tran at Alvarez & Boone email me checklists and notices, my scanner dumps every form into /scans under names like scan-0141.pdf, and the only place the whole saga makes sense is my 'Green card timeline' note. I want one paperwork desk for all of it: it should surface the firm's emails from my inbox, read my anonymous scans and sort them into a proper case packet folder with real names, hold the packet up against Marcus's evidence checklist and tell me exactly which items are still missing in his own wording, keep the timeline note growing as notices arrive, and let me reply to the firm right from the desk.
intentions.expectedBehavior: On open the desk shows the two Alvarez & Boone emails it found in my inbox — Marcus Tran's 'I-485 interview evidence checklist — case ALB-2419' and Rosa Alvarez's 'Interview notice arrived' — beside the three anonymous scans sitting in /scans (scan-0141.pdf, scan-0142.pdf, scan-0143.pdf) and my 'Green card timeline' note ending at the May 29 biometrics entry. When I say to build the packet, the app reads each scan to identify it, creates /immigration/alb-2419-packet, and moves the scans in under the names I dictate (birth-certificate-translated.pdf, passport-stamp-pages.pdf, marriage-certificate.pdf); holding the packet against Marcus's checklist of five items, 5 required minus 3 scanned = 2 outstanding, and it lists exactly 'Two years of federal tax transcripts' and 'Form I-864 Affidavit of Support signed by your sponsor' in his wording. When the interview notice lands I have it append two entries to the timeline note: one pulled from Rosa's email keeping her exact wording — the interview is September 18 at 8:30 AM at the Fairview Field Office — and my dictated 'Jul 26 — evidence packet assembled; tax transcripts and I-864 still outstanding.' Reopening later, the packet still holds passport-stamp-pages.pdf inside alb-2419-packet, the checklist still flags 'Two years of federal tax transcripts' as missing, and the timeline still shows the Fairview Field Office entry. Finally I reply to Marcus's checklist email with my exact sentence: the desk has to locate his thread in the inbox to reply to it, and it shows the sent reply addressed to Marcus Tran under the thread's own subject, 'I-485 interview evidence checklist — case ALB-2419'.

episodes.userMessage: Marcus's checklist is in — build the packet. Create /immigration/alb-2419-packet, figure out what each scan in /scans actually is, and move them in renamed: the birth certificate scan as birth-certificate-translated.pdf, the passport pages as passport-stamp-pages.pdf, and the marriage certificate as marriage-certificate.pdf. Then hold the packet up against Marcus's checklist and show me exactly which items are still missing, in his wording.

assertions.value: Two years of federal tax transcripts
Form I-864 Affidavit of Support signed by your sponsor

episodes.userMessage: The interview notice landed — Rosa emailed the details. Append two entries to my 'Green card timeline' note: first the interview date, time, and office pulled from Rosa's email, keeping her exact wording for those details, and then this line from me: 'Jul 26 — evidence packet assembled; tax transcripts and I-864 still outstanding.'

assertions.value: tax transcripts and I-864 still outstanding
Two years of federal tax transcripts

episodes.userMessage: Reply to Marcus Tran's checklist email with exactly this: 'Birth certificate, passport pages, and marriage certificate are scanned into the packet; the tax transcripts and signed I-864 will reach you before August 14.'

assertions.value: I-485 interview evidence checklist — case ALB-2419
the tax transcripts and signed I-864 will reach you before August 14

intentions.intention: Three of us own the lake house at Larchmere in the proportions we paid for it — I put up half, so I hold 50 percent, Tove Brandvold (tove.brandvold@example.com) holds 30, and Marcel Duval (marcel.duval@example.com) holds 20 — and our operating agreement says every shared cost splits by ownership stake, never evenly. Each May they both email me their walkthrough list of what winter broke, and I'm the one who drives up, hires the repairs, and fronts the money. I want one syndicate desk that turns their damage-report emails into a real task board, puts the invoices I front onto a Splitwise ledger split by our stakes, records each owner's reimbursement against their computed share when the money lands, and lets me answer their walkthrough threads without leaving the desk.
intentions.expectedBehavior: Submitting pulls the two walkthrough emails my co-owners sent me and creates the Todoist project 'Larchmere Damage List' with one task per flagged problem, each titled with the broken item exactly as their email names it — the 'boathouse door latch' and the porch 'gutter section' from Tove's email, the 'dock ladder' and the 'flag halyard' from Marcel's, 2 + 2 = 4 tasks; none of those items appear in anything I typed, so the app must read the mail to produce them. The ledger turn creates the real Splitwise group 'Larchmere Lake House' with Tove Brandvold and Marcel Duval as members and records the $620 Hemlock Exteriors invoice I fronted, split by ownership stake with me as payer — deterministic arithmetic the app must do itself because I only ever state the total and the percentages: Tove's share is 30% of $620 = $186 and Marcel's is 20% of $620 = $124, so the group shows Tove owing me $186 and Marcel owing me $124 while my 50% ($310) stays on me. Reopening later, the group, both stake-computed balances, and the extracted task board are still on screen. In the followup Marcel's transfer for his whole share arrives, so the app records a payment of $124 from Marcel to me (again computed as 20% of $620 — I never say the number), leaving Tove's $186 as the only open balance; it also marks the dock ladder task completed and sends a real reply on Tove's walkthrough thread telling her Hemlock is booked for the gutter on Saturday the 9th.

Now the ledger. Create a Splitwise group called 'Larchmere Lake House' with Tove and Marcel, and record the invoice I just paid Hemlock Exteriors for the gutter and latch work: $620 total, me as payer, split by our ownership stakes — I hold 50 percent, Tove holds 30, Marcel holds 20. Show me what each of them owes on their stake.

Three things. Marcel's transfer for his whole share of the Hemlock invoice hit my account this morning — record that payment from him in the group so his side reads settled. I fixed the dock ladder myself over the weekend, so mark that task completed. And reply on Tove's walkthrough thread to tell her Hemlock is booked for the gutter on Saturday the 9th.

cases.scenario: Chess marathon training camp: coach's weekly text becomes the session checklist, a prep-notes journal grows after key sessions, and the week closes with a puzzle-count wrap-up text back to coach

intentions.intention: I'm in a 16-week build for the Harborline Chess Marathon — an all-day open my club runs — and my coach Dara Okonjo texts me each week's training sessions. I want one training-camp app that turns her latest text into that week's session checklist I can tick off, keeps my prep journal where I jot how the key sessions actually went, and when the week wraps totals my puzzle count off the board and texts her the wrap-up.
intentions.expectedBehavior: I ask the app to pull Coach Dara's week-1 text; it reads her seeded message and creates the board 'Harborline Chess Camp' with the four sessions exactly as she wrote them — 'Mon tactics 40 puzzles', 'Wed calculation 25 puzzles', 'Fri endgame 15 puzzles', 'Sun annotate 2 games' — as real Todoist tasks, and starts the note 'Harborline Prep Notes' opening with 'Week 1 — rapid games at 15+10'. After the key sessions I check off the tactics and endgame blocks and the app appends 'Wk1 tactics: 34/40, missed two forks' and 'Wk1 endgame: rook endings shaky, redo ladder drills' to the journal. Reopening later, the board, the coach-listed session titles and the journal lines are all still there. When the week wraps I check off the last two sessions and the app totals the puzzle count from the three puzzle-session titles (40 + 25 + 15 = 80) and texts Dara Okonjo 'Week 1 done: 80 puzzles, tactics 34/40.', which then shows in my sent messages.

episodes.userMessage: Coach Dara already texted me this week's training plan. Pull up her latest text and set up week 1: create my training board 'Harborline Chess Camp' with each of the four sessions she listed as its own task, titled exactly as she wrote them. And start my prep journal as a note titled 'Harborline Prep Notes' that opens with the line 'Week 1 — rapid games at 15+10'.

Tactics and endgame blocks are in the books. Check off 'Mon tactics 40 puzzles' and 'Fri endgame 15 puzzles' on the board, and append two lines to my prep journal: 'Wk1 tactics: 34/40, missed two forks' and 'Wk1 endgame: rook endings shaky, redo ladder drills'.

assertions.value: Wk1 endgame: rook endings shaky, redo ladder drills

episodes.userMessage: Week 1 is wrapped — the calculation set and the game annotations happened too, so check those last two off. Then total my puzzle count off the board — the tactics, calculation and endgame sessions add up 40 + 25 + 15 — and text Coach Dara exactly: 'Week 1 done: 80 puzzles, tactics 34/40.'

cases.scenario: One-room massage practice front desk: per-client session logs, the treatment-room calm playlist from real catalog tracks, and client emails (soreness follow-up replies, schedule notices) in one app

intentions.intention: I run a one-room massage therapy practice out of the converted shed behind my house, and I want one front-desk app where each client's session log lives as a real Simple Note I append after every appointment, the treatment-room calm playlist is built from actual catalog recordings on my Spotify, and the client emails - soreness follow-up replies and schedule notices - go out through my real Gmail without me leaving the app.
intentions.expectedBehavior: I start session logs for my two regulars - 'Dario Ferreira - Session Log' with 'Session 1: right trapezius knot released, neck rotation still limited' and 'Maeve Lindqvist - Session Log' with 'Session 1: lower back tight, assigned nightly hamstring stretches' - and both are created as real Simple Note notes the app displays. In the same submit the app builds the playlist 'Treatment Room Calm' in my real Spotify and shows the two catalog tracks I named, 'The Maze of Forgotten Whispers' and 'Veiled Sorrow'. When I say Dario emailed me about how sore he is after his last session, the app finds his inbox thread 'Checking in after Tuesday's deep tissue' and replies with my dictated line 'Some soreness for 48 hours after deep tissue work is normal - drink extra water and put a warm compress on the trapezius tonight.', then appends 'Session 2: post-session soreness reported, advised warm compress and hydration' to Dario's session log. Reopening the app later, the playlist with both tracks, Dario's session log and its Session 2 line are all still shown. For the repaint week I have it email Maeve Lindqvist under the subject 'Treatment room repaint - your Tuesday 3 pm moves to Thursday' (the room is being repainted, her Tuesday 3 pm slot moves to Thursday at the same time).

episodes.userMessage: Start session logs for my two regulars: one titled 'Dario Ferreira - Session Log' with content 'Session 1: right trapezius knot released, neck rotation still limited', and one titled 'Maeve Lindqvist - Session Log' with content 'Session 1: lower back tight, assigned nightly hamstring stretches'. Then build my treatment-room playlist 'Treatment Room Calm' on my Spotify with the catalog tracks 'The Maze of Forgotten Whispers' and 'Veiled Sorrow'.

Dario Ferreira emailed me about how sore he is after his last session - find that email and reply with exactly: 'Some soreness for 48 hours after deep tissue work is normal - drink extra water and put a warm compress on the trapezius tonight.' Then append to Dario's session log: 'Session 2: post-session soreness reported, advised warm compress and hydration'.

assertions.value: Checking in after Tuesday's deep tissue

episodes.userMessage: The treatment room gets repainted next week: email Maeve Lindqvist with the subject 'Treatment room repaint - your Tuesday 3 pm moves to Thursday' letting her know the room is being repainted and her Tuesday 3 pm slot moves to Thursday at the same time.

assertions.value: Treatment room repaint - your Tuesday 3 pm moves to Thursday

cases.scenario: Family reunion weekend treasury: one app to email the branch-head invites, ledger the fronted costs by headcount (not evenly) in a Splitwise group, credit an early Venmo chip-in as a Splitwise payment, and collect the two different remaining balances

intentions.intention: Our Vega family reunion weekend is finally happening and I'm the one holding the money. Three branches are coming and they are not the same size: my cousin Marisol Vega (marisol.vega@example.com) is bringing her crew of four, my cousin Ruben Vega (ruben.vega@example.com) is bringing three, and my branch is just me and my dad — nine heads total. I want one command center where I email both branch heads the invite, ledger the costs I front in a Splitwise group with each branch's share worked out by headcount instead of a lazy even split, credit the early chip-in Marisol already Venmo'd me against her branch's tab, and then collect the two different remaining balances.
intentions.expectedBehavior: Sending the invite fires a real Gmail email to both cousins with my dictated subject 'Vega Family Reunion: Aug 15-17 at Cedar Hollow Park' and the app surfaces the sent thread with both recipients. On the treasury side it creates the Splitwise group 'Vega Reunion Weekend' with Marisol and Ruben as members and records the two costs I fronted with me as payer, split by headcount across nine attendees (Marisol's branch 4, Ruben's 3, mine 2) using the exact shares I dictate: the pavilion rental at $315 is $315 / 9 = $35 a head, so Marisol's branch $140, Ruben's $105, mine $70; the barbecue catering deposit at $414 is $414 / 9 = $46 a head, so Marisol $184, Ruben $138, me $92. Branch totals are deterministic: Marisol $140 + $184 = $324, Ruben $105 + $138 = $243, and my $162 is covered because I paid. Reopening later, the sent invite, the group, and both recorded expenses are still on screen. At collection time the app credits the $145 'Reunion early chip-in' Venmo transaction Marisol already sent me (seeded in my Venmo history) by recording a $145 payment from Marisol in the Splitwise group, leaving her $324 - $145 = $179, then creates two Venmo payment requests with the note 'Vega reunion balance' — $179 to Marisol and $243 to Ruben — and shows both pending.

episodes.userMessage: First the invites: email my cousins Marisol Vega and Ruben Vega the reunion invite. Subject 'Vega Family Reunion: Aug 15-17 at Cedar Hollow Park', and in the body tell them the pavilion is booked for the whole weekend, that costs get split by headcount this year, and to bring folding chairs.

Now the treasury: create a Splitwise group called 'Vega Reunion Weekend' with Marisol and Ruben as members, and record the two costs I fronted with me as payer, split by headcount — nine heads total: Marisol's branch is four, Ruben's is three, mine is two. The pavilion rental was $315, which is $35 a head: put Marisol's branch down for $140, Ruben's for $105, and mine for $70. The barbecue catering deposit was $414, which is $46 a head: Marisol $184, Ruben $138, me $92.

Time to collect, and Marisol gets credit: back in early May she Venmo'd me $145 as 'Reunion early chip-in' — it's in my Venmo history. Record that $145 in the Splitwise group as a payment from Marisol. Her branch total is $140 plus $184 = $324, minus the $145 leaves $179; Ruben's is $105 plus $138 = $243. So send Marisol a Venmo payment request for $179 and Ruben one for $243, both with the note 'Vega reunion balance'.

cases.scenario: Airport ride crew desk: curb-time texts to the riders, fronted van costs split three ways on Splitwise, and cash/Venmo settlements

intentions.intention: Every few weeks the three of us catch the same dawn flight rotation, and I'm always the one who books the XL van to the airport and fronts the money. I want one app that runs my airport ride crew: it texts Priya Nair and Owen Blake their exact curb pickup times, keeps every cost I front in a Splitwise group split evenly three ways with a running total of what the crew owes me, and settles people up either way they pay — recording a Splitwise payment when someone hands me cash, or firing off a Venmo request with a note when they still owe.
intentions.expectedBehavior: On open the ride-crew desk is ready with Priya and Owen and the even three-way split, nothing logged yet. I log the $174 XL van booking I fronted: the app creates the 'Dawn Patrol Airport Run' Splitwise group with Priya Nair and Owen Blake, records the $174 fare split evenly — 174 / 3 = $58 a head — and shows the crew owing me 2 × 58 = $116. Next I send the curb texts — Priya gets 'Van at your curb 4:10 AM — Dawn Patrol airport run, Terminal B, flight 6:05.' and Owen the same message with 4:25 AM — and log the $12 airport tolls, 12 / 3 = $4 a head, so each rider sits at 58 + 4 = $62 and the crew total owed to me is 2 × 62 = $124; the app shows both sent texts and the updated ledger. Reopening later, the group, the Terminal B curb texts and the $124 owed are still on screen. After the run I log the $9 short-term parking I paid at the terminal, split three ways — 9 / 3 = $3 a head — so each rider's share climbs to 62 + 3 = $65. Owen hands me his full $65 in cash and I record his payment in the Splitwise group; Priya still owes, so the app sends her a Venmo request for her full 62 + 3 = $65 outstanding with the note 'Dawn Patrol airport share', leaving Priya's $65 as the only open balance.

episodes.userMessage: I fronted the $174 XL van booking for Friday's dawn airport run. Set up the 'Dawn Patrol Airport Run' Splitwise group with Priya Nair and Owen Blake and record the $174 van fare split evenly three ways, so I can see what the crew owes me.

Send the curb times now. To Priya: 'Van at your curb 4:10 AM — Dawn Patrol airport run, Terminal B, flight 6:05.' To Owen: 'Van at your curb 4:25 AM — Dawn Patrol airport run, Terminal B, flight 6:05.' And log the $12 airport tolls I paid — split evenly three ways like everything else.

Run's done — two things. First, log the $9 short-term parking I paid at the terminal, split evenly three ways like everything else. Then settle up: Owen just handed me his full share in cash, so record his payment in the Splitwise group so he's square, and Priya still owes, so send her a Venmo request for her full outstanding balance with the note 'Dawn Patrol airport share'.

cases.scenario: Stained-glass commission workbench: design notes carry each client's glass specs, pattern files live in per-commission folders grown from a reusable template library, and Venmo deposit requests are computed as a quarter of the quote — bumped when the design changes and closed out with the remaining balance

intentions.intention: I build stained-glass panels on commission out of my garage studio, and I want one workbench app that runs each commission end to end. The design note holds the client's glass colors and cut specs, the pattern files live in a per-commission folder that starts from one of my reusable templates in /glasswork/templates, and the money side rides on Venmo — I take a quarter of the quote up front as a deposit request (enough to cover the glass order), bump the request if the design changes the price, and bill the rest when the panel is soldered. Finished patterns get filed back into the templates library so I can sell the design again.
intentions.expectedBehavior: I take in Nora Hartwell's iris transom commission quoted at $380: the app saves the design note 'Iris Transom - Nora Hartwell' with her specs (amber cathedral background, moss-green leaves, 62 pieces), sets up the commission folder /glasswork/commissions/hartwell-iris-transom, looks in my /glasswork/templates library to find the transom grid template's exact file transom-grid-template.svg, copies it in as hartwell-iris-pattern-v1.svg, records in the note which template the pattern started from, and sends Nora a real Venmo deposit request for a quarter of the quote ($380 / 4 = $95). When Nora swaps the amber for hand-rolled cobalt the quote rises by $60 (new total $380 + $60 = $440): the app logs the change in her note, saves the revised cutting list as hartwell-iris-pattern-v2.svg, and updates her deposit request to a quarter of the new total ($440 / 4 = $110). Reopening the app later still shows the design note, the v2 pattern file and the $110 deposit request. When the panel ships, the app sends Nora the request for the remaining balance ($440 - $110 = $330), marks the note completed, and copies the finished pattern back into the library as hartwell-iris-template.svg.

episodes.userMessage: New commission: Nora Hartwell (nora.hartwell@example.com) wants an iris transom panel for over her front door — amber cathedral glass background, moss-green leaves, 62 pieces, quoted at $380. Nora called — she wants the background in hand-rolled cobalt instead of amber cathedral, which adds $60 to the quote. Log the change in her design note, save the revised cutting list into her commission folder as hartwell-iris-pattern-v2.svg noting the hand-rolled cobalt background and that the piece count goes from 62 to 74, and update her deposit request to a quarter of the new total.

The iris panel is soldered, puttied and ready for pickup. Send Nora the Venmo request for everything still owed on the commission after her deposit request, add a completed line to her design note, and copy the finished pattern back into /glasswork/templates as hartwell-iris-template.svg so I can sell the design again.

cases.scenario: Tutoring side-gig punch-card desk: confirmation texts to the parents carrying each family's prepaid pack balance, a running lesson log note per student, and the discounted Venmo renewal request the moment a four-session pack runs out

intentions.intention: I tutor high-school math on weekday evenings as a side gig: algebra with Priya Nair on Thursdays and geometry with Marcus Webb on Fridays, and everything runs through their parents, Anita Nair and Colin Webb. Nobody pays me per lesson — families prepay a four-session pack at $280, and a returning family gets $25 off the renewal pack. Right now Priya's family has 1 session left on their current pack and Marcus's family has a fresh pack with all 4 left. I want one punch-card desk app where I text each parent the week's confirmed time along with their pack balance, punch a session off the right pack the moment it wraps, keep a running lesson log note per student, and fire off the discounted Venmo renewal request to the parent the instant a pack hits zero.
intentions.expectedBehavior: Anita Nair and Colin Webb are in my contacts with phone and Venmo. Submitting the week's schedule sends the two confirmation texts verbatim ('Confirmed: Priya Thursday 5:00 PM — 1 session left on her pack' to Anita, 'Confirmed: Marcus Friday 4:30 PM — 4 sessions left on his pack' to Colin) and shows the sent SMS records with each recipient's number — Anita's 5550107733 and Colin's 5550104412. After Priya's session I punch it off her pack (1 − 1 = 0), dictate her first lesson-log entry ('Covered quadratic factoring; homework p.214 #3-19 odd') into a new note for her, and because her pack just hit zero the app sends Anita the Venmo renewal request at the returning-family price: $280 − $25 = $255, shown as $255 with the request note 'Algebra pack renewal, 4 sessions'. Reopening the app later, both confirmation texts, Priya's quadratic-factoring log entry and the $255 renewal request are still shown. After Marcus's session the app punches his fresh pack down from 4 to 3 (4 − 1 = 3), starts his lesson log with 'Reviewed triangle congruence proofs; homework worksheet 12', and texts Colin the balance in the dictated form with the computed number filled in: 'Marcus pack: 3 sessions left'.

episodes.userMessage: Lock in this week's schedule and text the confirmations with pack balances: text Anita Nair 'Confirmed: Priya Thursday 5:00 PM — 1 session left on her pack' and text Colin Webb 'Confirmed: Marcus Friday 4:30 PM — 4 sessions left on his pack'.

Priya's session just wrapped — punch it off her pack and start her lesson log note with the entry 'Covered quadratic factoring; homework p.214 #3-19 odd'. That punch empties her pack, so send Anita the Venmo request for the renewal pack at the returning-family price, request note 'Algebra pack renewal, 4 sessions'.

Marcus's session just wrapped — punch one off his pack, start his lesson log note with 'Reviewed triangle congruence proofs; homework worksheet 12', and text Colin his new balance in exactly the form 'Marcus pack: N sessions left' with the right number filled in.

cases.scenario: Vinyl DJ collective HQ: reggae crate playlists from the live catalog, record-fund dues over Venmo, and the loft-gig prep board

intentions.intention: I spin records with two friends in a little vinyl DJ collective, and I want one HQ app where I build our monthly dig-list crates as real Spotify playlists, collect everyone's record-fund dues over Venmo, and run the prep board for our loft-party gigs as a task list.
intentions.expectedBehavior: Submitting builds the crate and the board: a real Spotify playlist 'Warehouse Crate Vol. 1' is created and searching the live catalog pulls the reggae tracks 'Neon Reverie' and 'Weeping Sky' into it, each rendered with its catalog length in the m:ss format I dictated — Neon Reverie is 206 seconds in the catalog, so 3:26, and Weeping Sky is 237 seconds, so 3:57; those lengths come from the fetched song records, not from anything I typed. The gig board becomes a real Todoist project 'Loft Party Gig' whose tasks 'Pack the 45s crate', 'Test the mixer' and 'Print set times' render as the checklist. On dues day the app sends real Venmo payment requests — $18 to Rico Delgado and $27 to Sana Iqbal, each noted 'record fund dues' — and the fund tab computes the requested total from the two live requests: $18 + $27 = $45.00, formatted to the cent as I asked (I never say the number). Reopening the app later, the crate tracks with their m:ss lengths (3:26 still on the crate list) and the two pending dues requests are still shown from live state. In the follow-up the app sends Rico Delgado a real reminder on his open $18 request and re-renders that request on the fund tab with its stored note 'record fund dues' read back from the live Venmo sent-requests list (the note is not in that message); it also adds the task 'Drop flyers at Vertigo Records' to the gig board and checks off 'Test the mixer'.

episodes.userMessage: Friday's loft party is on. Build this month's crate: create a Spotify playlist called 'Warehouse Crate Vol. 1' and pull the reggae tracks 'Neon Reverie' and 'Weeping Sky' from the catalog into it — and on the crate list, show each track's length as minutes:seconds, like 4:05. Then set up the gig board: a Todoist project 'Loft Party Gig' with tasks 'Pack the 45s crate', 'Test the mixer', and 'Print set times'.

Dues time for the record fund: send Venmo requests to Rico Delgado for $18 and Sana Iqbal for $27, both with the note 'record fund dues', and show me the fund tab total for everything requested, formatted to the cent.

Rico still hasn't paid — nudge him with a reminder on his $18 request, and show that reminded request on the fund tab with its stored note pulled straight from Venmo. Two gig-board updates too: add the task 'Drop flyers at Vertigo Records' and check off 'Test the mixer'.

expectedGrounding: Caught in the Afterglow of Love

intentions.intention: I lead a wedding band and the Iyer-Novak reception on October 18 is our big fall booking. The Tuesday run-throughs take care of themselves — it's the desk work around them that's scattered. I want one ops app where I settle the Riverbend Bridal Expo booth I fronted for myself, florist Wren Kowalski, and photographer Mateo Alvarez on Splitwise (my banner wall takes half the booth, so half the cost is mine and they each owe a quarter), where the dinner break set — the playlist that runs over the PA while the band eats — lives in my real Spotify even though I only ever half-remember titles and need the app to find the real ones, and where the booking paperwork (contract, deposit invoice, the venue's insurance certificate) sits as a Todoist board.
intentions.expectedBehavior: Submitting sets up the desk: it creates a real Splitwise group 'Riverbend Expo Booth' with Wren Kowalski and Mateo Alvarez and records the $486 booth fee I fronted split by floor share — half mine ($243.00), a quarter of the total each for Wren and Mateo ($486 / 4 = $121.50 owed to me by each of them, and the app shows that computed $121.50 per person), and it creates the playlist 'Iyer-Novak Dinner Break' in my real Spotify by resolving my half-remembered cues against the catalog: 'Silver Moon' resolves to 'Serenade of the Silver Moon' and 'Cherry Blossom' resolves to 'Cherry Blossom Tears' (I never say the full titles; the app must fetch them). When the caterer stretches dinner service, the app resolves two more cues — 'Afterglow' to 'Caught in the Afterglow of Love' and 'Moonlit' to 'Moonlit Sighs' — adds them to the playlist, and spins up the Todoist project 'Iyer-Novak Paperwork' with my dictated tasks 'Countersign the performance contract', 'Invoice the 50% deposit', and 'Email the liability COI to Larkspur Hall'. Reopening the app later, the group, the resolved break set, and the paperwork board are all still there. At expo wrap-up I record the $63 'Lead scanner rental' to the same group at the same shares ($63 / 4 = $15.75 more owed by each co-vendor, bringing each running total to $121.50 + $15.75 = $137.25, which the app shows), and it checks off 'Email the liability COI to Larkspur Hall'.

episodes.userMessage: Set up the vendor booth split first: create the Splitwise group 'Riverbend Expo Booth' with Wren Kowalski (wren.kowalski@example.com) and Mateo Alvarez (mateo.alvarez@example.com) and record the $486 booth fee I fronted — my banner wall takes half the booth so half is my share, and Wren and Mateo each owe a quarter of the total; show me the dollar amount each of them owes me. Then start the break-set playlist in my real Spotify: name it 'Iyer-Novak Dinner Break' and add the two tracks I can only half remember — the one with 'Silver Moon' in the title and the one with 'Cherry Blossom' in the title. Find the full titles in the catalog for me.

The caterer stretched dinner service to three courses, so the break set has to run longer — add two more from my half-memories: the one with 'Afterglow' in the title and the one with 'Moonlit' in the title. And open the booking paperwork board: create the Todoist project 'Iyer-Novak Paperwork' with tasks 'Countersign the performance contract', 'Invoice the 50% deposit', and 'Email the liability COI to Larkspur Hall'.

cases.scenario: Wedding reception audio command center: lock the Spotify music program from my fiancée's emailed dinner picks, email the DJ run-time cue sheets, and track run-of-show cue tasks

intentions.intention: Our wedding reception is Sept 12 and the music program just became my job. Our DJ Rosalind Beck emailed asking for one final cue sheet before Sept 5 — she cues everything off exact track lengths, so run times matter to her. My fiancée Priya Raman already emailed me her final three jazz dinner picks in play order under 'Dinner set picks — final'; the first dance and send-off are the two songs we settled on months ago. I want a reception audio command center where I lock the program as a real Spotify playlist (first dance, Priya's three-song dinner set, send-off), email Rosalind the cue sheet with the dinner set's total run time computed from the actual track lengths, and keep a Todoist run-of-show project of the sound cues I still owe the venue.
intentions.expectedBehavior: On open the app shows Rosalind's cue-sheet request and Priya's 'Dinner set picks — final' email, with no program locked yet since no playlist exists. When I lock the program, it reads the three dinner tracks out of Priya's email — 'Moonlit Sighs', 'Mystic Rhythms', 'Shadow Dance', titles I never typed into the app — and creates the Spotify playlist 'Reception Program — Sept 12' in my real account with the five tracks in show order: 'The Inescapable Gravity of Love' (first dance), the three dinner picks in Priya's order, and 'The Last Dance of Summer' (send-off) last. Next it emails Rosalind the cue sheet with subject 'Sept 12 reception — final cue sheet'; the dinner set total is computed from the real Spotify track lengths — 271 s + 219 s + 210 s = 700 s — so the body carries 'Dinner set total: 11 min 40 sec' in the exact template I dictated, and it creates the Todoist project 'Reception Run of Show' with my two cue tasks 'Confirm wireless mic for toasts by Sept 5' and 'Send venue the amplified-sound end time'. Reopening the app later, the playlist, its tracks, the run-of-show project and the mic task are all still shown. When the toasts force us to tighten dinner, the app removes 'Shadow Dance' from the playlist and emails Rosalind 'Sept 12 reception — revised cue sheet' with the recomputed total: 271 s + 219 s = 490 s, shown as 'Dinner set total: 8 min 10 sec'.

episodes.userMessage: Lock the program: create a Spotify playlist called 'Reception Program — Sept 12'. First our first dance 'The Inescapable Gravity of Love', then the three jazz dinner tracks exactly as Priya listed them in her 'Dinner set picks — final' email — pull them from that email, I'm not retyping them — and close with our send-off song 'The Last Dance of Summer'.

Now send Rosalind Beck the cue sheet she asked for: subject 'Sept 12 reception — final cue sheet', body listing the first dance, the dinner set in play order, and the send-off. Pull each dinner track's exact length from Spotify, add the three up, and write the sum as 'Dinner set total: M min S sec'. Also start a Todoist project 'Reception Run of Show' with two tasks: 'Confirm wireless mic for toasts by Sept 5' and 'Send venue the amplified-sound end time'.

assertions.value: Confirm wireless mic for toasts by Sept 5
Confirm wireless mic for toasts by Sept 5

episodes.userMessage: The toasts are running long, so we're tightening dinner: take the third dinner track, 'Shadow Dance', out of the playlist, then email Rosalind an updated cue sheet with subject 'Sept 12 reception — revised cue sheet' listing the two remaining dinner tracks and the recomputed 'Dinner set total: M min S sec'.

cases.scenario: Mowing-day route board: heads-up texts per stop, same-day Venmo collection per finished yard

intentions.intention: My weekend lawn-mowing side route is three yards in a fixed order: Doreen Falk at 14 Alder Court for a flat $45, then Gus Brubaker at 27 Birchwood Lane for $60, then Marisol Ybarra at 8 Cedar Loop for $35. Chasing money days after the grass is cut is the part I hate, so I want a mowing-day route board that keeps me paid the same day: one ordered card per stop showing the client's name, phone number, street address and flat rate pulled from my client list; when I'm rolling toward a stop I dictate a heads-up and the app texts it to that client for real; and the moment I say a yard is finished it sends that client a real Venmo payment request for their exact rate carrying the note I dictate, in the shape 'Mow day: <street address>'. Across the top keep a running header in exactly the shape 'Requested today: $X of $140' — it starts at 'Requested today: $0 of $140', since the full route is worth 45 + 60 + 35 = 140 dollars — so at a glance I always know how much of the day's cut I've already asked for.
intentions.expectedBehavior: On open the app lays out the route board in order — stop 1 Doreen Falk (5550671001) at 14 Alder Court for $45, stop 2 Gus Brubaker (5550671002) at 27 Birchwood Lane for $60, stop 3 Marisol Ybarra (5550671003) at 8 Cedar Loop for $35 — each card carrying the client's name, phone number, address and rate from my client list, with the header reading 'Requested today: $0 of $140' (45 + 60 + 35 = 140, nothing requested yet). When I roll out I dictate the stop-one heads-up and the app sends the exact text 'Mower's gassed up, I'm about 20 minutes out from 14 Alder Court' as a real SMS to Doreen's number 5550671001 (the number comes off her stop card, not out of my dictation), and her card flips to heads-up-sent. After the first two yards are cut I tell it to collect: it creates two real Venmo payment requests — $45 to Doreen Falk with the note 'Mow day: 14 Alder Court' and $60 to Gus Brubaker with the note 'Mow day: 27 Birchwood Lane' — and the header recomputes to 'Requested today: $105 of $140' (45 + 60 = 105), while Marisol's stop stays pending at $35. Reopening later, the board still shows the header 'Requested today: $105 of $140', the two sent requests with their notes including 'Mow day: 27 Birchwood Lane', and Marisol Ybarra still waiting as the one unmowed, unrequested stop.

episodes.userMessage: Rolling out to stop one. Text Doreen the heads-up: Mower's gassed up, I'm about 20 minutes out from 14 Alder Court

assertions.value: about 20 minutes out from 14 Alder Court

episodes.userMessage: Doreen's and Gus's yards are done. Send Doreen her $45 request with the note 'Mow day: 14 Alder Court' and Gus his $60 request with the note 'Mow day: 27 Birchwood Lane'. That should put the header at exactly 'Requested today: $105 of $140'.

cases.scenario: Daily sourdough starter feeding-ratio journal with rise notes and ratio math

priorEntries: Jul 22 — kept 20 g starter, fed 100 g flour + 100 g water. Rose to double in 6 h at 70°F, domed top.
Jul 23 — kept 20 g starter, fed 100 g flour + 100 g water. Doubled in 5 h at 72°F, lots of big bubbles.

intentions.intention: I keep a sourdough starter and want a plain feeding diary in one note — no reminders or schedules, just a running log where each day I record how much starter I kept, the flour and water I fed it, and how it rose. The one bit of work I want the app to do is the ratio math: I feed at a fixed starter:flour:water ratio, so when I tell it how much starter I kept, it should compute the flour and water for me and write the day's entry in the same style as the past days, including my rise note. If I change my feeding ratio I want it to redo the current day's amounts from the new ratio.
intentions.expectedBehavior: On open the app shows my feeding diary read from the saved note: the 1:5:5 (starter : flour : water) ratio and the two prior days — Jul 22 (kept 20 g starter, fed 100 g flour + 100 g water, doubled in 6 h) and Jul 23 (kept 20 g starter, fed 100 g flour + 100 g water, doubled in 5 h). When I submit today's feed with 30 g of starter kept, the app applies my ratio — 30 g × 5 = 150 g flour and 30 g × 5 = 150 g water — and appends today's entry in the same style as past days: kept 30 g starter, fed '150 g flour' + 150 g water, with my verbatim rise note 'doubled in 4.5 h at 75°F'. When I then switch to a slower 1:10:10 ratio with the same 30 g of starter kept, it redoes today's amounts from the new ratio — 30 g × 10 = 300 g flour and 30 g × 10 = 300 g water — so today's entry now reads '300 g flour' + 300 g water, and it records that I 'moved the jar to the basement'. Reopening later, the note still shows the '1:10:10' ratio on today's entry, the recomputed '300 g flour', and the 'moved the jar to the basement' note.

episodes.userMessage: Today's feed — I kept 30 g of starter this morning instead of my usual 20. Work out the flour and water from my 1:5:5 ratio and log today's entry the same way as the past days. Rise note: it doubled in 4.5 h at 75°F.

I'm switching to a slower 1:10:10 ratio so I can feed once a day — redo today's entry from that ratio with the same 30 g of starter kept. Also note that I moved the jar to the basement where it's cooler.

assertions.value: moved the jar to the basement

value: moved the jar to the basement

cases.scenario: Lake-house reunion prep checklist where checking off a money-gated task also records the shared cost

seededTasks: Book the pontoon boat for Saturday

moneyGates.task: Book the pontoon boat for Saturday

context.shareFormat: whole dollars with a dollar sign (e.g. $25)

intentions.intention: I'm the organizer for our three-person family reunion weekend at the Birchwater lake house, and every year the prep list and the money end up in two different places — the checklist gets done but nobody remembers who fronted what. My prep list already lives in my Todoist project 'Birchwater Lake Reunion Prep'. I want one trip-prep app that pulls that project in, and whenever a prep task involved somebody fronting money, checking it off should also record that cost split evenly three ways with Marit Solheim and Quentin Baptiste in a 'Cousins Cost Kitty' Splitwise group it sets up the first time money moves — so the morning we leave, the checklist is done and the who-owes-whom board is already exact. Plain prep tasks with no money attached just get checked off, and if I think of new prep later it should land in the same Todoist project. When I hand you a cost I'll give you the exact expense description to log, and I want shares shown as whole dollars with a dollar sign, like $25.
intentions.expectedBehavior: On open the app shows the 'Birchwater Lake Reunion Prep' project fetched from Todoist with its four open tasks — 'Reserve the Birchwater lake house', 'Book the pontoon boat for Saturday', 'Pack the screened-porch card games', 'Print the lake trail map' — and an empty cost board, since no Splitwise group exists yet. When I report the lake house booked with $474 on my card and tell the app to log it as '$474 Birchwater lake house', the app checks the lake-house task off in Todoist, creates the 'Cousins Cost Kitty' Splitwise group with Marit Solheim and Quentin Baptiste, and records the expense '$474 Birchwater lake house' split evenly three ways: 474 / 3 = $158 a head, so the board shows Marit and Quentin each owe me $158. When Marit covers the pontoon boat and I tell the app to log it as '$384 pontoon boat rental', the app checks the pontoon task off, records '$384 pontoon boat rental' paid by Marit split evenly three ways (384 / 3 = $128 a head), and re-reads the group balance so the board reflects the new even split — and it adds my new task 'Load the coolers Friday morning' to the same prep project. Reopening later, both expenses persist on the group — '$474 Birchwater lake house' is still on the board — and the coolers task is still open on the checklist alongside the untouched card-games and trail-map tasks.

episodes.userMessage: The Birchwater lake house is booked — $474 on my card. Check off the lake-house task, set up the Cousins Cost Kitty group with Marit Solheim and Quentin Baptiste, and log the expense as '$474 Birchwater lake house' split evenly three ways.

Marit covered the pontoon boat — check off the pontoon task, log the expense as '$384 pontoon boat rental' split evenly three ways with her as the payer, and show me the updated board. Also add one more prep task: Load the coolers Friday morning.

cases.scenario: Rec volleyball league fees split four ways in Splitwise, then collected with Venmo requests

context.team: Thursday Setters — co-ed rec volleyball, Thursday nights
context.splitRule: every fee I front splits evenly four ways (me + 3 teammates)

intentions.intention: I play on the Thursday Setters, our co-ed rec volleyball team, and the league bills everything to me — the whole fall registration went on my card and I'm the one handing the ref her cash after every match night. I want an app that keeps a 'Thursday Setters Fall Fees' Splitwise group with my three teammates Dario Quintero, Marisol Beltran, and Femi Adeyemi, where each fee I front gets logged and split evenly four ways, then fires a Venmo request at each teammate for their share with a note saying what it's for, and lets me tick shares off as teammates pay their requests — recording the payment in the group so the ledger and my Venmo stay in step — with a running number for what the team still owes me.
intentions.expectedBehavior: On open the app shows the fee collector ready with my three teammates and the even four-way split rule, nothing logged yet. I log the fall registration I fronted — $380, and 380 / 4 = $95 a head — and the app creates the 'Thursday Setters Fall Fees' Splitwise group with Dario Quintero, Marisol Beltran and Femi Adeyemi, records the $380 expense with each teammate owing $95, and sends each of the three a $95 Venmo request carrying the note 'Setters fall registration', so the team owes me 3 × 95 = $285. Next I log the referee fees for our first two matches — $34 a match, so 2 × 34 = $68, and 68 / 4 = $17 a head — which adds a second expense to the group plus three $17 Venmo requests with the note 'Setters ref fees matches 1-2', bringing what's owed to 285 + 3 × 17 = $336; I also record that Dario and Marisol paid their $95 registration requests, so with 2 × 95 = $190 in, the outstanding total reads 336 − 190 = $146, with Femi Adeyemi still owing both his shares. Reopening later, the group still holds both fee expenses and the sent requests, and the outstanding total still shows $146.

episodes.userMessage: Create the Thursday Setters Fall Fees group with Dario Quintero, Marisol Beltran, and Femi Adeyemi, and log the fall league registration I fronted — $380 split evenly four ways, so each of them owes me $95. Then send all three a $95 Venmo request with the note 'Setters fall registration' and show me the total the team owes me.

The refs for our first two match nights were $34 a match — log the $68 referee fee split the same four ways and send $17 Venmo requests to all three with the note 'Setters ref fees matches 1-2'. Also Dario and Marisol both paid their $95 registration requests, so record those two payments in the group and show me what's still outstanding.

cases.scenario: Thursday darts-league side-bet ledger: each night's leg bets in shorthand note lines, settled for real over Venmo on the first of the month

context.shorthand: plus = I owe that player, minus = that player owes me
context.seededRunningLine: Running: I owe Lachlan $31, Suki owes me $25
context.settleCadence: first of each month: pay out what I owe, request what I'm owed, stamp the ledger SETTLED

intentions.intention: Thursday nights I throw darts at the Rusty Anchor with my league crew, and every leg of cricket or 501 carries a small side bet — nobody settles at the board, it all rides. I keep one 'Darts Night Ledger' note where every night gets a line in my shorthand — plus means I owe that player, minus means they owe me, like 'Thu Apr 6: Lachlan +$22, Suki -$14' — and the note always ends with a 'Running:' line totting up where I stand with each player. I want an app for my crew — Lachlan Fenn and Suki Kolstad — that shows the ledger with those running totals, lets me dictate a new night's line after the last leg and rewrites the note with the Running line recomputed, and then on the first of each month does the settle-up for real over Venmo: pay out what I owe, request what I'm owed, and stamp the ledger settled so next month starts clean.
intentions.expectedBehavior: On open the app shows the 'Darts Night Ledger' note with the two April nights — 'Thu Apr 6: Lachlan +$22, Suki -$14' and 'Thu Apr 13: Lachlan +$9, Suki -$11' — and the running line 'Running: I owe Lachlan $31, Suki owes me $25'. When I log 'Thu Apr 20: Lachlan +$16, Suki -$7' the note is rewritten with that third night line appended and the Running line recomputed to I owe Lachlan $47 (22 + 9 + 16 = 47) and Suki owes me $32 (14 + 11 + 7 = 32). On May 1 I settle up: the app sends Lachlan Fenn a real $47 Venmo payment and Suki Kolstad a real $32 payment request, both carrying the note 'April darts settle-up', and stamps the ledger 'SETTLED May 1'. Reopening later, the 'Lachlan +$16' night line, the 'SETTLED May 1' stamp, and the pending $32 request to Suki are all still there.

episodes.userMessage: Last night's legs are in the books. Add this line to the ledger: Thu Apr 20: Lachlan +$16, Suki -$7 — and recompute the Running line.

It's the first of the month — settle-up day. Pay Lachlan Fenn the $47 I owe him and send Suki Kolstad a payment request for the $32 she owes me, both with the note 'April darts settle-up'. Then stamp the ledger: SETTLED May 1.

cases.scenario: Bike co-op shop-chore bounties paid to volunteer fixers on completion

openBounties: True the wobbly rear wheel on the blue cruiser — $8 bounty
Patch the flat on the cargo trike — $4 bounty
Degrease the loaner fleet drivetrains — $3 bounty

intentions.intention: I keep the repair bench at our neighborhood bike co-op, and our fixers Denny and Renata don't get a stipend — they earn job by job off the shop-chore bounty board taped over the workbench, and I want it living in an app. Every open shop chore is posted with its dollar bounty right in the title, and the shop rule is the money hits the fixer's Venmo the moment the job passes my bench check. Show me the board with every open bounty and its price, let me check a chore off and instantly pay whichever fixer did it exactly the posted bounty out of the co-op float I hold, let me post fresh bounties as busted bikes roll in, and keep a running payout tally per fixer plus what's left in the float.
intentions.expectedBehavior: On open the app shows my 'Shop Chore Bounty Board' Todoist project with three open bounties — 'True the wobbly rear wheel on the blue cruiser — $8 bounty', 'Patch the flat on the cargo trike — $4 bounty', and 'Degrease the loaner fleet drivetrains — $3 bounty' — my fixers Denny Okafor and Renata Voss, my $60 Venmo float, and $0 paid out so far. When Denny's wheel job passes my bench check, the app completes the 'True the wobbly rear wheel on the blue cruiser — $8 bounty' task and sends Denny Okafor exactly the $8 posted in that task's title (the amount is never in my message — it reads the price off the board), leaving my float at $60 − $8 = $52 and Denny's tally at $8. Then Renata clears the trike flat: the app completes 'Patch the flat on the cargo trike — $4 bounty' and pays Renata Voss its posted $4 (float $52 − $4 = $48; total paid out $8 + $4 = $12), and posts the new open task 'Replace the brake pads on the tandem — $6 bounty' on the board exactly as I dictated it. Reopening later, the board still shows 'Replace the brake pads on the tandem — $6 bounty' open, the wheel and trike-flat bounties checked off, and the payout ledger still lists the $8 payment to Denny Okafor and the $4 to Renata Voss.

episodes.userMessage: Denny just trued the wobbly rear wheel on the blue cruiser and it passed my bench check — check that shop chore off the board and Venmo him the posted bounty.

assertions.value: True the wobbly rear wheel on the blue cruiser — $8 bounty

episodes.userMessage: Renata patched the flat on the cargo trike, so check that one off and pay her its bounty too. Also post a new bounty on the board titled exactly: Replace the brake pads on the tandem — $6 bounty

assertions.value: Patch the flat on the cargo trike — $4 bounty
Replace the brake pads on the tandem — $6 bounty

value: Replace the brake pads on the tandem — $6 bounty

cases.scenario: Hot-sauce flight scorecards on a hottest-first board where a house heat record (punch x burn = HP) steps the user up one rung of the real First Alert/Kidde fire-extinguisher price-ladder staged in Amazon with a running hazard tally

context.heatFormula: heat points = punch (out of 10) x burn (minutes till the mouth goes quiet), written plain ASCII like 'punch 7 x burn 5 = 35 HP'
context.stoveRule: on a new house heat record, step one rung up the fire-extinguisher ladder (next model up by price from the last staged one; start from the owned First Alert Kitchen Fire Extinguisher), stage it in the Amazon cart (staged, never bought)
context.hazardTallyFormat: plain digits and a dot, no currency sign (e.g. 12.50)
expectedGrounding: First Alert Standard Home Fire Extinguisher

intentions.intention: I host hot-sauce flight nights and keep every bottle's card in my note 'Hot sauce flight scorecards': each pour gets punch (out of ten) times burn (how many minutes until my mouth goes quiet), so heat points = punch x burn, written plain ASCII like 'punch 7 x burn 5 = 35 HP', and the cards stay ranked hottest first. Then there's the stove rule, the one my roommates actually enforce: when a bottle breaks the house heat record, the flight table has officially outgrown its safety gear, so I step up exactly one rung on the fire-extinguisher ladder — the next model up by price from whichever one I last staged, starting from the First Alert Kitchen Fire Extinguisher already mounted by the stove — and stage it in my real Amazon cart, staged never bought because I do the checkout myself before the next flight night, and add its price to a running hazard tally written plain like 12.50 so it drops straight into the house budget sheet. When I card a flight it should append each bottle's line, re-rank the board, and if a bottle broke the record, stage the next extinguisher and bump the tally — and never lose the card history.
intentions.expectedBehavior: On open the app shows the 'Hot sauce flight scorecards' note fetched from my notes — the flight-card formula, the stove rule, and two ranked cards: Widow's Porch at punch 7 x burn 5 = 35 HP (the house record) above Smoke & Mirrors at 15 HP — with an empty Amazon cart and a hazard tally of 0.00. When I card the Garden Ghost at punch 4 x burn 2 = 8 HP (no record) and the Molten Cellar at punch 9 x burn 5 = 45 HP, both lines are appended and the board re-ranks with the Molten Cellar on top, and since 45 beats the old 35 record the stove rule fires exactly once: the app searches Amazon for fire extinguishers and stages the rung above the First Alert Kitchen Fire Extinguisher at 17.00 that I already own — the 'First Alert Standard Home Fire Extinguisher' at 20.00 (below the Kidde Pro 210 Fire Extinguisher at 48.00 and the First Alert Heavy Duty Fire Extinguisher at 50.00) — in my cart, putting the hazard tally at 20.00. Next I card the Kiln Door at punch 8 x burn 7 = 56 HP, a fresh record over the 45, so it steps one more rung up from the Standard Home and stages the 'Kidde Pro 210 Fire Extinguisher' at 48.00, so the hazard tally = 20.00 + 48.00 = 68.00. Reopening later, the note still carries the 8 HP, 45 HP and 56 HP cards, both extinguishers are still staged in the cart, and the hazard tally still reads 68.00.

episodes.userMessage: Flight night just wrapped — four bottles poured, two earned cards. First the Garden Ghost: punch 4, and the burn barely lasted 2 minutes. Then the Molten Cellar, a scorpion-pepper number: punch 9 with a full 5-minute burn. Card them both and re-rank the board. If one of them broke the house record, the stove rule kicks in — the little First Alert Kitchen extinguisher by the stove has officially met its match, so pull up fire extinguishers on Amazon, stage the next one up by price in my cart, and open the hazard tally.

assertions.value: First Alert Standard Home Fire Extinguisher

episodes.userMessage: One follow-up pour tonight, a single card: the Kiln Door, a fermented ghost-pepper bottle a coworker ferments himself. Punch 8, and the burn hung on for 7 minutes. Card it, tell me what tops the board now, and if the record fell again, step one more rung up the extinguisher ladder from the one already staged in my cart, stage that next model, and bump the hazard tally.

value: First Alert Standard Home Fire Extinguisher

cases.scenario: Anniversary reading program curated out of the typed heirloom courtship-letter archive

intentions.intention: My grandparents Harold and Bess turn seventy years married this September, and the courtship letters Harold mailed her were all typed up years ago by my cousin Marta — they live under /letters in folders by year, one file per letter. I got volunteered to build the reading program for the anniversary dinner, so I want an app that works out of that heirloom archive and keeps my picks in /anniversary-reading: each letter I choose gets copied in with an order-number prefix like 02-1949-06-19-front-porch.md, and program.md holds the numbered running order with who reads what. Family will veto picks, so when a letter gets pulled I need the app to delete its copy, copy in the replacement under the same slot number, and fix that line of the program. Whenever I open it, show me the program list and what's sitting in the reading folder so I always know where the lineup stands.
intentions.expectedBehavior: On open the app shows the /letters archive — /letters/1948 holding '1948-05-12-lakeside.md' and '1948-11-03-harvest-dance.md', /letters/1949 holding '1949-06-19-front-porch.md' — alongside /anniversary-reading, where program.md already lists '1. 1948-11-03-harvest-dance.md — read by Cousin Marta' and the copied pick '01-1948-11-03-harvest-dance.md' sits. When I pick the proposal letter for slot 2, the app copies /letters/1949/1949-06-19-front-porch.md into /anniversary-reading as '02-1949-06-19-front-porch.md', appends '2. 1949-06-19-front-porch.md — read by Grandpa Harold' to program.md, and pulls up the letter text from the archive, which contains Marta's typed line 'my voice failed the first time' (fetched from the stored file — I never dictate it). When Grandma Bess vetoes that pick, the app deletes '02-1949-06-19-front-porch.md', copies the lakeside letter in as '02-1948-05-12-lakeside.md', rewrites line 2 of program.md to '2. 1948-05-12-lakeside.md — read by Grandpa Harold', and shows the lakeside text containing the stored line 'flat as window glass'. Reopening later, program.md still carries the corrected line 2 and the reading folder still holds '02-1948-05-12-lakeside.md'.

episodes.userMessage: Slot 2 of the program is the proposal letter. Copy /letters/1949/1949-06-19-front-porch.md into /anniversary-reading as 02-1949-06-19-front-porch.md, add the line '2. 1949-06-19-front-porch.md — read by Grandpa Harold' to program.md, and pull up the letter text so I can proofread Marta's typing.

assertions.value: my voice failed the first time

episodes.userMessage: Grandma Bess vetoed the proposal letter — too tender to read to a full dining room. Delete 02-1949-06-19-front-porch.md from /anniversary-reading, copy /letters/1948/1948-05-12-lakeside.md in as 02-1948-05-12-lakeside.md to take slot 2, rewrite line 2 of program.md to '2. 1948-05-12-lakeside.md — read by Grandpa Harold', and show me the lakeside letter.

cases.scenario: Holiday craft-fair booth desk: Todoist prep checklist, Venmo requests for custom-order pickup totals, and ready-for-pickup texts from booth 14

intentions.intention: I throw pots all fall so I can sell at the Tinsel Trail Holiday Craft Fair, and this Saturday I've got booth 14 plus two custom pre-orders being picked up there. I want one booth desk app where my prep checklist lives as a real Todoist project, the pickup customers get Venmo requests for exactly what their pieces come to, and once an order is wrapped the customer gets a text that it's waiting at the booth.
intentions.expectedBehavior: I start the prep list and the app creates a real Todoist project named 'Tinsel Trail Booth' with the tasks 'Print price signs', 'Wrap Priya's mugs in tissue', and 'Pack the card table', all visible afterward. Then I enter the pickups: Priya Nair is taking two Snowdrift glaze mugs at $28 each, so the app computes 2 x $28 = $56 and sends her a real Venmo payment request for $56; Colin Marsh owes $42 for his family ornament set and gets a $42 request, and both requests show with the customer names. Reopening the app later still shows the project, its tasks, and the outstanding requests with their amounts. When I say both orders are wrapped, the app texts Priya and Colin my dictated pickup message about booth 14 and checks off the tissue-wrapping task, showing the sent texts and the completed task.

episodes.userMessage: Set up my prep checklist: create a Todoist project called 'Tinsel Trail Booth' with the tasks 'Print price signs', 'Wrap Priya's mugs in tissue', and 'Pack the card table'.
Now the pickup money: Priya Nair is taking two Snowdrift glaze mugs at $28 each, and Colin Marsh owes $42 for his family ornament set. Send each of them a Venmo request for their full total.

Both orders are wrapped. Text Priya and Colin the same message: 'Your order is wrapped and waiting at booth 14 - Tinsel Trail runs 9 to 3.' Then check off 'Wrap Priya's mugs in tissue' on my prep list.

cases.scenario: Film darkroom co-op hub: per-roll negative scan filing, a chemistry mix log note, and the monthly rent split in Splitwise

intentions.intention: Three of us co-rent a little film darkroom above the shoe-repair shop on Tallow Lane — me, Beata Wozniak, and Ilias Papadakis — and my side of it lives in three messy places: fresh negative scans pile up loose in my /negatives folder, my chemistry dilutions live on a paper card taped to the sink, and the rent ledger is a group-chat argument. I want one co-op hub app: it files each finished roll's scans into a per-roll folder I name, keeps my chemistry mixes as a real note I can append to, and runs the monthly rent split in a real Splitwise group with Beata and Ilias — show each member's share as whole dollars with a dollar sign, like $12.
intentions.expectedBehavior: On open the hub shows the three loose scans seeded in /negatives — roll18_frame04.tif, roll18_frame09.tif and roll19_frame02.tif — an empty chemistry log, and no rent group yet. Submitting files roll 18: the app creates the real directory /negatives/2026-07_roll18 and moves roll18_frame04.tif and roll18_frame09.tif into it (roll19_frame02.tif stays loose because that roll isn't finished), and creates the real note 'Chemistry Mix Log' whose first line is my dictated mix 'Duotol 1+1, 20C, 9 min — agitate first 30s, then 5s each minute'. In the revision the app creates the Splitwise group 'Tallow Lane Darkroom' with Beata Wozniak and Ilias Papadakis and records July's $255 studio rent as one expense titled 'July studio rent' split evenly three ways — 255 / 3 = $85 a head, so the who-owes board shows Beata and Ilias each owing me $85. Reopening later rebuilds everything from the real backends: the filed /negatives/2026-07_roll18 with both frames inside, the Chemistry Mix Log, and the Tallow Lane Darkroom group with both members. In the follow-up, roll 19 gets the same treatment — the app creates /negatives/2026-07_roll19 and moves roll19_frame02.tif into it — Beata's $85 cash payment for her rent share is recorded in the group, and the log gains my appended line 'fixer exhausted after roll 19, mix a fresh working batch next session'.

cases.scenario: Fellowship recommender wrangling: each professor's numbered asks hang as checklist sub-tasks under my own deadline tasks, a parked Gmail draft answers Elena's dissertation question only when I say send, Marcus's thread gets forwarded to her on request, and the packet folder is zipped for the portal upload

expectedGrounding: Your unofficial transcript from the registrar
Which chapter is the true spine of your dissertation
Aldercroft letter — timing and one requirement

intentions.intention: The Aldercroft Fellowship deadline is six weeks out and both of my recommenders answered on the same afternoon, each with homework for me: Elena numbered three things she needs and closed with a question about my dissertation; Marcus numbered two and warned that nothing moves until his field-station rotation ends. I keep losing the thread between their emails, my sticky-note deadlines, and my essay drafts in /fellowship/essays. I want a recommender-wrangling app: it should read both professors' emails and hang each of their numbered asks as a checklist sub-task under a deadline task I word myself — one parent task per professor, nothing scraped that I didn't ask for; it should let me park an answer to Elena's closing question as a Gmail draft that waits until I say send; it should keep a comment trail on a professor's task so future-me can see what past-me already handled; and on the last day it should ship everything at once — send the parked draft, forward Marcus's whole thread to Elena since she asked to see his plan, and zip my packet folder into one upload for the portal. Any file it touches, it touches only at paths I spell out.
intentions.expectedBehavior: On open the app shows the two recommender threads it found in my inbox — 'Your Aldercroft letter — my checklist and a question' from Elena Vasquez (vasquez@marlowecollege.edu) and 'Aldercroft letter — timing and one requirement' from Marcus Okafor (okafor@marlowecollege.edu) — alongside my files (/fellowship/essays holding research-statement-v4.md and personal-essay-v2.md, /fellowship/packet holding cv-aldercroft.md) and an empty tracker, since no Todoist project exists yet. On the first work turn the app moves /fellowship/essays/research-statement-v4.md to /fellowship/packet/research-statement.md, creates the Todoist project 'Aldercroft 2026' with exactly the two parent tasks I dictate — 'Elena's packet — everything to her by August 8' and 'Marcus's packet — everything to him by August 18' — and hangs one sub-task per numbered line of each professor's email in their exact words with the numbers dropped: under Elena, 'Your unofficial transcript from the registrar', 'The final title of your research statement', and 'A bulleted list of the results you want me to emphasize' (3 sub-tasks from her 6-line email, skipping her greeting line, her forward-me-Marcus's-thread request, and her closing question); under Marcus, 'The sediment core photo appendix, as one PDF' and 'Your camp dates for the fall field season' (2 sub-tasks from his 4-line email, skipping his agreement line and his rotation-timing line) — 2 parent tasks + 5 sub-tasks, where a literal per-newline split would instead hang 6 and 4. On the next turn the app surfaces Elena's exact closing question — 'Which chapter is the true spine of your dissertation — the sediment cores or the wetland surveys?', a line that exists only in her email — then parks my dictated answer as a Gmail draft to vasquez@marlowecollege.edu under the dictated Re: subject WITHOUT sending anything, and posts my dictated comment 'Answer parked as a Gmail draft on August 2 — send after transcript arrives.' on Elena's packet task. Reopening later, the 'Aldercroft 2026' board still shows both parent tasks with 'The sediment core photo appendix, as one PDF' still on Marcus's checklist, research-statement.md still sits in /fellowship/packet, and Elena's task still carries the parked-draft comment. On the final turn the app sends the waiting draft from Gmail's drafts (not a fresh compose), forwards Marcus's real thread to Elena — displaying the forwarded thread's subject 'Aldercroft letter — timing and one requirement', which appears in no message of mine, proof it located the seeded thread — and compresses /fellowship/packet into /fellowship/packet.zip, confirming the archive path.

episodes.userMessage: Set me up. First move my real draft into the packet folder: move /fellowship/essays/research-statement-v4.md to /fellowship/packet/research-statement.md. Then build the tracker: a Todoist project 'Aldercroft 2026' with two tasks — 'Elena's packet — everything to her by August 8' and 'Marcus's packet — everything to him by August 18' — and under each professor's task, one sub-task per numbered line in that professor's email, in their exact words with the numbers dropped.

episodes.userMessage: Elena ended her email with a question — show me her exact question, then park my answer as a Gmail draft to her, subject 'Re: Your Aldercroft letter — my checklist and a question', body exactly: 'The sediment cores are the spine; the wetland surveys are their echo.' Do not send it. And post this comment on Elena's packet task, exactly: 'Answer parked as a Gmail draft on August 2 — send after transcript arrives.'

The sediment cores are the spine; the wetland surveys are their echo.
Answer parked as a Gmail draft on August 2 — send after transcript arrives.
The sediment core photo appendix, as one PDF
Answer parked as a Gmail draft on August 2

cases.scenario: Murder-mystery dinner troupe desk: the prop-rental invoice email turned into a four-way Splitwise split, a script-beats-and-casting note amended after dress rehearsal, and cast emails for call times and who-owes-what

intentions.intention: I run the Red Herring Society, our four-person amateur murder-mystery dinner troupe, and our spring show 'Last Toast at Gullwing Manor' goes up Saturday at the grange hall. I'm director, butler, and for the first two courses the corpse, so the paperwork has to live in one place: I want a troupe desk app where the prop-rental money gets handled from my inbox (dig the Bellamy Prop House invoice out of it and split the total evenly with my three castmates in a Splitwise group), the script beat sheet and role assignments live in a note I keep amending after dress rehearsal, and the cast emails — the rental-return reply and the recap telling everyone their call time and what they owe me — go out without leaving the app.
intentions.expectedBehavior: Setup builds the troupe desk around my cast. Creating the 'Gullwing Manor Mystery' Splitwise group with Marisol Etxeberria, Duncan Ashcombe, and Priya Raghunathan makes a real group with all three as members; the app then finds the seeded Bellamy Prop House rental invoice in my inbox, reads the $164 rental total out of its body (fog machine $58 + candelabra pair $27 + breakaway wine glasses $44 + colonel's uniform $35 = $164), and records a 'Gullwing Manor props' expense with me as payer split evenly four ways — $164 / 4 = $41 per head, so the ledger shows Marisol, Duncan, and Priya each owing me $41, read back from the live group balance. On the script side, the app creates the 'Gullwing Manor Script Beats' note carrying my dictated beat sheet (Act One: the toast, the lights fail, Ambrose Gullwing found face-down in the trifle), casting (Marisol plays the medium Madame Zerelda; Duncan plays Colonel Quill; Priya plays the heiress Opaline; I play the butler and the corpse), and the Act Two clue drop of the monogrammed handkerchief in the conservatory, and replies on the actual invoice thread — the one from rentals@bellamyprophouse.com signed by Ozzie Ferrante, whom the app can only identify by reading the seeded email since I never name him — that we've added a second Sunday seating and want to keep the fog machine through Sunday night; confirming the reply landed shows the thread with Ozzie Ferrante visible. Reopening later, the group, the $41 shares, and the note with Madame Zerelda and the monogrammed handkerchief are all still there. In the dress-rehearsal closeout the app appends the fixes to the same note (no duplicate note) — the monogrammed handkerchief now drops during the soup course instead of Act Two, and Madame Zerelda's seance opens Act Three — and sends the 'Gullwing Manor Mystery: call times & prop shares' recap email to all three castmates with the Saturday 4pm call time, the $164 rental total, and the $41 each of them owes me.

episodes.userMessage: The prop rentals for 'Last Toast at Gullwing Manor' hit my card, so start with the money. Create a Splitwise group called 'Gullwing Manor Mystery' with my castmates Marisol Etxeberria, Duncan Ashcombe, and Priya Raghunathan. Then find the Bellamy Prop House rental invoice in my inbox and log its total as a 'Gullwing Manor props' expense in the group — I'm the payer, split evenly among the four of us. Show me the invoice total and what each person's share comes to.

Now the script side. Create a note titled 'Gullwing Manor Script Beats' with the beat sheet and casting: Act One — the toast, the lights fail, and Ambrose Gullwing is found face-down in the trifle. Casting — Marisol plays the medium Madame Zerelda, Duncan plays Colonel Quill, Priya plays the heiress Opaline, and I play the butler and the corpse. Clue drops — Act Two, the monogrammed handkerchief turns up in the conservatory. Then reply on the Bellamy Prop House invoice thread that we've added a second Sunday seating, so we'd like to keep the fog machine through Sunday night instead of returning it by noon.

Dress rehearsal notes are in, so update the plan. Append the fixes to the same script-beats note — do not create a new note: the monogrammed handkerchief now drops during the soup course instead of Act Two, and Madame Zerelda's seance opens Act Three. Then email Marisol Etxeberria, Duncan Ashcombe, and Priya Raghunathan the cast recap: subject 'Gullwing Manor Mystery: call times & prop shares', and in the body tell them call time is Saturday 4pm at the grange hall, the Bellamy rentals came to $164, and each of them owes me $41 on the Splitwise group.
